PAGE 1
       The Cohomology of Agent Evidence
        Typed Cellular Sheaves, Relative Extension, and Fault Observability

                       Erich Owens   erich@curiositech.ai
                                  Curiositech AI Research

                               September 2026



                                     Abstract

      A multi-agent workflow leaves local evidence on agents, handoffs, and joint review con-
       tracts. We model those observations as a typed cellular sheaf on a two-dimensional complex,
      with explicit vertex-to-edge and edge-to-face maps. The resulting degree-one cochains have
     two distinct algebraic obstructions: a violated face relation and a closed but nonexact class
       in H1. A relative connecting class tests whether a partially visible section can extend
      through unobserved contracts. We compute all three channels exactly on a heterogeneous
       four-role complex, including a face attachment that destroys H1 without changing total edge-
      compatibility detection. A sheaf edge-group distance characterizes when sparse erroneous
     handoffreports can be detected or uniquely recovered; a restricted projection gain quantifies
       stability. The graph-cycle case supplies a sharp baseline: when both endpoint claims are
       visible, direct equality catches every cycle inconsistency. These results specify what an audit
     can prove from selected evidence and what remains invisible, including coherent falsehood
     and copied observations. The prospective application is a provenance-bound audit of real
      agent workflows against independent ledger truth and equal-information contract checks;
       field utility and semantic fault attribution require that experiment.


1 Question and contribution

Agent workflows distribute evidence across roles: an author records work, a reviewer sees a
subset, a CI job observes a commit and test run, and a publisher sees an approval or artifact
receipt. A global claim can fail even when each observed overlap appears locally coherent.
The question is which incompatibilities can be inferred from the evidence an auditor actually
receives.
    Cellular sheaves give a precise language for this question. A stalk records one typed feature at
a cell; restriction maps state which part of a role’s state can be compared on a handoff or joint
contract. Cohomology distinguishes a local face-relation violation from a globally nontrivial
closed obstruction, while relative cohomology tests extension through a visibility boundary.
These constructions are established mathematics [2, 1, 6]. The contribution here is a concrete
agent-evidence contract, exact failure-observability criteria, and an executable comparison with
simpler checks. We make no claim that a topological signature alone establishes which agent
erred.
   The numerical examples use exact count features, one work item, and one immutable event-
log watermark. A production observation must bind each packet to its schema, work item,
source identity, log root, and evidence reference. An artifact digest or approval cannot be
treated as a real coordinate merely to make a Laplacian run. We keep the external truth oracle
separate from algebraic compatibility and use a synthetic fixture to expose the information
boundary before collecting field traces.





                                         1

PAGE 2
2 A typed cellular sheaf of work evidence

A multi-agent audit has several kinds of overlap: two roles can compare an exact count on one
handoff, while a three-role contract can require those comparisons to compose. A graph with
one scalar at each vertex cannot express which feature each overlap exposes. We therefore fix a
finite oriented two-dimensional simplicial complex K and a cellular sheaf F of finite-dimensional
real vector spaces. A vertex, edge, or face σ has a stalk F(σ); for each incidence σ ⊆τ, a linear
map ρστ : F(σ) →F(τ) states exactly which feature is shared. Maps along the two routes from
a vertex to a face must agree. The linear structure is used only for quantities with declared
additive units. Artifact hashes and approval identities instead require symbolic equality or a
separate constraint system.
Definition 1 (Typed evidence cochain complex). Put Cj(K; F) = ⨁︁ dim σ=j F(σ). With fixed
orientations, the coboundaries A = δ0 : C0 →C1 and B = δ1 : C1 →C2 are the signed sums of
the declared incidence maps. For an oriented edge e = (u, v),

                                (Ax)e = ρvexv −ρuexu.

For an oriented face t = (u, v, w),

                         (By)t = ρvw,tyvw −ρuw,tyuw + ρuv,tyuv.

The incidence maps are admitted only if BA = 0 exactly. An edge cochain y is an independently
collected set of same-schema overlap reports, not a difference computed from one already assem-
bled vertex assignment. All packet provenance, feature versions, and observation watermarks
are checked before forming y.
   The word independently  is an acquisition condition, not an assumption of statistical in-
dependence. Two packets copied from one unverified source can have distinct identifiers and
still supply one piece of evidence. A face is included only when its three-party contract and
incidence maps are declared in advance. Merely drawing a filled triangle does not create a new
measurement.
Lemma 1 (Sheaf cochain identity). Composition-compatible restriction maps imply BA = 0.

Proof. On each oriented face (u, v, w), substitute the three edge components of Ax into the
formula for B. The two contributions from each vertex cancel because the restrictions from that
vertex to the face agree along both incident edges. This is the typed version of the simplicial
boundary-of-a-boundary identity.

   Choose and publish inner products on every stalk before inspecting observations. They set
units and weights; changing them changes energy magnitudes. Let
                   H1 = ker A∗∩ker B,   Q = I −AA+.

The following decomposition is standard cellular-sheaf Hodge theory [2, 1]; its audit interpre-
tation depends on the evidence contract.
Theorem 1 (Typed local and global obstruction channels). Every y ∈C1(K; F) has a unique
orthogonal decomposition
                   y = Ax + B∗z + h,    h ∈H1,   Qy = B∗z + h.

The three summands are unique. Their parameters need not be: x is defined modulo H0(K; F) =
ker A, and z modulo ker B∗. The face channel satisfies By = BB∗z; it vanishes precisely when
the coexact component B∗z vanishes. If By = 0 and h ̸= 0, the observed cochain is locally closed
but has a nonzero class in H1(K; F) = ker B/ im A. The total completion residual obeys
                        min ∥y −Ax∥2 = ∥B∗z∥2 + ∥h∥2.
                                x

Neither channel identifies a cause or validates the truth of a compatible assignment.


                                         2

PAGE 3
Proof. The identity BA = 0 makes im A orthogonal to im B∗. The orthogonal complement of
their sum is ker A∗∩ker B = H1. Orthogonal projection therefore gives the decomposition and
the residual identity. On im B∗, B is injective:  if BB∗z = 0, then ∥B∗z∥2 = ⟨z, BB∗z⟩= 0.
Thus By = 0 precisely when the coexact term vanishes. A closed cochain is exact precisely when
its harmonic term vanishes; quotienting closed cochains by exact ones identifies the harmonic
subspace with H1.

  A nonzero By is a violation of a selected face relation. A nonzero h is a closed, nonexact
obstruction in the declared sheaf complex; nontrivial sheaf cohomology need not imply a hole in
the underlying simplicial space. Their energy ratio is not a universal classifier of “local mistake”
versus “network partition”: topology, feature maps, and inner products are model choices. A
gradient-shaped jointly false account lies in im A and makes both channels zero.


2.1 An exact heterogeneous two-complex

Consider four roles 0, 1, 2, 3, each with a two-coordinate vertex stalk (c, h): an accepted com-
pletion count c and a validated handoff count h for one work item and watermark. These are
two separately typed integer features; the real cochain calculation is an exact rational audit
of their differences. The oriented edges are (01), (12), (02), (23), (03). Edges 01 and 12 expose
only c; edges 23 and 03 expose only h; edge 02 exposes both. Thus the edge stalk dimensions
are (1, 1, 2, 1, 1), and the vertex-to-edge maps are coordinate projections except for the identity
map on 02. The one filled face 012 compares only c: its edge-to-face maps are the identity on
01, 12 and the c projection on 02. The loop 0230 has no face contract.

                                          01 : c
                             0                              1
                                                                       filled 012
                                                   count face

                                   02 :  (c, h)
                       03 : h                                 12 : c

                                             unfilled 023
                                   handoff loop

                             3                              2
                                          23 : h


Figure 1: A heterogeneous two-complex with five physical edges and six typed edge coordinates.
The 012 face compares completion counts; no face relation is declared for the 023 handoffcycle.

   Order edge coordinates as (01c, 12c, 02c, 02h, 23h, 03h). Direct substitution gives

           Ax = (c1 −c0, c2 −c1, c2 −c0, h2 −h0, h3 −h2, h3 −h0),               (1)
            By = y01c + y12c −y02c.                                                    (2)

The maps obey BA = 0. Exact row reduction gives rank A = 4 and rank B = 1, hence

                                                       (︁ dim H0, dim H1, dim H2)︁ = (4, 1, 0).

The unused count at vertex 3 and unused handoffat vertex 1 account for two of the four global-
section degrees of freedom. The remaining two are common count and common handoff values.
With unit weights in this synthetic fixture, set

                   a = (1, 1, −1, 0, 0, 0)T ,     b = (0, 0, 0, 1, 1, −1)T .

Then a ⊥b, ∥a∥2 = ∥b∥2 = 3, and exact projectors are

                     Pface = aaT /3,    PH1 = bbT /3,   Q = (aaT + bbT )/3.                (3)


                                         3

PAGE 4
The three controlled inputs y = a, y = b, and y = Ax have different observability signatures:
(By, ∥Pfacey∥2, ∥PH1y∥2) is (3, 3, 0) for a count-face violation, (0, 0, 3) for a closed handoff-loop
obstruction, and (0, 0, 0) for every gradient. These are labels for injected cochain patterns, not
labels for a dishonest role. A mixture a + b has both components. The exact code computes
these values without a floating-point threshold.
   Add a second declared face 023 that compares h, with the h projection from edge 02 and
identity maps from 23, 03. Its new B has rows aT and bT . The handoff class becomes coexact
and dim H1 falls from one to zero. The same edge reports and A still give the same Q in Eq. 3.
This distinction is general.

Theorem 2 (Face attachment and information boundary). For fixed vertex and edge stalks,
fixed A, and the same observed edge cochain y, changing or adding compatible face stalks and
edge-to-face maps can change B, H1, and the division of Qy into face and harmonic parts.
It cannot change Qy, minx ∥y −Ax∥, or which edge cochains admit a vertex completion. An
independently acquired face receipt is additional evidence only when it supplies an observation
beyond the edge cochain; a fair direct-contract baseline must receive that receipt too.

Proof. The projector Q = I −AA+ and the membership test y ∈im A depend only on A and y.
The Hodge split inside im A⊥depends on B through im B∗and ker B. In the fixture, the two
orthogonal rows aT , bT explicitly move b from the harmonic space to the coexact space without
changing Q.


2.2 Fault distance with typed edge stalks

The graph minimum-cut threshold is a special case of a sheaf-coded observation limit. Count
the support of an edge cochain by edge groups, not by scalar coordinates: a change in either
coordinate of edge 02 affects one edge packet. Define

                           dF =                               min ⃓⃓{e : (Ax)e ̸= 0}⃓⃓,                                           Ax̸=0

with dF = ∞if A = 0. This is the minimum group support of a nonzero compatible edge report.
It is computable in a small complex by checking ranks after deleting subsets of edge-stalk blocks.
Let ΣEk be the set of cochains supported on at most k edge groups.

Theorem 3 (Typed sheaf report-error distance). For an integer k ≥1 and y = Ax + e with
arbitrary-amplitude e ∈ΣEk , every nonzero k-edge error is detectable from Qy  if and only if
dF > k. Every e ∈ΣEk  is uniquely determined by y modulo the compatible component Ax if and
only if dF > 2k. Vertex assignments remain identifiable only modulo H0 = ker A.  If dF > 2k
and
                       α2k =       min           inf ∥QT v∥> 0,
                               ∅̸=T⊆E, |T|≤min(2k,|E|) ∥v∥=1

where QT contains every coordinate column in the selected edge-stalk blocks and v ranges over
those coordinates, a k-edge fit with projected residual at most ϵ under projected noise at most ϵ
has edge-error estimation error at most 2ϵ/α2k.

Proof. The kernel of Q is im A. Thus a nonzero error supported on at most k groups is invisible
exactly when such a cochain lies in im A, proving the detection criterion. If two k-group errors
explain the same y, their difference is a compatible cochain supported on at most 2k groups.
Conversely, partition the support of any nonzero compatible cochain with at most 2k groups
into two sets of size at most k to construct two explanations. Finitely many group selections
make α2k positive exactly when no selected column space intersects ker Q; this is the same
distance condition. The final bound follows by applying ∥Qh∥≥α2k∥h∥to the difference h
between the two k-group errors and using the triangle inequality on their residuals.


                                         4

PAGE 5
   The fixture has dF = 2: each channel occupies a three-edge loop, and a nonconstant state
on one of its connected triples changes at least two edge groups.  Changing only c1 attains
two. Therefore every single-edge error is detectable, but arbitrary single-edge correction is not
guaranteed. For example, (1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) is an error on 01, or the compatible report from c1 = 1                                                √
plus a unit error on 12. The smallest normalized projection gain for a one-edge fault is 1/  3
in the declared unit metric. The support theorem is a sheaf-code design criterion; it neither
names an agentic cause nor makes a copied packet independent.


2.3 Partial observations and relative obstruction

An auditor may see only a subcomplex L ⊆K. The relative cochain complex C•(K, L; F)
consists of cochains that vanish on L. Standard relative sheaf cohomology supplies the exact
sequence [2]
              H0(K; F) −→H0(L; F|L) ∂−→H1(K, L; F) −→H1(K; F).

The connecting map is a coverage certificate for a visible compatible section; it does not ap-
ply to arbitrary inconsistent edge observations without formulating a separate affine extension
problem.

Theorem 4 (Relative extension criterion). Let s ∈H0(L; F|L) be a section on the visible
subcomplex.  It extends to a global section on K  if and only  if ∂s = 0.  Vanishing proves
existence of a model-compatible extension, not uniqueness or agreement with unseen evidence.

Proof. Lift s to any vertex cochain  ˜︁s on K.  Its coboundary vanishes on L, so it is a relative
1-cocycle and ∂s = [A˜︁s]. A different lift changes this class by a relative coboundary. If s has a
global-section lift, the class is zero. Conversely, if the class is zero, a relative vertex cochain z
satisfies A˜︁s = Az; then  ˜︁s −z is a global section and still restricts to s.
   In the fixture, let L contain vertices 0, 1, 2 and only count edges 01, 12.  Counts c0 =
c1 = c2 = 0 and handoffs h0 = 0, h2 = 1 form a valid visible section because those edges
expose only counts.  Extending it with zero at vertex 3 produces the relative edge cochain
(02c, 02h, 23h, 03h) = (0, 1, −1, 0). No adjustment at hidden vertex 3 can remove its 02h = 1
component, so ∂s ̸= 0. Exact ranks give dim H0(L) = 4, dim im(H0(K) →H0(L)) = 3, and
dim H1(K, L) = 2. One relative dimension records this extension failure; the other maps to the
ordinary handoff-loop class. A zero relative class would allow an extension while leaving actual
unseen packets and event truth unresolved.


3 Graph specialization: one exact feature

Let G = (V, E) be a finite oriented multigraph. Every edge e = (u, v) represents one indepen-
dently collected report packet. Let f name one exact feature schema and w one immutable
event-log watermark. The packet carries endpoint claims ae,u and ae,v in Z, a work-item iden-
tifier, a packet identifier, and a reference to the underlying evidence.  It also carries its fea-
ture/schema version, watermark, and event-log root. Orientation is canonical and fixed before
observations are read. The reported difference is

                                         ye = ae,v −ae,u.                                     (4)

A precheck rejects a missing packet, duplicate packet identifier, mixed feature or schema, in-
consistent watermark, or inconsistent log root. These are input validity failures, not topological
alarms. A packet identifier or hash alone is not proof that an agent, workflow, or ledger produced
a claim. The offline benchmark tests metadata equality and does not verify signatures.




                                         5

PAGE 6
Definition 2 (Compatible edge differences). A complete, metadata-valid observation y ∈ZE is
compatible when there is an x ∈ZV such that ye = xv −xu for every oriented edge e = (u, v).
Compatibility asserts the existence of one node value per agent for this feature and watermark.
It does not assert that x equals the event ledger or that any event really happened.
   Write B ∈{−1, 0, 1}E×V  for the oriented incidence matrix, so compatibility is y ∈im B.
Over real numbers, the least-squares completion residual is

                          r(y) = min ∥y −Bx∥2 = ∥(I −BB+)y∥2.                        (5)
                               x∈RV

Here B+ is the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse. The exact decision r = 0 needs no floating-point
solver for integer packets. It is available from a spanning forest. Computing either the projection
or that forest check requires collecting the selected edge reports somewhere; no decentralized
implementation or communication advantage is established by this paper.

Theorem 5 (Exact cycle test). For a complete integer observation on G, the following are
equivalent: (i) the reports are compatible; (ii) the oriented sum of y around every graph cycle
is zero; (iii) a spanning-forest propagation assigns integer potentials to vertices and every re-
maining edge agrees with its endpoint difference; and (iv) r(y) = 0. The dimension of the real
cycle space is |E| −|V | + c, where c is the number of connected components, including isolated
vertices.

Proof. If y = Bx, each cycle sum telescopes to zero. Choose one root per component, set its
potential to zero, and propagate along a spanning tree by adding or subtracting each oriented
edge value.  Every vertex receives an integer value. A non-tree edge closes a fundamental
cycle, so its agreement with the propagated difference is equivalent to that cycle sum being
zero. Fundamental cycles span the cycle space, proving the reverse implication. Orthogonal
decomposition gives RE = im B ⊕ker BT and hence the equivalence with r = 0.  Finally
rank B = |V | −c and rank-nullity yields dim ker BT = |E| −|V | + c.

     If each observed edge difference is constructed from a single already assembled node vector x,
then y = Bx by construction and the completion residual is identically zero. The graph Dirichlet
energy ∑︁e ∥xu−xv∥2 may be positive for honest unequal counts; it is not the completion residual
in Eq. 5. Independent edge evidence is necessary for a nontrivial test.


4 What the algebra cannot identify

Theorem 6 (Information limits of compatibility). Under the model above: (a) on a forest, every
edge-difference vector is compatible; (b) adding any gradient Bz to a compatible observation
preserves compatibility, regardless of whether z is true; and (c) a jointly false but internally
consistent report passes the cycle test. A positive residual certifies incompatibility of the selected
reports, but alone identifies neither a dishonest party nor a physical network partition.

Proof. A forest has |E| = |V | −c, so Theorem 5 gives a zero-dimensional cycle space and
im B = RE.  If y = Bx, then y + Bz = B(x + z). In particular, x + z may disagree with an
independent event ledger while the residual remains zero. The same construction proves (c).
Permuting which packet is declared erroneous can produce the same nonzero cycle sum; the
algebra therefore supplies no unique source attribution.

  A three-edge triangle with values (1, 1, 1) around its orientation is incompatible because the
cycle sum is 3. A one-edge report with value 100 is always compatible: assign its endpoints
potentials 0 and 100. A triangle with values derived from false node values (10, 10, 10) is also
compatible. These examples distinguish a contradiction among reports from a contradiction
with the external event record.


                                         6

PAGE 7
   The decomposition in Theorem 1 separates chosen face relations from classes in the chosen
H1.  It does not turn those algebraic channels into causal diagnoses. Adding a face without
an independent observation changes the channel assignment but leaves completion detection
fixed by Theorem 2. Fencing an edge changes which claims are tested; it does not repair the
underlying work or prove the fenced agent was at fault.


5 The simpler baseline

When packets expose both endpoint claims, the auditor can compare repeated reports made
about the same node. Define D = 1 if some node has two incident packets giving it different
values at the same feature, work item, watermark, and log root. This check uses equality and
a map keyed by node; it needs no graph solver.

Theorem 7 (Duplicate-claim dominance for visible endpoints). On complete metadata-valid
packets as defined in Section 3,  if D = 0 then r(y) = 0.  Consequently, every positive cycle
residual is also detected by the duplicate-claim baseline. The converse need not hold: a duplicate
claim can be inconsistent even when the edge differences form a gradient.

Proof. If D = 0, choose xv to be the common endpoint claim for each non-isolated vertex v,
and choose any integer value for each isolated vertex. Then Eq. 4 gives ye = xv −xu on every
edge, so Theorem 5 yields r = 0. For the converse, take a triangle whose every reported edge
difference is zero.  Set endpoint claims to (0, 0) on two edges and (1, 1) on the third. The
differences are all zero, while at least one repeated node claim differs.

   This dominance result is a practical cut condition. With visible endpoint claims, topology
cannot improve detection recall over the equality baseline under the same metadata and packet
set.  It may still help explain a pattern when raw endpoint claims are unavailable, when only
edge differences can be disclosed, or when independent redundant paths have special provenance.
Those are distinct privacy and acquisition contracts requiring their own tests. We claim no cost
or utility advantage for the current setting.


6  Failure-separating feature maps and degeneracy

A choice of stalks is an engineering hypothesis about what the evidence preserves. A useful
feature map must be typed, versioned, and checked against the failure modes it is meant to
identify. Let tv,e be the evidence visible at endpoint v on edge e, and let φv,e(tv,e) take values
in a declared stalk F(v). The restriction map Rv,e : F(v) →F(e) must land in a common edge
feature space. When subtraction is meaningful, one can form an edge report

                               ye = Rv,eφv,e(tv,e) −Ru,eφu,e(tu,e).

The use of tv,e rather than a single shared tv is deliberate: applying one vertex map once and
taking all its edge differences produces y = Bx and forces the cycle residual to zero. Each
edge packet must have an independently accountable evidence path. For a count, the maps
can return exact integers. For an approval, artifact digest, or event sequence, use a suitable
typed or symbolic constraint; mapping its bits to an arbitrary real coordinate does not create
a meaningful distance.
   Fix one context: work item, feature schema, watermark, graph, admissible evidence, and
a reference trace t0.  Predeclare a finite set M = {0, 1, . . . , k} of fault interventions, with 0
denoting no injected fault. An intervention Ij changes specified edge evidence and produces a
deterministic edge signature sj = Φ(Ij(t0))−Φ(t0), with s0 = 0. These are signatures of specified




                                         7

PAGE 8
interventions, not generic labels such as “hallucination” or “partition.” Let Q = I −BB+ be
the graph-cycle projector and zj = Qsj. The failure-separation margin is

                  γ = min ∥zi −zj∥2,   D = {︁ {i, j} : i ̸= j, zi = zj }︁ .                  (6)
                                      i̸=j

Theorem 9 (Three-edge-connectivity criterion). For a connected loopless graph with at least
two vertices, all labels in the signed single-edge library have distinct cycle projections if and
only if the graph is three-edge-connected, meaning removal of any one or two edges leaves it
connected. A bridge makes its own error invisible; a non-bridge two-edge cut makes two signed
edge-error labels indistinguishable. This criterion assumes exact edge-only differences and known
unit amplitude.

Proof. Write qi = Qei.  If qi = 0, then ei = Bx for some potential x. On every edge other
than i the potential difference is zero.  If deleting i leaves the graph connected, x is constant
and Bx = 0, a contradiction.  If i is a bridge, assigning potentials zero and one to the two
components after its deletion gives Bx = ±ei and thus qi = 0.
   For distinct non-bridge edges i, j, an equality qi = ±qj means ei ∓ej = Bx. All potential
differences vanish outside {i, j}; if deleting both edges leaves a connected graph, x is constant,
again a contradiction.  Conversely,  if deleting i and j disconnects the graph while neither is
individually a bridge, the remaining graph has two components linked by those two edges.
Assigning potentials zero and one to the components gives Bx = ±ei ± ej, so one signed label
on i shares a cycle projection with one signed label on j. The nominal label is distinct from every
edge label exactly when there are no bridges. Combining these cases proves the criterion.

8 Operational application and scope

A field audit should start from one immutable work item, PR head, workflow attempt, artifact
identity, and ledger watermark. The additive coordinates in the typed fixture can count accepted
completions and validated handoffs. Reviewer approvals, commit digests, and publisher grants
remain exact symbolic predicates checked against authenticated event records. Each edge packet
must say which role acquired it, from which independent source, and through which map its
value enters the stalk. A three-party face contract needs its own provenance-bound receipt if
it is to add evidence; the algebraic face relation alone only changes the interpretation of an
existing edge residual.

provenance checks, repeated-claim equality, an exact typed-constraint solver, and the sheaf

9 Related work and novelty boundary

Cellular sheaves, their cohomology, relative exact sequences, and Hodge Laplacians are estab-
lished [1, 2].  Combinatorial Hodge ranking already separates gradient, curl, and harmonic
components of pairwise data [6]. Sheaf cosystolic expansion supplies local-to-global and testing
criteria under strong complex and sheaf hypotheses [3]; it does not make a nontrivial H1 class
visible to a face-only test. Relative spectral diagnostics with a separate grounding morphism
provide another relevant construction [4]. Sparse recovery and coding-distance arguments also
predate the edge-group support theorem [5]. Discourse sheaves model selective communication
and lying [7], while cellular-sheaf coordination has been studied for heterogeneous multi-agent
systems [8, 9].
   The mathematical statements in this paper specialize that literature to a declared agent-
evidence contract. The potentially distinctive contribution is a testable design method: specify
typed and provenance-bound restrictions, compute local, global, and relative obstruction classes,
state exactly which injected report errors the map can distinguish, and compare against an
equal-information direct solver. The heterogeneous fixture demonstrates the method and its
limits; it is not evidence of broad field utility. A useful next result would show that independently
sourced edge and face receipts reveal a real workflow failure more cheaply or more clearly than
direct authenticated contract checks, under a predeclared acquisition and privacy budget.


10 Conclusion

Typed cellular sheaves can express information that a scalar graph cannot: different overlaps
reveal different coordinates, joint contracts impose face relations, and incomplete visibility cre-
ates an extension problem. In the exact fixture, a count-face violation and a closed handoff-loop
obstruction occupy orthogonal cohomological channels; the relative class identifies a visible sec-
tion that cannot extend. The sheaf edge-group distance states when sparse erroneous reports
are detectable or uniquely recoverable. These are precise statements about a selected evidence
complex. The same calculations show why topology alone cannot establish truth: coherent
false reports remain invisible, a face without new evidence cannot increase detection, and a
direct solver with the same packets has the same compatibility information. The field ques-
tion is whether a provenance-bound sheaf audit improves the cost or clarity of checking real
multi-agent work. The protocol here makes that question falsifiable.

1.1 A1. The Split-Digest Theorem (comonotonicity characterization)

Lift: 1–2 days; the proof is short, the care is in the definitions.


Formalization.  Define a read-surface as a triple (X, Σ, π): substrate items X, per-item
evidence Σ, and a projection π producing a bounded rendering. A reader r is a loss func-
tion Lr(rendered set, true states); a scalar head h : X →R serves r if rank-ordering by h
realizes r’s optimal rendering at every budget. Two concrete readers: the successor (loss =
task-continuation value forgone; fit-shaped) and the operator (loss = regret-if-ignored; risk-
shaped). The theorem: a single head serves both readers iff their induced preference orders
are comonotone on the item domain — i.e., agree on every pair. The negative direction is
witnessed by two constructible items: a routine-but-essential working state (high continu-
ation value, negligible regret — the successor must reload it; the operator need never see
it) and an anomalously abandoned dead end with irreversible side effects (zero continuation
value — the successor should not reload it — maximal regret). Non-comonotone; hence no
shared head; hence Thm. I.7.1 is a special case of a general principle over every read-surface:
digests, checkpoints, resurrection handoffs, briefings.


Proof path.  The order-reversal argument is your Thm. I.7.1’s, generalized: strict mono-
tone transforms preserve pairwise order, so a shared head forces comonotonicity; conversely,
comonotone orders admit a common refinement, which any strictly increasing reparameteri-
zation serves — giving the iff, which the original theorem lacks. The quantitative addendum
is where new content lives: apply Thm. I.6.1 per reader. Each reader has its own critical
set Sr; a joint zero-miss digest must satisfy the floor for Sop ∪Ssucc, and when the sets are
nearly disjoint the joint floor approaches the sum of the individual floors — a single stored
compaction pays both bills at once or silently defaults on one. Corollary: compaction must
be computed per reader from durable artifacts; storing only one compaction is irreversible
information loss for the other reader, which is exactly the “never compact from the previous
summary” rule, now with a reason.


What it gives. A one-page theorem that converts an architectural opinion (the SLM
sidecar; two digest pipelines) into a mathematical necessity, upgrades Thm. I.7.1 from an
example to a characterization, and quantifies the cost of ignoring it via additive bit floors.
Lands in Chapter I as §I.8.2’s missing second half.

nature; they are born under a common power. The consent that matters is the operator’s
consent to be constrained by their own daemon: footgun guards that stop you, completion
gates that refuse your wishful green. That is Ulysses at the mast — Elster’s precommit-
ment devices — not Leviathan. Hobbes sells the pitch; Elster describes the mechanism.
The inalienable operator-override then becomes philosophically live rather than obvious: a
precommitment device with an escape hatch is barely a precommitment, and the tension
between revocable consent and binding oneself deserves a section.


3. At n=1 the economy is control theory in a costume — with a missing geneal-
ogy. A bond denominated in a currency you mint, forfeited to yourself, conserves trivially;
economic content appears only at federation. The honest defense of internal prices is that
they are decentralized optimization signals, and that defense has a distinguished lineage:
Sutherland’s “A Futures Market in Computer Time” (CACM 1968) and, above all, Miller
& Drexler’s agoric open systems papers (1988) — capabilities plus markets for computation
is their program, and Port Daddy is its direct descendant. Simon (1971) coined “a wealth
of information creates a poverty of attention”; read-poverty is nearly his phrase and he be-
longs beside Miller and Scott. The bibliography, ironically for a single-writer volume, has
many writers: Macaroons appears four times, Hobbes three, Demers three, Ostrom three.
Deduplicate.


4. The digest is an attack surface.  Stigmergic markers, bus messages, and digests
are attacker-controlled inputs read into other agents’ contexts and into the operator’s eyes.
Prompt injection through the coordination layer — digest poisoning — belongs in Chapter
II’s threat model as a named section, not in a starred exercise. The instinct in §I.3.2 (“the
zoom target must be verifiable, not self-reported”) is the right seed; grow it into provenance
labels and taint discipline on every read-surface. (Part 5 builds the full apparatus.)


1.4 What the volume is almost arriving at

1. The split-digest corollary. Theorem I.7.1 proves two readers with incompatible loss
   functions cannot share one scoring head; “the digest IS the compaction” then quietly
   assumes compaction has one reader. It has two: the successor agent (task continuation)
   and the operator (oversight). By the theorem’s own construction, no single compaction
   serves both. Corollary: every read-surface projection needs per-reader heads over shared
   substrate — digests, checkpoints, resurrection handoffs. Compact from durable artifacts,
   per reader class. One-page proof, real design change.

2. Digest-with-zoom is two-stage group testing. Theorem I.6.1 is a covering bound
   on the non-adaptive stage; zoom is adaptive, and the group-testing literature (Dorfman
   onward; Du & Hwang) quantifies what adaptivity buys over the k log2(N/k) floor. There
    is a provable Pareto frontier trading digest bits against expected zoom-opens.  Better:
  Thm. I.6.1 is falsifiable — zero-miss digests below the bit floor must miss. Plot empirical

5. Attenuation is scope of employment. The economically relevant continuity is liabil-
    ity continuity — a legal concept, not a metaphysical one. The law of agency maps exactly:
   respondeat superior (the principal answers for the agent’s torts within scope of employ-
   ment); scope of employment ≈capability attenuation; the bond is vicarious-liability
   insurance. This gives Chapter III a second spine sturdier than the personal-identity one,
   with centuries of boundary case law attached.


1.5 Genealogy and citation gaps

Miller & Drexler (agoric open systems, 1988); Sutherland (1968); Simon (1971); Elster
(Ulysses and the Sirens, 1979); Becker (1968); inspection games (Avenhaus–von Stengel–
Zamir); Kamenica–Gentzkow (Bayesian persuasion, for reputation disclosure); group testing
(Dorfman 1943; Du & Hwang); and — substantively — CONIKS (Melara et al., USENIX
Security 2015) and its descendants (Key Transparency; WhatsApp’s auditable key direc-
tories): transparency logs specifically for identity-key binding across mutually distrusting
domains, which is much closer to the federated witness log than Certificate Transparency
is, and is the nearest existing relative of the cross-operator-attestation gap. Evaluating it is
cheaper than inventing.


1.6 What is less interesting

The Myerson–Satterthwaite corner is correctly scoped but least binding:  real platforms
escape MS via fees and subsidies, and the shared grading oracle makes values common-ish,
putting the setting in Akerlof/lemons territory where the live theory is information design.
The sheaf gesture, as it stands,  is ornament:  either build the small gluing model for a
bounded gossip topology (the volume’s own E3⋆; Solution 26 sketches it) or cut it. Gap #1
(multi-dimensional reputation aggregation) may dissolve by the volume’s own philosophy:
refuse to aggregate; expose the vector; buyers gate on per-axis predicates — which “score as
telemetry, gate on predicates” already licenses.

2.1 Chapter I, §I.6 (read-poverty and the lower bound)

Solution 1 (6.1). Read-poverty binds because the write side already has mature primitives
— claims backed by database uniqueness constraints, locks, merge queues, anomaly detection
— so double-writes are structurally handled, while the read side (find the right agent, the
relevant work, the trustworthy collaborator) has no primitive at all: legible state accumulates
faster than it can be consulted, and participants regress to O(n) eyeball search or act blind.

Solution 2 (6.2). Write-time cost:  every registration, claim, note, and episode update
must also maintain the directory structure (index maintenance on insert). Read-time speed
purchased:  queries of the form “who/what matches q” answer in O(query) — an index
lookup — instead of scanning O(n) participants, exactly the table-scan-to-index trade.

Solution 3 (6.3). At n=1: the session briefing (state recovery after absence), the honest-
attestation/completion gate (verified-green vs. no-evidence-of-bad), and the footgun guard
(irreversible-action interception). None is discovery-ranking because discovery answers “who
among many”: with a single agent there is no candidate set, so a ranker is vacuous while the
three surfaces above already have a customer.

Solution 4 (6.4). The floor is log2 (︁Nk )︁ −log2 (︁mk )︁ . As k →0 both terms vanish: a swarm in
which almost nothing is critical is digestible in a few bits (“nothing to see, here’s why”). As
k →N/2, (︁N )︁ peaks at ≈2N/√︁πN/2, so for any fixed review budget m ≪N the floor grows             k
to Θ(N) bits — essentially one bit per artifact; the digest must enumerate. Hence a mostly-
safe swarm is cheap to digest and a mostly-dangerous one cannot be summarized at all: past
a critical density, “summarize” degenerates to “list,” which is the formal justification for
keeping the dangerous set small by construction (attenuation, footgun guards) rather than
hoping to digest it.

Solution 5 (6.5⋆, adversarial critical estimation). The bound survives trivially against an
oblivious adversary (it is a lower bound). Against an adaptive adversary the right model is:
the digest is computed from observable features ϕ(a) of each artifact, and the adversary per-
turbs ϕ within a budget. A zero-miss digest must then treat all ϕ-indistinguishable artifacts
alike, so the effective bound becomes log2 (︁Nk′ )︁ with k′ the size of the indistinguishability class
containing the true critical set — the adversary attacks in two directions: inflation (make
everything appear critical, driving the floor toward Θ(N): a legibility denial-of-service that
forces the operator to open everything) and mimicry (make critical artifacts appear inert,
making zero-miss unattainable from corrupted features at any digest size). The defense is
the volume’s own §I.3.2 made quantitative:  build the digest only from signals the agent
cannot forge (witnessed outcomes, oracle-bound checks, structural facts the kernel records),
and treat forgeable features as advisory. The residue is an inspection game: sample-audit
inert-labeled artifacts at rate ρ with penalty B such that ρdB exceeds the gain from a suc-
cessful mimicry — the same Becker condition as Conj. III.11.1, which suggests one unified
deterrence budget across mimicry, escalation-spoofing, and dishonest grading.


2.2 Chapter I, §I.7 (discovery and the split ranker)

Solution 6 (7.1). No strictly monotone scalar transform can identify the discovery head with
the attention head, because high-fit/low-risk and low-fit/high-risk items order oppositely
under them.  Discovery maximizes capability fit (Eq. I.2); the attention queue maximizes
regret-if-ignored = stakes × irreversibility × anomaly (Eq. I.3).

Solution 7 (7.2). The attention queue’s inputs (anomaly, distress) are self-influenceable
by the scored party, its payoff (operator attention) is a scarce prize agents compete for,
and its miss-cost asymmetry forces it to err toward surfacing — so manufactured distress
is subsidized. The discovery head is anchored in pull signals (what the agent demonstrably
did), which are costly to forge, and its prize is self-punishing: winning a routing you cannot
serve produces a witnessed failure.

Solution 8 (7.3). Without Prop. I.7.1: agent A dies holding a claim on f; the row persists
as “current”; every claim attempt by live agent B is rejected by the uniqueness constraint
indefinitely; unblocking requires manual garbage collection. With  it: the claim is a lease
with a class-specific half-life; the read-projection weights it by e−λt and the write boundary
treats an expired lease as vacant. B unblocks at its first claim attempt after the lease lapses
— the stale row decayed out of “current” instead of persisting as misleading truth.

Solution 9 (7.4). Escalation e fires; the queue surfaces it; the operator dismisses. The dae-
mon debits the agent’s escalation standing by δ; subsequent escalations from that identity
carry a discounted prior and need a higher regret score to surface. Genuine distress survives
because (i) the debit prices dismissed escalations, not escalations per se — validated ones
(operator acts) restore standing; and (ii) the regret head still multiplies stakes and irre-
versibility, so a true high-stakes anomaly clears even a raised threshold.  It is a reputation
loop on the alarm channel: crying wolf has negative expected value unless the wolf is usually
real.

Solution 10 (7.5⋆, implicit relevance feedback). Accept/reject is click data; pairwise pref-
erences (accepted ≻rejected) can train the weights w by standard learning-to-rank. Two
Goodhart channels: the loop optimizes for operator acceptance, not task success, so agents
drift toward legibility-pleasing self-presentation over capability; and only surfaced candidates
receive feedback (selection bias), requiring propensity-weighted counterfactual correction.
The fix is to move the label downstream: train on the witnessed outcome of the routed work
(did it land, per the outcome ledger), using the click only as an intermediate signal. Chapter
III’s substrate is thus the correct training signal for Chapter I’s ranker — a cross-chapter
dependency worth stating in the text.

Solution 11 (7.6⋆, decay vs. summary). Classify each signal by (a) reconstructability from
durable artifacts, (b) decision-relevance horizon, (c) write frequency.  Rule:  decay high-
frequency, short-horizon, reconstructable coordination traces (claims, presence, pheromones);
summarize low-frequency, long-horizon, non-reconstructable decisions (why-notes, design ra-
tionale); evict-plus-pointer for reconstructable artifacts (diffs, logs). Slogan: never summa-
rize what you can decay; never decay what you cannot reconstruct. The optimization un-
derneath: choose the treatment minimizing expected retrieval cost (storage + re-derivation
× recall probability + miss cost) subject to Thm. I.6.1’s floor on the critical set.


2.3 Chapter II (kernel)

Solution 12 (Linearizability, check). The four assumptions: (i) every claim/lock read and
write routes through one daemon and one database connection; (ii) read uncommitted dis-
abled; (iii) responses sent only after commit; (iv) no out-of-band writer. An out-of-band
SQLite connection breaks (iv) first — and, transitively, (i): there is now a second stream
of writes not ordered by the daemon’s commits, so the single serial order that the proof
linearizes against no longer exists.

Solution 13 (Linearizability, trace). History: A: claim(f) over [t0, t3]; B: claim(f) over
[t1, t4] (overlapping A); C: release(f) by A over [t5, t6]. Observed: A succeeds, B rejected,

C succeeds. Valid linearization: A (at its commit t2), B (at its rejection t2.5), C. Because
A and B overlap, the alternative order B →A would also respect real time if the results
matched it (i.e., B succeeded and A were rejected); with overlap, more than one linearization
can respect real time, and the observed outcomes select among them. Non-overlapping pairs
(B before C) admit only one order.

Solution 14 (OP-3⋆, differential-test harness). Minimal suite: (1) claim–release–claim cy-
cles on one key; (2) the multi-organ sequence claim + session-open + commitment (exercising
the OP-11 wrapper once it exists); (3) crash injection — kill -9 between write and com-
mit, then reopen and assert recovery state; (4) WAL checkpoint boundaries straddled by
operations; (5) contention — two clients through the daemon’s queue with busy-timeout at
the boundary; (6) pragma-sensitive sweeps: synchronous and journal mode settings the
shim normalizes. Observable-state assertions: after every step, a canonical full-table dump
hash must be identical across runtimes, and every response (including error codes and re-
jection reasons) must be byte-identical. Drive the identical operation sequence against the
test-runtime bindings and the compiled daemon; any divergence is an I11 counterexample.
This turns runtime parity from hope into a CI artifact.

Solution 15 (OP-11, cross-organ atomicity). Partial failure: port claimed, session opened,
commitment write fails.  Residual state:  a resource held by a session with no recorded
obligation — the completion gate has nothing to close, the agent sees a live session and
works, the monitor sees an unaccounted claim, and later audit cannot bind outcome to
commitment. The interface change: expose a single multi-organ begin endpoint whose body
is one local transaction (BEGIN IMMEDIATE . . . COMMIT) spanning all three writes. The Saga
alternative — compensations that release the port and close the session on commitment
failure — is strictly worse here: there is a visibility window in which other agents observe
the partial state, the compensation itself can fail, and idempotent undo logic must be written
and tested. Sagas earn their complexity when steps are remote; with one writer and one file,
atomicity is free and the transaction is strictly simpler and strictly stronger.


2.4 Chapter III (identity and the oracle)

Solution 16 (III.6, ex. 1). A reputation is exactly as meaningful as the cost of discarding
the name it attaches to. Whitewash: mint fresh i′ at zero cost, route future work through it;
the newcomer score weakly dominates the sanctioned score, so the sanction is never borne.
Sybil: mint n identities; each receives newcomer standing; their aggregate outweighs any
honest signal, forging every quorum. One cause, two attacks; one cure — strictly positive
abandonment cost.

Solution 17 (III.6, ex. 2). The shape (full work ability, reduced economic ceiling) charges
the whitewasher the cumulative surplus gap W every reset, while the honest newcomer pays
only the one maturation they would pay anyway — and retains full capacity to contribute
and accumulate witnessed history. “Distrust newcomers” (reduced work ability) inverts this:
it imposes deadweight loss on the honest party’s contribution capacity while barely touching
the fraudster, whose objective is the earning ceiling, not the work. The shape taxes exactly
the behavior it means to deter.

Solution 18 (III.6, ex. 3⋆, bond-farming). Principal binding is necessary: it kills the laun-
dering channel, since reputation keys to the principal via the delegation chain, so “selling
experienced agents” transfers nothing without transferring the principal — and then the
buyer inherits the whole record, wash trades included. But binding alone does not stop a
principal from inflating its own record. The elegant sufficient defense is counterparty-diversity

weighting: an outcome graded against a counterparty sharing your principal (or one with
high interaction correlation) contributes zero or heavily discounted reputation weight —
EigenTrust’s pre-trusted-set instinct applied to outcome provenance. Its false-positive cost
on honest pairs is near zero, because honest high-volume pairs across distinct principals are
unaffected; only intra-principal volume is discounted, which is precisely the wash-trade signa-
ture. Sampled adversarial re-audit of high-velocity, low-diversity pairs then covers collusion
across principals, at cost ρ× audit price × flagged volume, tuned by the Becker condition
(ρdB > wash gain). The listing fee is a rate limiter, not a defense.

Solution 19 (III.11, ex. 1). The grade’s producer must itself be incentive-compatible. “The
daemon derives the grade” relocates trust without discharging it:  the daemon computes
mechanically from judge inputs, and if a judge gains from a dishonest input, mechanical
derivation faithfully launders the dishonesty into an authoritative-looking grade.

harbors within the revocation window); J’s bond is slashed to the harmed party or commons;
J’s judge-reputation is debited; the graded agent’s downstream reputation is recomputed net
of the tombstoned entry.

synchronous rounds, reliable per-edge delivery; let each harbor hold an append-only log
and let restriction be prefix projection.  Claim:  if all pairwise overlaps agree on common
prefixes (compatible local sections), a unique global log exists (the glue), and this holds
iff no harbor equivocated. Proof: prefix-compatible logs form a semilattice under longest-
common-prefix; compatibility pairwise implies a unique join by induction on the graph; an
equivocation is exactly a pair of incomparable prefixes signed by one key, which destroys
pairwise compatibility on some edge once co-located. The lesson the exercise teaches: at
this scale the sheaf language adds naming, not power — the entire content lives in the
equivocation-detection protocol — which is the concrete ground for the review’s “commit or
cut” advice on §IV.13.

4.3 What a conflict is, and who decides

Define a conflict as a deontic inconsistency: commitments whose oracles cannot jointly close
— OA(φ) and OB(¬φ), two owners scheduled onto one resource window, an accepted pro-

split: detection is mechanical; resolution is political. Detection bound worth stating: general
propositional consistency of a commitment set is co-NP-hard, but a restricted commitment

5 The clean-room harbor: Derek and Erin

5.1 The problem, stated in the volume’s terms

Derek holds confidential data D; Erin holds a proprietary agent stack S (skills, prompts,
fine-tunes). Each fears exfiltration of their asset through the other’s channel. This is the
strongest possible test of “hosted trust is the product” (§IV.11):  the harbor must let S
compute over D while provably bounding what flows out in either direction.


5.2  Theoretical base

Four literatures, each carrying its own limit honestly:

1. Information-flow control. Noninterference (Goguen–Meseguer) as the ideal; the de-
   centralized label model (Myers–Liskov) as the practical lattice:  every artifact carries
   owner labels, labels join on combination, and only an owner’s declassifier lowers its own
    label.

2. Quantitative information flow (min-entropy leakage, Smith 2009) to measure what
   a declassifier releases, and differential privacy to release aggregates under a metered
   ε-budget.

3. Confidential computing. TEEs with remote attestation answer “whose machine can
   be trusted to run the sandbox”:  a neutral enclave neither party controls.  Note for
   the volume: TEE attestation is also the most concrete existing candidate for the cross-
   operator attestation gap (Def. III.7.2) — a hardware root standing in for the missing PKI
   between distrusting operators.

4. Provenance. in-toto attestations (already cited) extended from build artifacts to datasets
   and skills: every artifact’s lineage is a signed chain, so “where did this number come from”
    is answerable in court, not just in prose.

And the honest limit up front: token-level taint tracking through an LLM is impossible —
the model taints everything it writes with everything it read (taint explosion). Therefore
the unit of control is the channel, not the token: complete mediation of every I/O path
(Mechanism 5 is a prerequisite), with declassification gates at the only exits.


5.3 The design

A neutral clean-room harbor: a daemon in an attested enclave (or a bonded neutral host),
with:

1. Labels. Lattice {⊥} ≤{D}, {E} ≤{D, E}. Derek’s data enters at {D}; Erin’s skills,
   prompts, and weights at {E}; anything the agent produces from both is {D, E} by join.

2. Complete mediation. The hypervisor daemon mediates fs/net/exec; no raw egress
   from the agent sandbox; the only exits are two gates, G→E and G→D.

3. Erin’s exit gate G→E (what Erin may learn): schema-restricted aggregates only; DP
   noise drawn against a metered ε-budget; verbatim-span suppression (n-gram and em-
   bedding match against D’s corpus); canary sentinels planted in D whose appearance
   anywhere past the gate is a tripwire with statistical power against leak size.

4. Derek’s exit gate G→D (what Derek may learn): results and reports, never the skill text,
   prompts, or weights — Erin’s stack runs as a sealed capability: an attested, inference-
   only binary Derek can invoke but not read. Symmetrically, no fine-tuning on D unless
   the resulting weights remain {D, E}-labeled inside the enclave, with a signed disposal-or-
   escrow ceremony at engagement end (memorization is exfiltration by gradient).

5. The release ledger. Every declassification is a witnessed event: gate policy version
   hash, artifact hash, ε spent, signer. The cumulative privacy budget is conserved exactly
    like the bond ledger — same theorem shape as VI.10.1, which is a satisfying structural
   rhyme: the harbor already knows how to conserve a scarce quantity through buckets; ε is
   one more.

6. Economics, correctly subordinated. An exfiltration bond deters marginal probing

   volume’s own layer ordering governs: structural prevention (Layers here: labels + media-
   tion + gates) is primary; bonds price the residual; an insurer (Rothschild–Stiglitz caveats
   apply) prices what neither can.

## Observation contract

Fix a fact f, its nonempty finite value set A, and a snapshot identifier.
Only channels with both directed reports for this fact and snapshot enter its
observed graph K_f. Missing reports remain unknown. For an oriented edge u–v,
retain the signed difference of the one-hot reports, `d_uv = e_b - e_a`.
This observation is either zero or has exactly one negative and one positive
coordinate. A zero difference erases the common value; it asserts equality only.

Categorical feasibility asks whether there is a map `x: V -> A` such that
`d_uv = e_{x(v)} - e_{x(u)}` on every retained edge. This is an existence question
about the admitted observations. It is not a verdict that all actual messages
were consistent, that all relevant messages were retained, or that any claim
was true. Raw directed reports permit a distinct, richer per-sender check.

## Exact decision and certificate theorem

Let Z be the subgraph of zero-difference edges. Every nonzero edge with
`d_uv = e_b - e_a` pins u to a and v to b.

**Theorem (categorical feasibility).** The admitted differences have a
categorical realization if and only if no connected component of Z contains
two pins with different values.

**Proof.** A realization is constant on each component of Z, and must satisfy
every pin, proving necessity. Conversely, assign each pinned component its
unique pinned value, and each unpinned component any value in A. Every zero
edge then has equal endpoint values, and every nonzero edge has its required
ordered endpoint values. This realizes all differences. The algorithm is
union-find followed by a pin scan, with near-linear complexity in input size.

An infeasibility certificate consists of two incompatible pins and a zero-edge
path joining their vertices. A path of length zero is allowed: two reports can
pin the same vertex differently. A single nonzero edge can supply both pins if
its endpoints are connected by a zero path. The verifier checks the cited
observations, orientation, pin labels, snapshot and fact, zero-edge path, and
distinct labels. It does not need to trust the decision algorithm.

This is elementary constraint propagation, not a novelty claim. Its importance
here is that it uses more of the stated categorical contract than real-valued
least squares. On the path 0–1–2, setting both differences to `e_b-e_a` forces
vertex 1 to both a and b. No categorical realization exists, but the real
potential `(e_a,e_b,2e_b-e_a)` fits exactly. A zero Hodge residual therefore
cannot certify categorical feasibility.

## Minimum-cost retained-evidence theorem

Assign each admitted difference edge a finite nonnegative cost. This is the
cost of retaining or presenting that complete edge observation, including its
two receipt references. Costs are additive over distinct edges. Values and
differences are already observed; no unknown query answer is supplied for free.

For a pin p, let `v(p)`, `a(p)`, and `e(p)` denote its vertex, value, and source
nonzero edge. Write `dist_Z` for shortest-path cost using zero edges, with
infinity between disconnected components. Then the minimum cost of an
infeasible retained subset is

`min_{a(p) != a(q)} [ dist_Z(v(p), v(q)) + cost({e(p), e(q)}) ]`,

where a shared source edge is counted once. If there is no finite candidate,
the complete observation set is feasible and has no such certificate.

**Proof.** Each finite candidate gives an infeasible subset by the preceding
theorem. Conversely, every infeasible subset contains two incompatible pins
connected by zero edges within that subset. A shortest zero path in the full
admitted graph costs no more than that connecting path. Its source edges and
zero path therefore yield a candidate costing no more than the subset. The
two inequalities establish equality. Nonnegative costs allow redundant edges
and cycles to be discarded. Pin edges are nonzero, so their costs never overlap
the zero-path costs; the only possible duplication is the two pins' source edge.

Enumerating pin pairs and running Dijkstra from each pinned endpoint gives a
polynomial exact algorithm. The implementation processes one source at a time
and can repeat a vertex for its distinct pins; with p pins it makes at most p
shortest-path searches and O(p²) pair comparisons, with O(|V|+|E|) auxiliary
storage beyond the input and output. This specializes standard shortest-path
and equality-constraint reasoning; it is not a theorem about optimal unknown
evidence acquisition, minimum semantic repair, or fault attribution. Other cost
models, such as shared disclosure overheads, are outside the statement.

## What topology contributes

For each fact separately, the optional real-valued residual and clique-complex
Hodge decomposition describe how its observed differences project onto gradient,
curl and harmonic spaces. Missing observations never introduce zero rows.
An edge's single-perturbation sensitivity is `1-R_eff(e)`; on a bridge this is
zero and its harmonic-share ratio is undefined. These are properties of the
linear detector, not limits on all categorical detectors. Dense diagnostic
budgets are enforced before allocation; declining optional diagnostics does not
disable the exact categorical check.

Gradient/curl/harmonic analysis of pairwise inconsistency is established in
[Jiang, Lim, Yao and Ye's HodgeRank paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.1067).
The useful comparison is what each checker certifies under identical retained
observations and what each certificate costs to inspect.

# Continuation after an unknown remote effect

## Decision and scope

The decision is whether a successor may send a second attempt for one work unit after the first caller crashes without a durable local result. A non-idempotent remote effect is counted as `effects += 1`; safety means `effects <= 1`. The finite checker covers one operation `O`, epochs 0 and 1, at most one old call and one successor retry, one effect location, and all interleavings of its declared transitions. It proves no property of deployed Harbor, arbitrary numbers of retries, multiple effect locations, or a real provider's contract.

The durable outbox contains an intent before the first send: work-unit identity, stable operation identity `O`, stable remote key `K`, target, input digest, the authorized effect and epoch 0. The successor inherits the same intent, obligations and uncertainty status. An acknowledgment can be lost after the remote effect; a local result receipt is a distinct durable transition. The remote dedup record, when available, is **atomic with the effect and result**. A local receipt alone cannot repair a missing remote record. A cached result may be read after epoch advancement to reconcile an old operation. Dedup protects this operation's effect count; denying stale actor authority for other effects requires a separate effect-boundary guard.

## Transition system and observations

The state is `(intent, old_sent, old_pending, old_done, old_result, crashed, epoch, remote_fence, observed, retry_sent, retry_pending, retry_done, effects, dedup, local_receipt, stopped, dropped)`. Boolean fields have their literal meanings; `epoch ∈ {0,1}`, `observed ∈ {unknown,absent,present}`, `dedup ⊆ {K,J}`, and `effects ∈ {0,1,2}` on explored shortest paths. `old_pending` and `retry_pending` include calls in transit that the crashed caller cannot inspect. A network loss marks the old call terminal **without** setting `old_result`; it cannot produce a success receipt. Remote commit is an atomic effect-boundary transition. A crash leaves in-flight calls intact and may occur before or after remote commit and before or after a durable local receipt. A successor promotion changes the assigned actor; in the readback adapter it additionally installs a durable remote fence serialized with remote effects. Remote receipt lookup/readback and local receipt persistence occur separately.

The caller's observation is its durable intent, crash/epoch assignment, acknowledged remote-fence installation, last readback result, known retry send, local receipt and stop status. It cannot see remote pending calls, network loss, actual effect count or dedup internals. A diagnostic `absent` is a snapshot, not a certificate that an unseen old call will never arrive. The checker constructs two reachable worlds with identical caller observations after an `absent` read: in one the old call remains pending, in the other it was lost. In the first, old remote commit remains enabled. Thus, with no dedup and no remote fence, retry is outside the common safe-policy set. Examples of safe policies are never resending while awaiting authoritative evidence, and stopping for reconciliation. These are examples from the no-second-send argument, not an exhaustive synthesized controller. If authoritative external reconciliation proves an outcome by a stronger contract, it may enlarge the set; this model does not assume such a contract.

For an observation class `C`, let `Safe(C) = ⋂_{s∈C} {π : every finite modeled continuation trace from s under policy π satisfies effects <= 1}`. The quantifier includes every enabled network and remote transition. A policy that sends a retry is assessed through both pending remote completions; the send step alone is never counted as a safety proof. If evidence refines `C` to `C' ⊆ C` while the policy and transition contracts stay fixed, then `Safe(C) ⊆ Safe(C')`. This monotonicity is about safety over the declared finite continuations; it promises neither completion nor a viable fair schedule. Operationally a continuation capsule needs the stable identity, obligations and evidence that determine the same safe-policy class. It need not reproduce an actor's whole transcript merely to preserve this decision, though other obligations may demand more data.

### Adapters and allowed actions

| Adapter | Exact capability and observation | Action after crash | Safety condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Atomic dedup and result | Remote serializes check of stable `K`, effect and durable result record at one effect boundary. Pending or completed duplicate requests with `K` cannot create another effect. | Retry `O,K`, or fetch its result, across actor epochs. | `K` stays bound to this logical operation and the result/dedup record remains until no old or successor retry can be admitted. This row proves duplicate-effect safety for `O,K`, not a general stale-epoch authority rule. |
| Authoritative readback and fence | A durable remote epoch fence rejects epoch 0 at the **actual effect boundary**. A later linearizable read of `O` returns exact committed outcome and result, or absence, ordered after that fence. | Persist a present result; on absence, send one epoch-1 attempt. | The fence is installed before the read; all earlier commits are reflected; old requests cannot commit after it. An in-flight epoch-1 attempt would need its own admission discipline before another retry. |
| Neither | No durable dedup/result contract and no remotely enforced fence/readback pair. | Stop and seek authoritative external reconciliation. | No automatic retry from silence, timeout, outbox entry or missing local receipt. |

The readback row is stronger than a plain GET. A linearizable negative GET alone is insufficient: an old request still in transit can commit after the GET. The remote fence must order with the effect and reject stale calls **when they actually reach that boundary**; a control-plane owner flag or a check only before send does not do this. An authoritative read must also resolve the specific operation and its result, rather than infer it from a coarse current resource value that may have changed for another reason.

## Finite checks and counterexamples

Run `python3 skills/harbor-results/scripts/continuation_observation_model.py` from the repository root. It is standard-library-only and import-safe; direct execution prints deterministic JSON and writes no files. BFS exhausts 23 honest dedup states, 24 honest fenced-readback states and 17 honest stop states, with no `effects > 1` and no local success receipt without a remote effect. State counts are for the exact finite alphabet above; they are neither a population estimate nor an unbounded proof. Four weakened variants yield shortest traces:

| Weakened guard | Shortest trace length | Decisive suffix |
|---|---:|---|
| Retry after a negative read alone | 8 | read absent; old call commits; retry commits |
| Admit stale epoch at effect boundary | 8 | fence; read absent; old call commits despite fence; retry commits |
| Change operation key on retry | 7 | old `K` commits; successor retries with `J`; second effect commits |
| Drop dedup result while retry admissible | 8 | old `K` commits; record evicted; same-key retry commits again |

Each trace begins with durable intent, first send, crash and successor promotion. The checker asserts honest safety and requires a violating witness for every mutation. Its shortest paths are shortest **within these transitions**, not minimum network failures in a production system.

## Safety argument and progress boundary

For dedup, induction over effect-boundary steps suffices: the only first commit of `O,K` atomically installs its result; any later `K` request reads that record and makes no effect. This induction requires the record's retention and stable identity conditions above. For fenced readback, any old commit either precedes the fence and is visible in the ordered read, or follows the fence and is rejected. If the read says absent, at most the single admitted epoch-1 attempt can commit; if present, there is no retry. The stop adapter never sends a second attempt. These arguments are conditional on the adapter contracts; the script checks their finite realization and exposes violations when selected conditions are removed.

Safety does not imply completion. Dedup permits progress only if the remote store remains durable, duplicate calls rendezvous with the record, retries are eventually delivered, and the operation eventually finishes or reports an explicit permanent error. Fenced readback permits progress only if fence installation and ordered read eventually complete and the successor attempt is eventually delivered. Under neither capability, conservative stop preserves safety but may remain unresolved indefinitely; operator or provider reconciliation is an additional capability, not a fairness consequence. A durable outbox plus blind at-least-once delivery is a baseline for not losing work, but it does not establish at-most-once non-idempotent effects. A durable outbox paired with stable-key remote idempotency is the direct baseline for safe automatic continuation.

## Relation to existing work and operational value

The result-record baseline is established prior art. RIFL requires a unique RPC identifier, an atomic durable completion record containing the result, retry rendezvous and guarded garbage collection; its paper also distinguishes in-progress and stale calls. [Lee et al., *Implementing Linearizability at Large Scale and Low Latency*, §§3–4](https://web.stanford.edu/~ouster/cgi-bin/papers/rifl.pdf). The Harbor contribution here is a bounded decision table and falsification harness for a specific cross-actor continuation question, not a new generic RPC impossibility theorem or a novelty claim.

Paper 2's controllability discussion motivates making the remote effect boundary the enforcement point; Paper 5's migration model concerns inherited score attribution and does not settle unknown external effects. The [corpus reading ledger](corpus-reading-20260928.md) identifies those gaps. The operational test for a candidate provider is concrete: can it bind an operation ID through retries, atomically retain and return its result, or install an effect-boundary fence and provide exact ordered readback? If neither contract can be demonstrated, the work unit remains pending for reconciliation. No provider API, Harbor deployment, or field outcome was tested here.
