                                     Abstract

    What survives of a software agent when its body changes? An agent forks into eight copies,
        distills a skill into its successor, swaps the model engine behind its name, or dies with its
      provider and is resurrected from a checkpoint somewhere else. The classical framing of these
      events is metaphysical — the ship of Theseus, personal identity, survival under fission —
     and we refuse it entirely. A market does not need a fact of the matter about identity; it
      needs three conservation properties on ledgers, and this paper proves them.  (1) No-mint
      inheritance: when a fork or distillation grants the child a discounted share of its source’s
      reputation and debits the source that share — transfer semantics, not photocopy semantics
   — no sequence of forks, merges, chains, or re-derivation cycles pushes total live creditable
      reputation above total witnessed value; the theorem’s correct statement was forced by a
      counterexample that refuted the naive budget-only phrasing, and the copy-mutant it forbids
      turns one lucky episode into an 8.2× quorum multiplier. (2) Engine substitution: unattested,
      the price can never depend on the engine actually running, so swapping in a cheap engine
      always pays and Akerlof’s death spiral runs inside one identity; with attested engine ids the
      incentive flips to the planner’s own efficiency rule at zero audit stake whenever the attested
      price schedule passes through the full quality difference — a hypothesis on the pricing regime,
      not a consequence of attestation, and we name where it fails (Bertrand pricing on attested
      keys) — and the same three checks make resurrection across providers sanction-sound against
        its three named attacks. (3) The probation cliff: among all newcomer-restriction schedules
      with equal power to deter whitewashing, the maximally front-loaded feasible one uniquely
      minimizes the tax on honest newcomers — the ramp should be a cliff, of positive width
     when the newcomer’s own ceiling caps what a single period can hold back, and of no shape
      at all once the fraud gain exceeds what that ceiling can carry. Express lane: each section
      opens with its idea in one breath; the formal statement is in the box below it; a reader in a
      hurry needs nothing else.


1 The problem: the ship, rebuilt at sea

The scene. Overnight, a fleet does what fleets do. An agent with a strong track record forks
eight ways to parallelize a migration. A skill distilled from one of its good episodes becomes
v2 and wants a warm start instead of a cold one. An identity that built its record running an
expensive frontier engine quietly swaps a cheap distilled engine in behind the same name. A
provider shuts down, and the agent’s principal resurrects it from a checkpoint on a competitor’s
infrastructure, asking that its reputation come along. And at the harbor gate, a newcomer
arrives with no history at all — perhaps genuinely new, perhaps a sanctioned identity wearing a
fresh key. Each event asks the same question: is this still the same agent, and what is it owed?
   Philosophy has owned that question for twenty-four centuries without producing a fact of
the matter that a mechanism could safely depend on. We borrow exactly one thing from it and
say in §7 which half we decline: Parfit’s move of dissolving the identity question in fission cases,
so that what matters survives without any yes-or-no verdict on identity ever being reached [1, 9].

The design rule that licenses is flat: any mechanism whose safety depends on resolving the ship
of Theseus is unbuildable. We never decide whether the fork “is” its ancestor or the resurrected
agent “is” the deceased one. We ask instead what a reputation economy must conserve across
these events so that the sanctions it levies keep their teeth, and we prove three conservation
results — one per door through which continuity can be abused. The root the chain hangs from
is the program’s prior impossibility result (whitepaper Def. III.6.1 and its necessity theorem):
a reputation mechanism is sanction-respecting  if a dishonest witnessed outcome reduces the
score its producer can act under by some ∆> 0 for a non-trivial window;  if fresh identities
can be minted at zero cost, no sanction-respecting mechanism exists, because the whitewasher’s
accessible score never falls below a clean newcomer’s [4, 7]. Non-forgeable identity with positive
abandonment cost is therefore necessary — and this paper is about what remains once you
have it: the abuses that ride on legitimate continuity operations.  Forks and distillation ask
what a child may inherit (§2); engine swaps ask what the price must key on (§3); resurrection
asks what must be verified before a body change carries a record across providers (§4); and the
front gate asks what shape the newcomer ramp must be so that honest entrants pay the least
while whitewashers are still deterred (§5). Section 6 composes the answers into one sentence
about what actually survives a body change, and §7 places the results against the economics
they import.

6 What survives, then

   What survives of an agent when its body changes is not a soul but a ledger position: its
witnessed evidence, counted once; its price keys, scoped to the engine that earned them; and its
                          debts, scoped to the principal that owes them.

   The three theorems compose into a single continuity contract, and the composition is the
point. Theorem 1 makes derivation safe: any number of forks and distillations may share an
ancestor’s evidence, but the evidence is counted once. Theorems 2–3 make body changes safe:
the price follows the attested engine, the sanction follows the principal, and a record crosses
providers only with its lineage verified and its liabilities attached. Theorem 4 makes the residual
entry point — starting fresh — cost the deterrence price up front, where it deters most and
taxes honest entrants least. Together they answer the operator’s real questions without ever
answering the philosopher’s: the eight forks are not “the same agent” or “different agents” —
they are eight debit lines against one witnessed balance. The resurrected agent is not “the
deceased, continued” — it is a successor that passed three checks and inherited a score and a
sanction ledger. The engine swap is not “a change of body” — it is a new price key under an
old sanction key. Continuity, operationally, is the conserved ledger; metaphysics never enters,
which is why the mechanism can be built.
   What falls out for the product is concrete: the resume button and estate export/import
get Theorem 3’s checklist as their acceptance test; skill distillation gets Theorem 1’s transfer
semantics as its inheritance API; the marketplace’s engine badges are Theorem 2b’s price keys;
onboarding gets Theorem 4’s cliff. And the quorum layer inherits the guarantee it actually
needs: no sequence of continuity operations manufactures voting weight, because every path —
fork, merge, distill, migrate, resurrect — conserves the same witnessed total.


7 Related work, and what is actually new

Imported. We take Parfit’s move and not Parfit’s thesis, and the difference is worth stating
because it runs the other way from what one would guess. What we borrow is the dissolution
[1, 9]: an identity question can be refused rather than answered, because what matters can
survive without any verdict on identity — §1’s refusal to adjudicate forks is that move re-run
on a ledger. What we do not borrow is his positive claim. Parfit insists that fission does not
divide what matters: “the relation of the original person to each of the resulting people contains
all that interests us — all that matters — in any ordinary case of survival” [9]. Theorem 1
makes the inherited prior scarce, conserved and divisible precisely so that it must split eight ways
among eight forks. A reputation ledger is exactly the kind of thing Parfit argues psychological
continuity is not, and that is why a ledger can be conserved where a stream of experience cannot.

one end of a continuum Grossman drew in 1981. His §2 shows that when quality is verifiable at
negligible cost a monopolist voluntarily discloses in full, because a buyer with rational expecta-
tions reads any withheld information as unfavourable [10]; Milgrom proves the same conclusion
game-theoretically — “at every sequential equilibrium of the sales encounter game, the salesman
uses a strategy of full disclosure” [11]. His §3 takes the opposite extreme, disclosure costlier
than the whole quality spread, and lands on our Theorem 2a: “we will have the usual ‘lemons’
problem . . . each high-quality seller will want to be distinguished from those of average quality,
but in this case there is no way for him to do so.” So Grossman’s §2/§3 pair is our Theorem
2b/2a pair, indexed by a disclosure-cost parameter we do not model — and we have accordingly
renamed Theorem 2a, since in this literature “the unraveling result” names the §2 conclusion,
which is full disclosure, not collapse.
   That renaming exposes a real question about Theorem 2b, and answering it is the sharper
contribution.   If unraveling holds, the daemon need only permit attestation and voluntary
disclosure will do the rest; our mandatory-attestation premise would be stronger than the
economics requires. The unraveling result needs several strong hypotheses [12], and at least two
fail here. Attestation is not costless. And more decisively, buyers cannot detect concealment
— Milgrom is explicit that his result assumes the buyer “can verify . . . statements like: ‘I have
reported everything I know’,” and in an agent marketplace a buyer cannot distinguish an agent
that declines to attest from one whose runtime cannot. With that hypothesis gone, voluntary
disclosure no longer unravels, which is why the daemon must furnish the attestation channel
rather than merely allow it. What Theorem 2b then adds to disclosure theory is that attestation
does not only reveal the engine, it re-prices it.
  A third hypothesis fails for a different reason: even a competitive market for attestation need
not unravel to full disclosure.  Lizzeri shows a monopoly certification intermediary optimally
withholds everything and extracts the entire surplus whenever its own profit, not the buyer’s
welfare, sets the disclosure rule, and that full revelation is recovered only in the frictionless
limit of infinitely many free-entering competitors — a limit any positive, sequential entry cost
defeats, sustaining the pooling monopoly indefinitely [13]. A voluntary, third-party attestation
market therefore inherits a failure mode a protocol-mandated channel does not: the daemon
is not a profit-maximizing intermediary choosing how much of the engine id to reveal, so its
incentive to pool never arises in the first place.

Intuition: the working port.  Watch a real port for a day (Figure 1). Whether two vessels
are on a collision course is geometry — constant bearing, decreasing range — computed identi-
cally by every watch officer; nobody’s authority is consulted. Who gives way is next decided by a
rulebook (the collision regulations) — still mechanical, still nobody’s judgment. Only where the
rulebook ends — a three-vessel crossing the rules never anticipated — does harbor traffic control
exercise chartered discretion. And the port’s one genuinely personal authority, the licensed pilot
with twenty years on these shoals, is hired against a pool of tug crews only when the water is
hard enough to pay the premium — and the port licenses a second pilot, because a port whose
only pilot can fall ill has priced its channel’s availability at one human body. The structural
mapping: collision geometry →in-fragment conflict detection (mechanical, witness-producing);
the rulebook’s edge →the fragment’s NP-complete frontier (where chartered resolution begins);
the pilot’s premium and the second license →the gA(ρ, c) boundary and the succession price
D⋆. The analogy maps relations, so it earns a prediction: making the rulebook richer should
eventually make rule-following itself intractable and reintroduce discretion — and that is exactly
what the NP-completeness theorem says happens one disjunction past the fragment.
   The predictable misread, preempted: mechanical detection does not mean mechanical gov-
ernance. The checker certifies the norm system, never the norms — a bad policy consistently
held is consistent — and detection without a resolution charter just produces alarms. The
theorems do not abolish authority; they relocate it, from noticing to choosing, and then hand

Logic.  Deontic logic is the logic of obligation and permission, as opposed to the logic of truth
— it reasons about what ought to be, not what is. Its two operators here are O (obliged) and
F (forbidden), and we apply them only to ground facts: an action, a scope, a time interval. A
Horn rule is an implication whose premise is a conjunction of atoms and whose conclusion is a
single atom — the shape almost every rules engine and every Prolog program already uses. A
definite Horn program has no negation, which is exactly what makes it cheap: its consequences
can be computed by repeatedly firing whatever rules are satisfied until nothing changes, and
this process is guaranteed to terminate at one canonical answer. That answer is the least model
M, and its defining property is the one Theorem 1a leans on:  it contains precisely the facts
forced in every model — and when ⊥∈M there are no consistent worlds at all, which is exactly
the conflict Theorem 1a is built to report. Either way a status the least model assigns is not one
possibility among several but a certainty. Unit propagation is the name for the firing procedure,
and Dowling–Gallier [1] showed it runs in time linear in the program.
  A difference constraint is an inequality of the form xj −xi ≤δ over deadline variables —
“the runbook update must land no more than six ticks after the deploy.” A system of them is
satisfiable exactly when its constraint graph contains no negative cycle, a loop of constraints
whose weights sum below zero and which therefore demands that some event precede itself.
Bellman–Ford finds such a cycle if one exists, and hands it over as the witness. This is standard
temporal-reasoning machinery; §8 names the literature that owns it.
  A problem is in P when some algorithm solves it in time polynomial in the input size —
the practical meaning of “tractable at scale.”  It is NP-complete when it is in NP — a
proposed solution can be checked in polynomial time — and every problem in NP reduces to it


                                         3

PAGE 4
in polynomial time, so a polynomial algorithm for it would put all of NP in P and settle the P
versus NP question. The working consequence, which is all Theorem 1b needs: an NP-complete
check cannot be run on every proposal at commit time as the policy set grows. 3-SAT is the
canonical NP-complete problem (is a Boolean formula in three-literal clauses satisfiable?), and
a reduction from it is the standard way to prove a new problem at least as hard: encode any
3-SAT instance as an instance of yours, so that solving yours would solve 3-SAT.
  A witness is the concrete object a checker returns alongside a yes — the derivation chain,
the two clashing rules with their overlap, the negative cycle. Producing witnesses is a strictly
stronger requirement than deciding, and it is the difference between a checker that says “re-
jected” and one a human can argue with.

3 Part I. The lookout is a subroutine: the fragment Lc

Cheap detection is a language-design choice, not a discovery about deontic logic in general. The
commitment language Lc buys it by construction. A policy set in Lc contains:
   • facts (ground atoms), definite Horn rules a1 ∧· · · ∧ak →b with b an atom, and
     integrity constraints a1 ∧· · · ∧ak →⊥; operationally ⊥is carried as a distinguished
     atom, so the program is definite over the atom vocabulary extended with ⊥, and the
      least-model machinery of §2 applies unchanged — a derivable ⊥is then simply ⊥∈M,
     the first of our four conflict kinds, rather than a failure of the procedure;

   • deontic rules body →M(act, s, [t1, t2]) with M ∈{O, F}: when the (Horn) body holds,
      action act is obliged or forbidden on scope atoms s over the ground time interval [t1, t2];

   • exclusive interval claims (resource x is exclusively mine on [t1, t2]);

   • difference constraints xj −xi ≤δ over deadline variables.
A conflict is any of four things: derivable ⊥; a fired O/F pair on the same action with overlapping
scope-and-interval; two exclusive claims overlapping on the same resource; or a negative cycle in
the difference-constraint graph (an unsatisfiable deadline system). This is deliberately a ground
fragment — no nesting of deontic operators, no negation-as-failure, monotone bodies only —
and §8 says explicitly which classical deontic puzzles are thereby left outside the door.

4 Composition with Paper 2: the lookout is not even a role

Paper 2 proved that a safety policy over an agent’s event alphabet is enforceable-by-prevention
— regimented, in the normative-systems sense of a norm the institution makes impossible to
violate rather than merely sanctioning after the fact [14] — iff it is Ramadge–Wonham con-
trollable — no uncontrollable event carries a legal history out of the policy — and its design
rule was: uncontrollable events in a policy’s condition are free; only uncontrollable events in its
prohibition are fatal. Now compose. In the harbor, acceptance of a commitment is a mediated
write: the accepted set lives in the single-writer store, and the acceptance event is a member
of Σc, the controllable alphabet. The policy “never accept a proposal whose union with the
accepted set conflicts in-fragment” therefore gates a controllable event on a condition that The-
orem 1a makes a total, polynomial-time-computable predicate of committed state. The policy
is controllable, hence regimentable: the conflict never enters the accepted set, because the dae-
mon refuses the write, with the theorem’s witness attached to the refusal [verified: composition
of Theorem 1a with Paper 2’s boxed theorem; both components machine-checked separately,

disjunction and you have hired a judge, with a queue.


5 Part II. The sole owner: an inequality, not a principle

The vocabulary of Part II: queueing.  An M/M/1 queue is one server, arrivals landing at
random at average rate λ, each job taking a random time averaging 1/µ. M/M/c is the same
with c interchangeable servers sharing one line — the airport-check-in arrangement, not the
supermarket one. Utilisation ρ is the fraction of capacity in use; as it approaches 1 waiting time
diverges, which is the entire reason these comparisons are not obvious. The Erlang-C formula
C(c, ρ) gives the probability that an arriving job finds every server busy and must wait at all.
It is a century old [5] and it is the only non-elementary ingredient in Theorem 2; everything
else there is algebra on it. Pooling is the practice of putting all work in one queue served by
everyone, as opposed to dedicating a specialist to it. The classical fact — and the tension the
paper prices — is that pooling wins on waiting time through statistical smoothing, while a
specialist may win on service rate through skill. The skill premium r = µs/µg is how much
faster the specialist is, and Theorem 2 asks exactly how large it must be to pay. Four prices
ride along: the accountability value A (the worth of single-writer attribution per unit time of
demand), the waiting cost w per request-hour, the specialist’s death rate ξ, and the succession
rate η (mean spin-up 1/η); K = A/(wλ) + Wpool is the shorthand for the pool’s cost line the
two theorems compare against.  Finally, a queue with breakdowns is one whose server fails at
some rate and is restored after some delay.  Its relevance is that a sole owner is a server that
can fail: sessions die, containers are reaped. Theorem 3’s W∞is the residual delay such a queue
carries even with an infinitely fast server, which is why no amount of skill buys it back.
   Part I located the one place inside conflict management where a mind is genuinely required:
not to notice a contradiction but to choose a discharge among disjuncts the fragment cannot
rank on its own. Part II asks the harbor’s other standing authority question, about a different
kind of decision entirely — not which candidate resolution to pick, but whether one designated
person should be doing the picking at all — and it gets the same kind of answer: not a principle
to invoke but a number to compute. The whitepaper’s sole-responsibility roles (roadmap owner,
test-suite curator, release avatar) trade pooled capacity for accountability and skill. Model the
trade honestly.  Requests for the invariant-critical function arrive Poisson at rate λ; a sole
specialist serves them as an M/M/1 queue at rate µs; the pooled alternative is an M/M/c
queue of generalists at rate µg each, utilization ρ = λ/(cµg); the skill premium is r = µs/µg.
Sole ownership also carries the accountability value A against the waiting cost w just defined.

8 Related work

Imported. Linear-time Horn satisfiability and unit propagation are Dowling–Gallier [1]; we
import the algorithm and the least-model property unchanged, and our fragment is designed
so that it applies. NP-completeness machinery is Cook and Karp [2, 3]; the reduction in The-
orem 1b is standard 3-SAT gadgetry, and the contribution is only the location of the frontier
— discharge-choice disjunction — in a commitment language a scheduler would actually want.
The temporal half of the dichotomy is Dechter, Meiri and Pearl [17], who established both the
polynomial simple temporal problem and the NP-hardness of the disjunctive temporal problem;
Stergiou–Koubarakis [18] is the algorithmic successor we cite alongside it. The regimentation
composition imports Ramadge–Wonham supervisory control [4] via Paper 2, and uses regimen-
tation in Jones and Sergot’s [14] sense. On the queueing side, the Erlang-C delay formula is a
century old [5]; the economies of pooling are classical — Smith and Whitt [7] established the
resource-sharing comparison of one shared multi-server queue against dedicated ones (and the
heterogeneity caveat under which sharing can hurt), which is the ancestor of Theorem 2’s finite-
c pooled-vs-dedicated form, while Halfin–Whitt [6] sharpened the many-server scaling regime
in which the economy is usually quantified — and queues with server breakdowns descend from
Mitrany–Avi-Itzhak [9]; Theorem 3’s Wbd is in that lineage. Positioned against deontic
logic. The fragment is ground and operator-nesting-free:  conflicts are defined operationally
(O vs F on overlapping scope and interval), not as theoremhood in classical deontic logic [10],
and the classical paradoxes — Ross’s paradox [11], Chisholm’s contrary-to-duty puzzle [12]
— simply cannot be stated in Lc:  that is a designed retreat, declared rather than hidden,
and it is what the tractability is paid for with. Positioned against computational nor-
mative systems. The adjacent literature that owns detecting conflicts between obligations
and prohibitions is not the philosophical one: it is the normative-multi-agent-systems line col-
lected in Meyer and Wieringa [13] and pursued in the normative-conflict work of Vasconcelos,
Kollingbaum and Norman [15], whose conflict predicate is, like ours, operational rather than
logical — and that is the point at which their line and ours converge rather than diverge. The
tractable/intractable dichotomy is not new in shape, and a search since the last
draft found the nearest neighbor. Colombo Tosatto, Governatori and van Beest prove

1 What the analyst can know

A federation sends authenticated witness-log reports along a graph. An auditor wants to know
whether one witness gave incompatible reports to different peers. The evidence question asks
which authenticated statements reach the auditor. The algebraic question asks whether derived
edge differences fit one assignment of states to vertices. A cycle residual answers the second
question; the first determines whether that answer adds information.

claims reach the auditor with the same source, coordinate, and snapshot identifier, a direct
duplicate-claim check detects the conflict. The check does not require a and b to compare with
each other. A detector that discards those claims and retains only edge differences cannot fairly
claim an advantage over the direct check.

2 Cochains, sections, and cycles

A cellular sheaf assigns a vector space to each vertex and edge and a restriction map from
each incident vertex into the edge space. The paper uses coordinate-selection maps.  Its real-
valued stalks model features of log reports, conditional on an equality-preserving map from
authenticated claims; they are not raw cryptographic log heads.
   The coboundary δ maps a vertex assignment x to its oriented edge differences.  For one
scalar coordinate, δ is the signed incidence matrix. The assignment x is a zero-cochain; the
pattern δx is a coboundary. A global section of the unshifted sheaf instead satisfies δx = 0.
The detector asks whether the observed edge cochain g lies in im δ, meaning that some vertex
assignment explains its differences. It does not assert that the explaining assignment is a global
section of the unshifted sheaf, or that the sender claims were mutually consistent.
  A signed sum of a coboundary around a graph cycle telescopes to zero.  The quotient
H1 = coker δ describes edge data modulo coboundaries; in the coordinate-selection graph model,
its Euclidean representative is the projection onto the cycle space. The existence of nonzero H1
says the topology admits an obstruction. It does not say the observed execution has one: only
the class of g can do that.
   The completion residual r is the Euclidean distance from g to im δ after severed edge rows are
omitted. Effective resistance of an edge is the voltage drop across it under one unit of injected
current in the unit-resistor graph. It governs how strongly a single-edge perturbation survives
this projection. These objects can be computed with incidence matrices and least squares; the
cohomological language identifies their structural meaning without adding information to the
observed receipts.

5 The harness: what its trials establish

The synthetic harness uses 200 trials per arm at seed 20260816, real five-dimensional stalks,
and shared coordinate subsets. The checked-edge baseline tests whether a directly checked edge
exposed the fault. A trial labeled cohomology-only means the residual was positive while this
restricted baseline was silent. The harness also reconstructs each sender’s visible coordinate
claims and runs Proposition 2’s equal-information duplicate-claim check.

  Observed behavior. In the two-path split-view arm the residual was positive and the
  checked-edge baseline silent in 200/200 trials. In the expander arm the corresponding count
  was 113/200, with 87 residual-dark trials. Of those 87, 79 had no relayed incident fault
  edge and 8 had a relayed fault edge on no visible coordinate cycle. The severed-cycle arm
  gave 0/200; a cut-edge arm had maximum numerical residual 1.5 × 10−13 over 400 trials.
  The no-equivocator control gave 0/200. Across all nine arms and 1,800 trials, the equal-
  information checker found zero residual-only cases and 209 direct-only cases. These counts
  support Proposition 2 within the synthetic feature and snapshot model; they are not a
  deployed signed-log evaluation.

   The counts depend on the sampled topology, offsets, metric, and threshold. The harness
checks the blind-spot dimension against independent sender-map nullity calculations in all 224

parison has been run on these synthetic records; exact cycle sums and noisy scoring have not
been compared. An operational benchmark must predefine authenticated receipt and snapshot
binding, the equality-preserving feature map, noise, false-alarm threshold, runtime cost, and
localization target, then run all three evaluators on matched evidence.

declared worst-pair margin per query cost; the ranking needs predicted signatures and costs,
and no universal optimality follows. Actual observed y is unknown before a query, so (3) alone
is not an ex ante information-gain promise. If authenticated endpoint claims are retained, direct
sender-claim comparison is still the equal-information baseline.


9 Related work and contribution

Cellular sheaves on graphs and their coboundary calculus follow Curry [3]; spectral sheaf meth-
ods follow Hansen–Ghrist [4]. HodgeRank already decomposes edge observations into a best-fit
gradient and a cyclic residual [5].  Effective resistance as an incidence-row leverage score is
also established  [7]. The language of local consistency without a global assignment is related
to Abramsky–Brandenburger contextuality [2].  Robinson [8] supplies the consistency-radius
perspective. The projection, cycle-space identity, and effective-resistance law here are familiar
graph linear algebra rather than a new cohomology invariant. The marginal receipt formula
is likewise a rank-one least-squares identity in graph form. Its use here is to state a checkable
acquisition rule and its disconnected-component exception for this evidence contract; it is not
a claim of a new resistance or experimental-design theorem.
   Robust HodgeRank studies noisy and contaminated edge comparisons with cyclic projections
and statistical outlier detection [6]. The bounded-error separation above is an exact statement
for the paper’s specified edge-only evidence and adversarial Euclidean error balls; it does not
claim a new general robust-ranking method.
   PeerReview [1] and BFT forensics [10] motivate preserving authenticated statements that
can identify a conflicting sender. When both endpoint claims are available to the analyst, a
direct duplicate-claim check has that evidentiary advantage. The present real-coordinate model
instead characterizes the consistency score of derived edge differences. An exact cycle-sum
checker sees the same noiseless inconsistency as its least-squares residual; the residual adds
a metric magnitude and a topology-dependent distribution of error. The contribution is an
explicit information contract, the one-edge sensitivity formula under visible-edge deletion, the
general single-sender kernel characterization, sharp bounded-error margins for one-edge and
all one-sender faults, and a counterexample that prevents extending the one-edge criterion to
arbitrary split views.

        yield the same edge-difference vector; retaining authenticated claims is necessary for
        direct attribution.

1 Question and contribution

Agent workflows distribute evidence across roles: an author records work, a reviewer sees a
subset, a CI job observes a commit and test run, and a publisher sees an approval or artifact
receipt. A global claim can fail even when each observed overlap appears locally coherent.
The question is which incompatibilities can be inferred from the evidence an auditor actually
receives.
    Cellular sheaves give a precise language for this question. A stalk records one typed feature at
a cell; restriction maps state which part of a role’s state can be compared on a handoff or joint
contract. Cohomology distinguishes a local face-relation violation from a globally nontrivial
closed obstruction, while relative cohomology tests extension through a visibility boundary.
These constructions are established mathematics [2, 1, 6]. The contribution here is a concrete
agent-evidence contract, exact failure-observability criteria, and an executable comparison with
simpler checks. We make no claim that a topological signature alone establishes which agent
erred.
   The numerical examples use exact count features, one work item, and one immutable event-
log watermark. A production observation must bind each packet to its schema, work item,
source identity, log root, and evidence reference. An artifact digest or approval cannot be
treated as a real coordinate merely to make a Laplacian run. We keep the external truth oracle
separate from algebraic compatibility and use a synthetic fixture to expose the information
boundary before collecting field traces.

5 The simpler baseline

When packets expose both endpoint claims, the auditor can compare repeated reports made
about the same node. Define D = 1 if some node has two incident packets giving it different
values at the same feature, work item, watermark, and log root. This check uses equality and
a map keyed by node; it needs no graph solver.

Theorem 7 (Duplicate-claim dominance for visible endpoints). On complete metadata-valid
packets as defined in Section 3,  if D = 0 then r(y) = 0.  Consequently, every positive cycle
residual is also detected by the duplicate-claim baseline. The converse need not hold: a duplicate
claim can be inconsistent even when the edge differences form a gradient.

Proof. If D = 0, choose xv to be the common endpoint claim for each non-isolated vertex v,
and choose any integer value for each isolated vertex. Then Eq. 4 gives ye = xv −xu on every
edge, so Theorem 5 yields r = 0. For the converse, take a triangle whose every reported edge
difference is zero.  Set endpoint claims to (0, 0) on two edges and (1, 1) on the third. The
differences are all zero, while at least one repeated node claim differs.

cannot improve detection recall over the equality baseline under the same metadata and packet
set.  It may still help explain a pattern when raw endpoint claims are unavailable, when only
edge differences can be disclosed, or when independent redundant paths have special provenance.
Those are distinct privacy and acquisition contracts requiring their own tests. We claim no cost
or utility advantage for the current setting.

Theorem 8 (Conditional failure-mode identifiability). For the fixed deterministic library above,
the projected observation Qy uniquely identifies the injected label j in the absence of noise if
and only if γ > 0.  If the observed projection is zj + Qη and ∥Qη∥2 < γ/2, nearest-signature
classification returns j uniquely.  If γ = 0, no rule using only the projected observation can
always distinguish every label in M.

Proof. When γ > 0, all prototypes are distinct. For any i ̸= j, the triangle inequality gives
∥zj +Qη−zi∥2 ≥∥zj −zi∥2−∥Qη∥2 > γ/2, whereas the distance to zj is below γ/2. Conversely,
if γ = 0, finiteness implies zi = zj for some distinct pair. The same observation then occurs
under both labels, so a deterministic or randomized rule cannot be correct with certainty in
both worlds.

   For the particular library of one signed unit error on an unknown edge, topology alone gives
a sharper criterion. Let ei denote the ith coordinate vector in RE, and consider the 1 + 2|E|
labels {0} ∪{+ei, −ei : i ∈E}. The label describes one corrupted edge report, not the agent or
event that caused it.

Theorem 9 (Three-edge-connectivity criterion). For a connected loopless graph with at least
two vertices, all labels in the signed single-edge library have distinct cycle projections if and
only if the graph is three-edge-connected, meaning removal of any one or two edges leaves it
connected. A bridge makes its own error invisible; a non-bridge two-edge cut makes two signed
edge-error labels indistinguishable. This criterion assumes exact edge-only differences and known
unit amplitude.

Proof. Write qi = Qei.  If qi = 0, then ei = Bx for some potential x. On every edge other
than i the potential difference is zero.  If deleting i leaves the graph connected, x is constant
and Bx = 0, a contradiction.  If i is a bridge, assigning potentials zero and one to the two
components after its deletion gives Bx = ±ei and thus qi = 0.
   For distinct non-bridge edges i, j, an equality qi = ±qj means ei ∓ej = Bx. All potential
differences vanish outside {i, j}; if deleting both edges leaves a connected graph, x is constant,
again a contradiction.  Conversely,  if deleting i and j disconnects the graph while neither is
individually a bridge, the remaining graph has two components linked by those two edges.
Assigning potentials zero and one to the components gives Bx = ±ei ± ej, so one signed label
on i shares a cycle projection with one signed label on j. The nominal label is distinct from every
edge label exactly when there are no bridges. Combining these cases proves the criterion.

   The signed-unit criterion is a special case of a support-level boundary.  Let λ(G) be the
minimum number of edges crossing a nontrivial vertex cut, counting parallel edges separately,
and let Σk = {a ∈RE : ∥a∥0 ≤k} denote arbitrary-amplitude edge-report errors on at most k
edges. This model permits unknown support and magnitude; it still does not identify the agent
or event that produced an erroneous report.

7 Reproducible offline protocol

The typed-complex companion scripts/sheaf 2complex study.py constructs the nonuniform
stalks and incidence maps of Section 2.1 with exact rational arithmetic.  It rejects malformed
maps when BA ̸= 0, computes cohomology ranks and Hodge projectors independently of a

These are synthetic cochain tests, not observed rates of agent failures. Their purpose is to force
a claim about a face, a hole, or a missing observation to have a reproducible exact witness.
   The graph fixture script sheaf observability study.py constructs a four-node square
with a diagonal, plus a triangle with a bridge. It fixes one integer feature and one watermark,
and tests all 35 = 243 edge perturbations in {−1, 0, 1}5 on the first graph.  Its exact rational

oracle. The two implementations agree on all 243 perturbations; this checks the implementation
against a distinct calculation, not against a field truth source.  It reports the duplicate-claim

8 Operational application and scope

A field audit should start from one immutable work item, PR head, workflow attempt, artifact
identity, and ledger watermark. The additive coordinates in the typed fixture can count accepted
completions and validated handoffs. Reviewer approvals, commit digests, and publisher grants
remain exact symbolic predicates checked against authenticated event records. Each edge packet
must say which role acquired it, from which independent source, and through which map its
value enters the stalk. A three-party face contract needs its own provenance-bound receipt if
it is to add evidence; the algebraic face relation alone only changes the interpretation of an
existing edge residual.
   The practical comparison uses the same available inputs for every method: metadata and
provenance checks, repeated-claim equality, an exact typed-constraint solver, and the sheaf

channels. Predeclared interventions include a stale CI attempt, mismatched PR head, replayed
approval, forged edge report, jointly consistent false reports, missing packet, and no fault. An
independently extracted ledger or symbolic contract oracle supplies truth labels. A graph or
sheaf score earns an operational claim only  if it improves detection or audit cost at a fixed
false-alarm budget, or gives a measured explanation benefit that a direct solver does not. The
synthetic fixture makes no such field claim.
   Relative cohomology adds a precise question when evidence is partial: can the visible com-
patible section extend through the declared hidden contracts? A nonzero connecting class rules
out any extension under those maps; a zero class leaves actual hidden work unverified. Hodge
components similarly describe the selected cochain complex. Human intervention must follow
authenticated provenance and policy evidence, not a harmonic-to-curl ratio. Large sheaves may
also make exhaustive support-distance and singular-value calculations expensive; deployment
would need bounded, receipted approximations or a smaller audit subcomplex.


9 Related work and novelty boundary

Cellular sheaves, their cohomology, relative exact sequences, and Hodge Laplacians are estab-
lished [1, 2].  Combinatorial Hodge ranking already separates gradient, curl, and harmonic
components of pairwise data [6]. Sheaf cosystolic expansion supplies local-to-global and testing
criteria under strong complex and sheaf hypotheses [3]; it does not make a nontrivial H1 class
visible to a face-only test. Relative spectral diagnostics with a separate grounding morphism
provide another relevant construction [4]. Sparse recovery and coding-distance arguments also
predate the edge-group support theorem [5]. Discourse sheaves model selective communication
and lying [7], while cellular-sheaf coordination has been studied for heterogeneous multi-agent
systems [8, 9].
   The mathematical statements in this paper specialize that literature to a declared agent-
evidence contract. The potentially distinctive contribution is a testable design method: specify
typed and provenance-bound restrictions, compute local, global, and relative obstruction classes,
state exactly which injected report errors the map can distinguish, and compare against an
equal-information direct solver. The heterogeneous fixture demonstrates the method and its
limits; it is not evidence of broad field utility. A useful next result would show that independently
sourced edge and face receipts reveal a real workflow failure more cheaply or more clearly than
direct authenticated contract checks, under a predeclared acquisition and privacy budget.


10 Conclusion

Typed cellular sheaves can express information that a scalar graph cannot: different overlaps
reveal different coordinates, joint contracts impose face relations, and incomplete visibility cre-
ates an extension problem. In the exact fixture, a count-face violation and a closed handoff-loop
obstruction occupy orthogonal cohomological channels; the relative class identifies a visible sec-
tion that cannot extend. The sheaf edge-group distance states when sparse erroneous reports
are detectable or uniquely recoverable. These are precise statements about a selected evidence
complex. The same calculations show why topology alone cannot establish truth: coherent
false reports remain invisible, a face without new evidence cannot increase detection, and a
direct solver with the same packets has the same compatibility information. The field ques-
tion is whether a provenance-bound sheaf audit improves the cost or clarity of checking real
multi-agent work. The protocol here makes that question falsifiable.

records.title: The five assurance modes (Observed/Coordinated/Brokered/Confined/Attested) are the Book's one taxonomy of its own and had never been placed against Sheridan's l
records.result: The five assurance modes (Observed/Coordinated/Brokered/Confined/Attested) are the Book's one taxonomy of its own and had never been placed against Sheridan's levels of automation, Parasuraman-Sheridan-Wickens, or the Common Criteria's EALs. Either the ladder is a restatement -- say whose and cite it -- or it is a different axis, in which case say precisely what it measures that those do not.
assumptions: Targets and adjudication are source claims at the ledger revision; they do not prove current manuscript state.
evidence: Supersedes the one-sentence gesture landed for LR-111 (e62037ada), which asserted 'a third axis' without saying what it measured.

Not a restatement; the three axes are independent and the placement now says why. Sheridan & Verplank (1978) grade the allocation of the decide-and-act loop (who does it) and Parasuraman-Sheridan-Wickens split that across four processing stages; Common Criteria EAL1-EAL7 grade how much independent evaluation effort a claim received before deployment, once, for a whole product; the ladder grades what an adversary would have to defeat for one runtime claim about one mechanism to be false. Stated at the kernel chapter's 'What it buys', with the independence written as a pdclaim{Design invariant} exhibiting the corners (a Sheridan-level-10 component whose actions are merely logged is Observed; a level-3 component routing its one effect through an attested broker is Attested; EAL7 products can contain Observed mechanisms), and the boundary in the same breath (a design vocabulary, not a measured scale; the rungs are not evenly spaced or totally ordered). sheridanverplank1978 added as a bibitem to the kernel chapter and the sealed room -- it was uncited, only parasuraman2000 was present; cciso15408 sharpened from 'current edition' to ISO/IEC 15408-1:2022. The appendix's 'Five assurance modes' prose was rewritten to match but stays citation-free, since that file has no reachable bibliography (the constraint LR-111 recorded).

records.title: The tractable-then-NP-complete frontier of ch.6 stands against Colombo Tosatto, Governatori and van Beest's compliance-checking dichotomy. Determine whether L_c
records.result: The tractable-then-NP-complete frontier of ch.6 stands against Colombo Tosatto, Governatori and van Beest's compliance-checking dichotomy. Determine whether L_c is inside their tractable side, outside it, or orthogonal, and make the chapter say so.
assumptions: Targets and adjudication are source claims at the ledger revision; they do not prove current manuscript state.
evidence: Supersedes LR-408 (0ac32d8b2), which added the citations and a hedge ('one does not subsume the other') but did not answer inside/outside/orthogonal.

ORTHOGONAL, and now demonstrated rather than asserted. Both papers read in full (arXiv:2001.10148, arXiv:2105.05431). Their axis across all eight variants is literals vs formulae in the obligation's elements: for full compliance, literals give P in all four variants and formulae coNP-complete in all four; the 1/n and G/L coordinates do not move the class. L_c fires on Horn bodies -- conjunctions, derived through a program that may chain -- so it is on the HARD side of their only decisive coordinate and is polynomial anyway, which is the tell that the problems differ. Their hardness comes from the process model, not the obligations: the coNP-completeness reduction builds an interpretation WF-net with one XOR bond per propositional variable so the 2^n executions enumerate every interpretation, and quantifies over them universally. L_c has no process model to branch and conflict-freedom is existential over schedules, which is exactly why one step out is NP rather than coNP. Honest residue recorded in the chapter: the nearest variant in their lattice is PARTIAL compliance (NP-complete in six of eight, P in one, and still open for 1L-, a single conditional obligation over literals); our theorems neither close that hole nor can, and a reduction in either direction between L_c-conflict-freedom and 1L- partial compliance would settle the relation. Nobody has written one. Also fixed: both ctgvb bibitems gave van Beest the initial P; he is Nick.

records.title: The Anchor chapter was described as silent on algorithm-confusion attacks on its token encoding while proofs/anchor/token-verify/algconfusion.pv models exactly
records.result: The Anchor chapter was described as silent on algorithm-confusion attacks on its token encoding while proofs/anchor/token-verify/algconfusion.pv models exactly that and passes; a chapter whose ProVerif model covers an attack its prose never names is under-claiming.
assumptions: Targets and adjudication are source claims at the ledger revision; they do not prove current manuscript state.
evidence: Supersedes LR-106 (e62037ada), whose added sentence is the one this row corrects.

Sharper than the review's framing: the chapter was not silent, it CONTRADICTED ITSELF. Table tab:properties already claimed 'Algorithm Confusion Immunity / Yes / ProVerif' while limitation (iv) said the boundary 'rests on the fixed-algorithm implementation, not on a mechanized proof of it' and that 'no query in Table 4 models the parser's algorithm-selection logic' -- false, since algconfusion.pv had been passing. Limitation (iv) rewritten to name both attacks (alg:none downgrade; asymmetric public key as HMAC secret), state the Model-checked property (accepted_pinned(m) => issued_A(m) TRUE under an adversary handed the AlgB symmetric key outright), give the naive verifier's counter-trace in its four steps as ProVerif returns it, and cite the model by path; the two queries added as rows to tab:proverif-results so the prose's reference is honest. Boundary moved rather than closed and said so: the model gives the signature slot two non-coercible types, which is the type-safety a real parser must supply and which no query checks, so the decoder remains covered only by the bounded Kani harness. Also fixed: ietf2024jwtbcp was cited as a 2024 IETF draft; it has been RFC 8725 (BCP 225) since February 2020.

records.title: Theorem 4.4.1's Erlang-C specialization boundary assumes stationary Poisson arrivals and strictly exponential service; agent execution durations are heavy-taile
records.result: Theorem 4.4.1's Erlang-C specialization boundary assumes stationary Poisson arrivals and strictly exponential service; agent execution durations are heavy-tailed and submissions arrive in correlated bursts, so the specialist queue is exposed to Kingman-type delay explosions. Qualify the theorem with an M/G/1 Pollaczek-Khinchine variance expansion.
assumptions: Targets and adjudication are source claims at the ledger revision; they do not prove current manuscript state.
evidence: ADJUDICATION-2026-09-08.md CA-004 ACCEPT-IN-PART: a boundary paragraph, not a change of statement, plus an Allen-Cunneen heuristic and a Pareto/lognormal sweep of `skills/harbor-results/scripts/b8_specialization.py`.

New $\S4.4.3.1$ *What heavy tails do to the boundary*: Kingman for the general cost, Allen--Cunneen and Pollaczek--Khinchine worked through both sides, and the un-obvious conclusion the adjudication predicted -- variance scales both waiting terms by about the same $\kappa=(1+c_s^2)/2$, so the boundary barely moves and accountability enters as $A/\kappa$, weighing *less* against queueing rather than more. Stated as an Empirical hypothesis with its falsifier and the `b8_specialization.py` sweep that would settle it; no number is quoted because no sweep has run, and infinite-variance Pareto is named as where the heuristic stops rather than degrades. Boundary, not statement -- the theorem is exact inside its named model.

records.result: Theorem 7.7.2's repeated-game analysis assumes perfect public monitoring; under message loss, partitions and gossip latency, monitoring is imperfect and private, and deterministic trigger strategies collapse into unrecoverable punishment cascades. Contextualize within the private-monitoring literature (Kandori-Matsushima belief-free equilibria) and introduce communication and review phases before sanctions.
assumptions: Targets and adjudication are source claims at the ledger revision; they do not prove current manuscript state.
evidence: ADJUDICATION-2026-09-08.md CA-011 ACCEPT-IN-PART: a monitoring boundary naming what supplies perfect public monitoring inside one harbor (the single-writer ledger) and what happens once the history is gossiped; re-deriving the theorem under private monitoring is research, filed for ch. 8. The adjudication also found the reviewer's root 0.3419 to be a slip -- the cubic's real root is 0.34251, so the Book's 0.342 stands.

Monitoring boundary under `prop:claim-signaling-ic`. Green--Porter and Kandori--Matsushima cited as the mechanisms for that regime, and the cross-harbor case recorded as open in both ch. 7 and ch. 8 rather than assumed away; it is also now a row in the open-problem concordance. No reordering, no new bridging chapter, no retitling of $\S4.1$--$4.2$ -- all three stay the author's call or declined per the adjudication.

records.result: The relationship between discrete epidemic gossip dissemination and continuous sheaf Laplacian diffusion remains unresolved in Section 8.5.4 and is admitted in Section 8.12; formalize it as Open Problem 12 so readers do not conflate continuous topological diffusion with discrete packet-switched gossip.

records.title: Incorporate Holmstrom (1982): in joint production with unobservable individual effort, budget-balanced sharing rules cannot achieve efficient effort without an
records.result: Incorporate Holmstrom (1982): in joint production with unobservable individual effort, budget-balanced sharing rules cannot achieve efficient effort without an external budget breaker. The commons pool functions precisely as that budget breaker, since forfeit bonds are absorbed into it rather than refunded to the buyer.
assumptions: Targets and adjudication are source claims at the ledger revision; they do not prove current manuscript state.
evidence: ADJUDICATION-2026-09-08.md CA-035 ACCEPT and called apt: `slash(id,p)` routes p to the commons pool and never back to the counterparty, which is exactly the budget breaker.

The adjudication called this the most valuable of the literature set and it reads that way. Holmström (1982) now explains a design decision the conservation worked example walked past: the slashed bond routes to the commons pool and never back to the counterparty, which is a budget breaker, and budget balance has to break for his reason -- a penalty that is another participant's windfall costs the pair nothing. Scoped: the mechanism is not claiming first-best effort, only borrowing the structural reason, which is why Conservation holds over $W+E+C$ and not over wallets alone.

records.result: Chapter 6 §6.17's Purchased Assurance Bound notes reviewer correlation only in an informal pitfall box; formalize the degradation with a pairwise correlation parameter rho, expressing the effective panel size, to show mathematically how foundation-model monocultures undermine purchased assurance.
assumptions: Targets and adjudication are source claims at the ledger revision; they do not prove current manuscript state.
evidence: ADJUDICATION-2026-09-08.md CA-041 ACCEPT-IN-PART: the mixing-model form of CA-008, shared with ch. 5; the reviewer's design-effect exponent declined for the reason given there (it is the design effect for the variance of a mean, exact only at rho in {0,1}).

New $\S$*Putting a parameter on the echo* in ch. 6 carries the model ch. 5 shares. Per-panel detection rate $D$ of mean $d$ drawn once and shared; miss probability $\mathbb E[(1-D)^k]\ge(1-d)^k$ by Jensen, so the independent bound is *optimistic* rather than conservative, for every mixing distribution -- that inequality is the part to quote. Beta mixture with intra-panel correlation $\theta$ telescopes into a product of $k$ fractions. Worked example uses only numbers the chapter had already fixed ($d=0.8$, $k=3$) and lands on the pitfall's own sentence as arithmetic: at $\theta\to1$ three reviewers deliver the assurance of one, 25x worse than the line item. Checked against a Monte Carlo run and the Gamma-function form before printing. $\theta$ is unmeasured and the text says what would measure it.

records.result: Section 1.7 conflates cryptographic capability attenuation (who authorized whom) with coordination lineage (the task parent-child DAG) by using "delegation chain" for both; enforce a strict terminological distinction, "authorization chain" for cryptographic tokens and "task lineage" for coordination graphs.

evidence: ADJUDICATION-2026-09-08.md CA-045 REFUTED: §1.7 has a subsection making exactly this distinction, in these words; the review read an older draft.

Now actually done, and the earlier `DONE 1cad994e3` was wrong: that commit landed ch. 1's subsection *Two delegation chains, one dangerous name*, which is why the reviewer's charge against §1.7 is refuted, but the promise it makes -- "We never again write bare 'delegation chain'" -- was kept in ch. 1 and nowhere else, as this row's own Notes said while the Status said otherwise. Every site in the eight chapters was read and classified rather than replaced. Eighteen uses resolved to `authorization chain`, the object every one of them turned out to denote (ch. 1, 2, 5, 7, 8); ch. 4's rival name `delegation trace` for ch. 1's **coordination lineage** is retired, one object to one name. Twelve sites keep the phrase because they mention rather than use it: the titles that name the pair, the four quoted appearances in the defining subsection, a verbatim ProVerif model comment, and the descriptive genus used immediately after naming the object. The guard the old Notes said was missing is `scripts/harbor-research/check_delegation_chain_vocabulary.py`, wired in `library-checks.yml` with those four recorded by exact phrase (permanent editorial decisions, not debt); 15 tests, mutation-tested both directions. Note the old Notes' site list was short because `grep` is line-based and the phrase wraps: the check finds the wrapped ones too. Reviewer's proposed `task lineage` is declined in favour of the Book's own `coordination lineage`.

records.title: The caption of Figure 4.5 notes that the simulation sweep data (r1-floor.csv) was not yet committed, so the plot reflects the analytic curve rather than measure
records.result: The caption of Figure 4.5 notes that the simulation sweep data (r1-floor.csv) was not yet committed, so the plot reflects the analytic curve rather than measured empirical data; execute the experiment script, commit the raw CSV, and overlay the empirical points on the theoretical curve.
assumptions: Targets and adjudication are source claims at the ledger revision; they do not prove current manuscript state.
evidence: ADJUDICATION-2026-09-08.md CA-053 ACCEPT: the R1 script emits the CSV, the plot reads it, and the caption's sentence is deleted in the same commit; verified by a check that no caption in the corpus says "not yet present" or "not committed".

Closed, and closed without inventing a data series. `a7_experiment.py` now emits `whitepaper/figures/data/r1-floor.csv` (seed 20260816; 16 budget points at N=60, k=2, m=8; oracle, noisy and random encoder miss rates) and the CSV is committed. What is overlaid is one measured *marker*, not a measured curve, and the caption says why: Floor(N,k,m) is a closed form and exactly computable, so it has no empirical counterpart to plot against it. The honest measurement is the smallest swept budget at which the oracle encoder observed zero misses -- 8.99 bits against the 5.98-bit analytic floor. The three-bit gap is the finding, not an embarrassment: the bound holds as a bound and a real encoder pays more, because the shared codebook is a randomised cover rather than an optimal one. No zero-miss point is marked on the flat curve because the sweep's range tops out at 10.98 bits, below that curve's 12.77-bit floor -- the split penalty made visible by the measurement failing to reach it. The caption sentence at `:48` and the source comment at `:2` are gone, the `--allow` is dropped from the `library-checks.yml` step, and `tests/harbor-research/test_check_absent_data_captions.py` now asserts the corpus is clean *and* that the CSV exists and the figure cites it, so the debt cannot be cleared by deleting the sentence alone.

records.result: Theorem 5.6.1 proves non-forgeable identity is necessary for any sanction-respecting reputation; explicitly contrast the centralized daemon-attested identity chosen for Port Daddy with alternative Sybil-resistance mechanisms from permissionless systems such as proof-of-stake or deposit bonding, to justify the architectural trade-off.

evidence: ADJUDICATION-2026-09-08.md CA-055 ACCEPT-IN-PART: one paragraph in §5.7 -- stake binds capital, not a principal; the Book's answer is the no-mint result plus per-principal exposure pooling, and ch. 7's bonds are where capital enters.

$\S$*Why not stake?* after the no-mint result. The contrast is made on the axis that matters: stake bounds how many identities an adversary mints and says nothing about whose they are, which is the wrong axis when the conduct being sanctioned is a party's; the no-mint result conserves creditable reputation across a derivation graph whether identities are cheap or dear, and per-principal exposure pooling does the rest. The trade is named rather than won by definition -- daemon attestation costs a trusted local authority, which is what a permissionless system refuses to assume -- and capital is placed where it does enter, as ch. 7's bonds priced against a breach rather than a toll at the door.

records.title: Several exercise solutions contain valuable theoretical extensions -- the Succession-Rate Breakdown Threshold in Exercise 4.19 and the five-tier Agent Death Tax
records.result: Several exercise solutions contain valuable theoretical extensions -- the Succession-Rate Breakdown Threshold in Exercise 4.19 and the five-tier Agent Death Taxonomy in Exercise 5.38; promote these formal results from the solutions manual into the primary chapter narratives.
assumptions: Targets and adjudication are source claims at the ledger revision; they do not prove current manuscript state.
evidence: ADJUDICATION-2026-09-08.md CA-061 ACCEPT-IN-PART: the taxonomy yes (with CA-070); for the succession result, name the exercise by label, because the exercise number is edition-specific and the formula the review quotes does not occur in the source.

The accepted half (naming `ex:ls-succession-corner` by label rather than by edition-specific number) predates this pass. The remaining half turned out to be smaller than the row reads, and the reason is worth recording. The result was ALREADY in the Book's narrative -- ch. 6 carries it as `thm:succession-price` with the full closed form, the $\eta K<1$ proviso, the $\eta K\ge1$ case, a `pdboundary` that declares the death-at-all-times breakdown model as decisive, and verification against a matrix-geometric solution (1.95e-13), a truncated CTMC (1.38e-14) and a Gillespie DES [verified, `b8_specialization.py`]. It belongs there: it is a condition on what a succession plan costs, which is an economic statement. What ch. 4 needed was a pointer, not a second copy -- a copy would have been the CA-014 defect (one result defined twice in two chapters) in a new place. `sec:succession-corner` in $\S4.4$ is now that pointer plus the two consequences that change what a sole-responsibility role MEANS rather than what it costs: skill has a ceiling ($W_\infty$ is never attained, so past a point the fix is a better handoff and not a better owner), and the ceiling binds absolutely only while $\eta K<1$. Two LOCAL corrections land in the ch. 4 exercise solution, which is where the genuine defects were: it gave $D^\star$ unconditionally, dropping the $\eta K<1$ proviso (and $\eta K\ge1$ is the commoner case in a well-run fleet, so this was not a corner), and it called the breakdown-corrected wait 'exact' without naming the model that makes it exact. PROCESS NOTE, since the skill forbids silent rewrites: this pass first drafted a full duplicate theorem in ch. 4 together with a claim that ch. 6's closed form was not exact, on the strength of a 7-46% disagreement with a Pollaczek-Khinchine computation. Running `b8_specialization.py` refuted that: the disagreement was against a DIFFERENT model (active-only breakdowns), not a defect in the formula, and ch. 6's boundary already declares which model it means. The draft was retracted before commit. The surviving observation is the one the chapters now state: under active-only breakdowns the floor is 0 and $D^\star$ does not exist, so the model choice is the whole result.

records.title: Frame cognitive attention explicitly as an information-theoretic channel-capacity problem.
records.result: Frame cognitive attention explicitly as an information-theoretic channel-capacity problem.
assumptions: Targets and adjudication are source claims at the ledger revision; they do not prove current manuscript state.
evidence: New row: not separately adjudicated; the adjudication took the two figure rows from this table cell (CA-065) but not the framing.

$\S4.6$ now names the frame before proving against it: the operator is a channel with a capacity, the swarm a source with a rate, and the chapter is what information theory says when the rate exceeds the capacity. That is why the results are rate results and the central bound is in bits rather than seconds or dollars, and it closes the tempting mistake -- more dashboards move the capacity, and the bounds hold at every capacity. Read-poverty is named as the regime rather than as the chapter's only vocabulary.

records.title: Unify Parfitian psychological continuity with cryptographic key-lineage transfer protocols.
records.result: Unify Parfitian psychological continuity with cryptographic key-lineage transfer protocols.
assumptions: Targets and adjudication are source claims at the ledger revision; they do not prove current manuscript state.
evidence: Done as $\S$`sec:parfit-lineage-map` in ch. 5, and done at the epistemic kind the claim actually earns -- `pdclaim{Design invariant}`, not Theorem, because it states what the system is built to do and takes no position on whether it tracks personal identity. The correspondence that holds is exact and narrow: both Relation R and credential lineage are the ANCESTRAL of a direct relation that is not itself transitive ($\mathsf{conn}^*$ and $\mathsf{succ}^*$), so the engineering is not Parfit-inspired but the same construction on a witnessed base. The previous pass was right that the honest version has to say where the analogy fails, and the `pdboundary` names three places. (i) Connectedness admits degree and signature verification does not, so the ledger criterion cannot express partial survival at all -- the case Parfit finds most interesting is the one it is structurally unable to represent. (ii) Fission gets a determinate answer from the no-mint rule (debit the source, discount each child) that Parfit deliberately refuses to give; that is a decision imposed because an economy needs conservation, not a discovery about identity. (iii) Lineage is constitutively third-personal, which immunises it against the Williams framing warning the chapter already cites -- its one clear advantage over its source -- but means possession of a predecessor's key proves CUSTODY TRANSFER, not continuity of anything psychological. (iii) carries a stated obligation rather than an answer, per the skill's open-problem rule: a continuity witness attesting WHAT THE SUCCESSOR ACTUALLY LOADED (which notes, which checkpoint, which ledger positions), which is a schema and attestation-coverage question and which no design in the chapter specifies.

records.result: Conjectures without formal proofs must either be stated as numbered research problems with empirical falsification criteria, or scaled back to exploratory design discussions.
assumptions: Targets and adjudication are source claims at the ledger revision; they do not prove current manuscript state.
evidence: New row: the review states this as a separate requirement from the concordance and it was not rowed in the adjudication. Related in spirit: the falsification-first discipline the research program already applies to results.

STILL OPEN: a wave, not a commit, and the adjudication says as much. Re-measured on this branch rather than restated: `chapter_lint.py --table` reports 17 blocking failures and 8 advisory floors unmet across the eight chapters, and `claims_carry_epistemic_kind` is one of the two blocking floors, failing on six of the eight (only `sealed-harbor.tex` passes it outright). The apparatus exists -- `pdclaim{Conjecture}` is available and used, `program.json` carries nine open problems each with a falsifier -- but the workflow step is `continue-on-error`, so nothing acts on the measurement. Closing this means clearing the floor chapter by chapter and then dropping `continue-on-error`; doing it partially leaves the step still advisory and buys nothing. Worth recording from this pass: the floor checks only that a kind TAG EXISTS, never that the chosen kind is CORRECT, and the one claim added on this branch (`inv:parfit-lineage`, tagged Design invariant rather than Theorem because it states what the system is built to do) was kind-checked by hand, not by the linter. A floor that cannot catch a mislabelled kind is not sufficient for what this row asks; that gap is part of the obligation and is not yet designed.

records.title: Critical Analysis of 2026-09-08 (`docs/harbor-research/exposition/critique/CriticalAnalysis-2026-09-08.md`)
records.result: A thirty-page outside review of the whole Book by a reader who reworked the mathematics: an executive assessment, an audit of seventeen theorem statements, a literature table, a visual-register audit, chapter-by-chapter tactical guidance, and a publication roadmap. It was adjudicated the same day, item by item, against commit `daf24d62e`, in [`ADJUDICATION-2026-09-08.md`](exposition/critique/ADJUDICATION-2026-09-08.md) -- sixty-one rows, `CA-001` to `CA-061`, each with a verdict (ACCEPT / ACCEPT-IN-PART / DECLINE / REFUTED) and a receipt. Item 13 of that file's own work list ordered this fold, and until now it had not happened: `CA-` matched nothing in this ledger or in `critique-ledger.json`, and no file in the repository linked to the adjudication, so the one question this ledger exists to answer could not be asked of it. Ids here are the adjudication's own, so `CA-017` in this table is `CA-017` there. Rows `CA-062` and up are items the adjudication grouped or did not separately row -- the eight figures the review prioritises are eight distinct renderer specifications, OP-6, OP-7 and OP-8 get three different recommended actions, the chapter/module table asks for five things no other section repeats -- plus two of the review's checkable factual assertions about the Book, which are rowed so that checking them is on the record rather than in someone's memory. `Status` here is filled in against the tree at `c92efaa5c`, not against the adjudication's verdict: a row is `DONE` only where a file and a line say so, `DECLINED` where the premise is refuted or the action was adjudicated away with a reason, and left empty where the change has not landed. Every `Notes` cell opens with `NOT ADDRESSED`, `PARTIAL`, `Receipt:` or `Verified:` and then gives the evidence, because an audit that says "addressed" without a receipt is exactly the failure mode this apparatus exists to catch. | # | Section / page | Kind | Item | Targets | Prior adjudication | Status | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | CA-001 | Rigorous mathematical and formal analysis -- Thm 1.8.3 | correction | Theorem 1.8.3 (Regimentation is controllability) proves its result under complete observability; i

records.result: Every "the paper does not cite X" claim in these packages was produced by running grep against the source, not by reading and remembering. Run from `docs/harbor-research/tex/`, case-insensitive, extended regex: | Command | Result | |---|---| | `grep -Eic "kofman\|lawarr" paper3.tex` | 0 | | `grep -Eic "2607\|certified runtime\|tool-using agent" paper2.tex` | 0 | | `grep -Eic "halpern\|weissman\|robaldo" paper6.tex` | 0 | | `grep -Eic "herlihy\|rajsbaum\|kozlov\|saks\|zaharoglou" paper7.tex` | 0 | | `grep -Eic "peerreview\|haeberlen" paper7.tex` | 0 | | `grep -Eic "ligatti\|falcone\|edit automata" paper2.tex` | 0 | | `grep -Eic "dechter\|simple temporal" paper6.tex` | 0 | | `grep -Eic "schaefer\|dichotom" paper6.tex` | 0 | | `grep -Eic "diamond\|townsend" paper3.tex` | 0 | A row of zeros proves nothing on its own — it is equally consistent with a broken pattern or the wrong file. Controls, run at the same time against citations the papers demonstrably do carry: | Control | Result | |---|---| | `grep -Eic "ramadge" paper2.tex` | 9 | | `grep -Eic "becker" paper3.tex` | 3 | | `grep -Eic "chisholm" paper6.tex` | 2 | | `grep -Eic "robinson" paper7.tex` | 4 | Two of the absence rows are worth calling out because they are not about the four flags and were found while checking them. `paper6.tex` contains no occurrence of "dichotom" in any form, which is the direct evidence for the renaming recommendation below — the result is a dichotomy and the paper never says the word. records.title: Why these four and not the whole sweep
records.result: The first sweep was run against the website's summary copy (`website-v2/src/data/researchPapers.ts`) rather than the papers themselves, so its headline conclusion — "no prior art engagement" — was wrong. Every paper in `docs/harbor-research/tex/` already carries a substantive Related Work section with real citations. That correction is on the record in `BIBLIOGRAPHY.md` under "What the first sweep got wrong." What survived the correction is these four. Each was re-checked by grepping the actual source for the specific citation in question, and in each case the source genuinely does not engage the work named: | Flag | Paper | Missing engagement | Verified absent by | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Paper 3, `paper3.tex` | Kofman & Lawarrée 1993 and the hierarchical-collusion line | `grep -i "kofman\|lawarr"` → no match | | 2 | Paper 2, `paper2.tex` | A possible same-year, same-claim preprint | `grep -i "2607\|certified runtime"` → no match | | 3 | Paper 6, `paper6.tex` | The complexity-of-compliance-checking line | `grep -i "halpern\|weissman\|robaldo"` → no match | | 4 | Paper 7, `paper7.tex` | Combinatorial topology of distributed computing | `grep -i "herlihy\|rajsbaum\|kozlov"` → no match | Flags 1–3 are novelty risks: prior work may already own the result. Flag 4 was two things at once — a citation the sweep itself flagged as possibly fabricated, and a real canon (Herlihy–Shavit and successors) that Paper 7 omits entirely.

records.title: What the four dives taught about the sweep that spawned them
records.result: These packages were written on the assumption that the earlier sweep had fabricated a citation. **That assumption was wrong in both places it was tested.** Flag 4's "suspiciously round numbers" paper is real (just weak), and flag 2's arXiv preprint is real (just orthogonal), confirmed with a control: `2607.22868` returns HTTP 200, a same-shaped fake `2607.99999` returns 404. Three lessons carry forward, and they invert the packages' original framing: 1. **`uncertain` entries should be checked, not discounted.** The sweep's hit rate on unverified citations is better than assumed. 2. **A `WebFetch` block is not evidence a source does not exist.** `curl` through the agent proxy reaches hosts `WebFetch` refuses; flag 1's decisive source was found this way, via Semantic Scholar's `openAccessPdf` field pointing at a DSpace@MIT copy no search engine surfaced. Flag 4's unresolved Bach 1999 is worth retrying by that route. 3. **The control test is the transferable technique.** An arXiv `abs` 200 proves nothing on its own. One extra request settles it. And the deeper lesson: **three of the four most valuable findings came from places the packages did not point.** Flag 1's C=1 arithmetic defect and flag 2's two Schneider bugs were found by hostile reading of our own papers, not by literature search; flag 3's closest-on-problem citation (Gaertner et al.) came from a survey fetched while chasing an unrelated open item. The flags were worth running, but what they were *aimed at* was mostly not what they hit.

records.result: Run 2026-08-26, after the four flags closed. records.title: Severity, and what each outcome means
records.result: Each dive ends in one of four verdicts. Write the verdict at the top of `findings.md`, before the evidence. - **CLEAR** — the prior work is genuinely different. Add a citation and one honest "how we differ" sentence. No result changes. - **NARROW** — the prior work covers part of the claim. The claim survives but must be restated with the narrower scope stated up front. - **SUBSUMED** — the prior work already proves this. The contribution becomes the application, not the theorem. Rewrite the contribution paragraph and say so plainly. - **CONTRADICTED** — the prior work proves something incompatible. Stop. This is an error to fix, not a citation to add. Flag 1 is the only one where CONTRADICTED is a live possibility, which is why it is first.

records.title: The rules every dive runs under
records.result: 1. **Read the primary source.** Not the abstract, not a summary, not another paper's characterization of it. If the PDF cannot be obtained, the verdict is `UNRESOLVED — source not obtained`, never an inference from the abstract. 2. **Quote the competing theorem verbatim**, with its own hypotheses, into `findings.md`. Most apparent conflicts dissolve on the hypotheses, and the only way to see that is side by side. 3. **Never invent a citation.** Every entry needs a DOI, arXiv ID, or stable URL that resolves. A source you cannot find is reported as not found. 4. **Label confidence on every claim**: `verified` (primary source read), `probable` (secondary source consistent across two independent references), `uncertain` (single unverified mention). Only `verified` entries may enter a `.tex` file. 5. **A negative result is a result.** "Read it, it is genuinely different, here is the distinguishing hypothesis" is the most valuable outcome and the one to expect most often.

records.title: The two dive patterns
records.result: **Planned dive** (`flag-N-<slug>/`) — use when the risk is narrow and specific enough to hand to a separately-dispatched agent (or a future session) with no other context: a single named competing result, a single suspect citation. The brief has to stand alone, so it needs all six files. ``` flag-N-<slug>/ README.md the claim under test and what a resolution looks like reading-list.md sources in priority tiers, with retrieval notes questions.md the questions the read must answer, most decisive first prompt.md the verbatim agent prompt skills.md which skills apply to this dive and why findings.md filled in by the dive; verdict first, then evidence ``` **Direct dive** (`paperN-<slug>/`) — use when the calling session runs the read-plus-falsification pass itself, in one sitting, against a whole paper rather than one named risk. There is no separate brief to write because nothing is being handed off — `prompt.md`/`questions.md`/`reading-list.md`/`skills.md` would just restate what `findings.md` already answers. Two files are correct here, not a gap against the planned-dive layout: ``` paperN-<slug>/ README.md one-paragraph index entry: paper, verdict, one-line summary findings.md verdict first (per claim, if the paper has several), then evidence ``` Write `TEMPLATE.md` in this directory before starting a new dive of either kind — it has copy-pasteable skeletons for both patterns and the rule for choosing between them. `BIBLIOGRAPHY.md` holds the consolidated citation register across the four planned dives, plus the cross-disciplinary renaming register — terms the papers coined that already have established names in other fields. A citation surfaced by a direct dive that should move into the register goes there too; `BIBLIOGRAPHY.md` is corpus-wide, not per-flag.
