This guarantees runtime parity across bindings." **Current text** (fig-swk-dual-runtime.tex caption, unchanged): "Invariant I11 (runtime parity) is therefore \textsf{partial}, and open problem OP-3 asks for the differential-test harness --- identical operation sequences against both runtimes, asserting identical observable state --- that would make it a theorem." **Current text** (line 1234, exercises): "\textbf{(open, $\bigstar$ OP-3)} Specify the minimal differential-test suite that would make I11 a theorem: what operation sequences, what observable-state assertions, run against both runtimes?" **Current text** (Table `tab:invariants`, line 1167, unchanged): "I11 & Runtime parity... & \BuiltWeak{} (OP-3)" **Proposed rewrite:** If Differential Fuzzing is real and running in CI, upgrade I11 to `\Built` in the table, rewrite the figure caption's last sentence to state the fuzzing regime as the closing mechanism instead of a still-open ask, and turn the exercises entry into a `(check)` — "the CI pipeline's differential fuzzer asserts hash-equivalence over $10^6$ operations; what class of divergence would $10^6$ *not* catch?" — rather than asking the reader to design a suite that (per the body) already exists. If it is aspirational, say so with `\Designed` and drop "This guarantees." **Priority:** high. ---

records.title: A3. OP-4 (checkpoint with teeth): the paper's own "most important unbuilt thing" is declared solved 500 lines later
records.result: **Location:** §"The continuity organ," lines 1069–1074 and the pull-quote at lines 1056–1062, plus `fig-swk-continuity-organs.tex` caption, vs. §"Open problems," line 1597. **Issue:** *Overclaim contradicting the paper's own headline finding.* §7 (continuity organ) is explicit and consequential: "Checkpoint is \BuiltWeak... A checkpoint with teeth... is open problem OP-4, the most important unbuilt thing at this layer because it is the literal foundation of any reputation economy." The pull-quote calls it "the weakest continuity link." The figure caption repeats "partial... is the literal foundation of a cross-machine reputation economy." Then, in the master Open Problems list, unhedged: **Current text** (line 1597): "\item[$\bigstar$ OP-4 --- Checkpoint with teeth.] Realized via \textbf{Event-Sourced Neural Rehydration}. By restoring the Git SHA, truncating the JSON message array, and replaying via Prompt Prefix Caching, the daemon restores the full KV-Cache state, turning ``recovery passes notes'' into ``recovery restores work.''" This is also, independent of the consistency problem, the single least-hedged, least-graded, and technically shakiest sentence in the paper: no maturity grade, no citation, and "restores the full KV-Cache state" glosses over the fact that a KV cache is bound to a specific model/inference session, not a portable artifact a restarted process can simply "replay" back into existence. **Proposed rewrite:** Either (a) remove this entry and leave OP-4 genuinely open, consistent with §7 and the figure — the honest and currently-accurate choice given the rest of the document — or (b) if some version of this mechanism is real, restate it with a maturity grade and the same rigor as the rest of §7: "\Designed: a proposed checkpoint mechanism snapshots the working-tree diff, open claims, commitment set, and the last $N$ turns of transcript (name the concrete artifact — not KV-cache state, which is not durably restorable across a process boundary); replaying it primes a fresh agent's context but does not resume its exact internal state." Then update the pull-quote and figure caption to match whichever choice is made. **Priority:** high. ---

records.title: A4. OP-5 (oracle completeness): CSMA is declared solved but the algorithm it extends was never updated
records.result: **Location:** §"Cryptographic State-Machine Assertions (CSMA)," lines 1017–1019, vs. Algorithm `alg:close` (lines 990–1001) vs. exercises box line 1034. **Issue:** *Internal inconsistency at the level of the pseudocode itself*, not just prose. §7.6 claims: "CSMA extends the oracle vocabulary by adding \emph{Delta Oracles}... and \emph{AST Assertions}... By restricting `done' conditions to these cryptographically verifiable state transitions, the kernel achieves oracle completeness." But Algorithm `alg:close`, three subsections earlier, enumerates the *entire* oracle kind set in code: **Current text** (line 996): `if kind not in \{RELEASED_CLAIM, MERGED_COMMIT, PASSING_TEST, POLICY_SUBCHECK\}:` No `DELTA_ORACLE` or `AST_ASSERTION` kind appears. And the exercises box for this very section still poses the problem as unsolved: "\textbf{(open, $\bigstar$ OP-5)} Extend the Law-2 oracle vocabulary to capture a `done' condition it currently misses, without re-admitting free text. State your new oracle and prove it is Goodhart-resistant." **Proposed rewrite:** If CSMA is real, add the two kinds to the algorithm listing and to Table `tab:invariants` row I6, and change the exercise from `(open)` to `(check)`: "CSMA adds `DELTA_ORACLE` and `AST_ASSERTION` kinds; walk one closure attempt through each and show where `verify_holds_now` would call out to `tree-sitter`." If it is not yet real, grade it `\Designed` and keep OP-5 open as currently written elsewhere. **Priority:** high. ---

records.title: A5. OP-7 (schema evolution): the "solution" abandons the exact property the open problem asks to preserve
records.result: **Location:** §3.3 "Linear Migration Ledger (OP-7)," lines 499–501, vs. its own exercises box, lines 513–522, vs. master Open Problems entry, lines 1602–1603. **Issue:** *Overclaim that also mismatches its own problem statement.* OP-7, as posed in the exercises box for this very section, asks: "Can idempotent self-init be extended to safe renames/backfills/down-migrations \emph{while preserving `any module, any order'}? Or is a version table unavoidable?" The body's answer is the second option — abandoning "any module, any order" entirely in favor of a strict sequencer — which is a legitimate engineering answer, but the section doesn't say so; it reads as though the original property survived. **Current text** (line 501): "The kernel now enforces a strict, linear migration ledger managed exclusively by \texttt{agentsd} via SQLite's \texttt{pragma user\_version}. Modules no longer self-initialize; instead, the daemon executes a strictly ordered set of migrations upon boot, guaranteeing a deterministic schema state for all subsequent agent access." **Proposed rewrite:** "The kernel resolves OP-7 by giving up `any module, any order' rather than saving it: a strict, linear migration ledger, managed exclusively by \texttt{agentsd} via SQLite's \texttt{pragma user\_version}, replaces per-module self-initialization. Modules declare migrations; the daemon applies them in one total order at boot. This is Table~\ref{tab:honestkey}'s second question ('is a version table unavoidable?') answered yes — the schema is now deterministic, at the cost of the flexibility the schema-by-union design offered." Then update the exercises box and the master Open Problems entry to match (retitle from a live question to a closed decision with its trade-off named). **Priority:** medium. ---

records.title: A6. OP-9's `SO_PEERCRED` claim directly contradicts the Threat Model table — a security-relevant factual conflict, not a tone issue
records.result: **Location:** §"Hash-chain tamper-evidence and OS-Level Ephemeral Namespaces (OP-9)," line 1393, vs. §"A second transport," lines 819–823, vs. Table `tab:threat-model`, line 1298. **Issue:** This is the most serious individual finding in the review, because it is not an exposition problem — it is two mutually exclusive claims about the same security mechanism, one of which a reader relying on the threat-model table for a go/no-go decision would trust and be wrong to. **Current text** (lines 819–823, §"A second transport"): "We note in \S\ref{sec:threatmodel} that the peer-credential check is a software handshake, not the kernel-enforced socket-level credential check (\texttt{SO\_PEERCRED}) it resembles --- a real trust-boundary caveat." **Current text** (Table `tab:threat-model`, line 1298, row "Different-uid process"): "...but the socket peer-credential check is a software handshake, not the kernel-enforced socket credential (\texttt{SO\_PEERCRED}) --- a real authentication caveat." **Current text** (line 1393, §OP-9, the contradicting claim): "IPC sockets strictly enforce \texttt{SO\_PEERCRED} validation, guaranteeing that the daemon can cryptographically bind incoming requests to a specific, sandboxed spawn instance, making same-user filesystem bypasses impossible." **Proposed rewrite:** This must be resolved as a fact, not just reworded, but the exposition fix is: state explicitly whether OP-9's namespace work *changes* the §5.4/Table~\ref{tab:threat-model} finding. If `SO_PEERCRED` enforcement is now real for the ephemeral-namespace path, say so precisely and narrow the scope: "The default transport's peer-credential check remains a software handshake (§5.4); the OS-Level Ephemeral Namespaces path introduced for OP-9 additionally enforces kernel-level \texttt{SO\_PEERCRED} validation for spawned, sandboxed agent processes specifically — a stronger, narrower guarantee than the general-transport caveat above, not a blanket replacement of it." Then update the threat-model table's "Different-uid process" row to reflect the narrower carve-out, or explicitly note it does not yet apply generally. Do not leave both claims standing unqualified. **Priority:** high. -

records.title: A7. OP-10 (selective checkpointing): claimed solved in prose, still posed as an open design exercise two paragraphs later, and not reflected in the formal Property statement
records.result: **Location:** §4.2, line 596, vs. Property `prop:durability` (§4.1, lines 552–564) vs. exercises box, lines 616–619. **Issue:** *Overclaim that the paper's own formally-stated Property doesn't carry.* Property~\ref{prop:durability} states unconditionally: "\textbf{I1b (power-loss durability).}... \NotGuar{} under the normal synchronization level; it would require full synchronization or a checkpoint on the commit path." Two subsections later, the "would require" is claimed done for a subset of writes — but Property `prop:durability` is never amended, and the exercises box for the exact same section still asks the reader to invent the mechanism just described: **Current text** (line 596): "To solve this (OP-10), the kernel implements \textbf{Selective Checkpointing}. High-stakes, money-bearing writes (like those in the settlement ledger) append \texttt{PRAGMA wal\_checkpoint(FULL);} to their execution paths, forcing a synchronous flush to disk. This achieves power-loss durability (I1b) dynamically without compromising the high-throughput standard paths." **Current text** (line 616): "\textbf{(open, $\bigstar$ OP-10)} Design a per-write-path durability selector: how would the kernel let a settlement-ledger write opt into I1b while keeping claim writes fast? What is the cleanest interface that does not re-introduce the conflation?" **Proposed rewrite:** Add a corollary to Property `prop:durability` naming the exception precisely: "\textbf{Corollary (selective I1b).} A write path may opt into power-loss durability by forcing \texttt{wal\_checkpoint(FULL)} on its commit path, at the cost of that path's throughput; this is applied today to \emph{[name the concrete write paths]}. All other paths remain I1b-\NotGuar{} by Property~\ref{prop:durability}." Then either delete the OP-10 exercise (superseded) or retarget it at the genuinely remaining question, e.g. "what interface prevents a future write path from silently defaulting to the fast, I1b-exposed path when it should have opted in?" **Priority:** high. ---

records.title: A8. OP-2's theorem is proved, then the exact same claim is restated as a still-open exercise
records.result: **Location:** Theorem `thm:decidability` + Remark `rem:controllability-scope`, lines 931–943, vs. §"Formalizing Synchronous State Decidability (OP-2)," lines 1013–1019 (near-duplicate restatement), vs. exercises box, line 1030. **Issue:** *Redundancy plus an unresolved open/closed status.* Lines 1013–1019 restate, in prose, almost exactly what Theorem `thm:decidability` already proved with a proof sketch — a genuine "iff" theorem with citations to Ramadge–Wonham controllability in the remark that follows it. That's a real, closed result. Yet the exercises box for the same material still asks: "\textbf{(open, $\bigstar$ OP-2)} Formalize the regimentation-vs-enforcement boundary: which monitor rules are truly regimentable... versus only enforceable...? A clean theorem here is the deontic heart of the layer." The theorem the exercise asks for already exists two pages earlier. **Proposed rewrite:** Delete §"Formalizing Synchronous State Decidability (OP-2)" (lines 1013–1019) entirely — it adds nothing Theorem `thm:decidability` and Remark `rem:controllability-scope` don't already say, more precisely. Then change the OP-2 exercise from `(open)` to `(check)`: "Theorem~\ref{thm:decidability} settles which monitor rules are regimentable. Classify each of I7–I9's monitor rules (note-monotonicity, capability escalation, lock-owner validity) against it: which are pure functions of committed local state, and which cross the boundary?" Update the master Open Problems list entry (line 1593–1595) the same way. **Priority:** medium. ---

records.title: A9. The Compute-to-Data Airlock section imports cross-machine, cross-operator content into a chapter that explicitly promises not to
records.result: **Location:** §8.5 "Information Flow Control (IFC) and the Compute-to-Data Airlock," lines 1395–1409, vs. the abstract's own scope disclaimer, lines 243–244, and §1's four-layer stack description, lines 267–269. **Issue:** *Scope violation against the paper's own stated contract* — not a wording problem but a structural one. The abstract is explicit: "...cross-machine capability transfer --- which belongs to the cross-machine layer and lives there, not here." Section 1 assigns "the cross-machine market in which operators trade work and reputation" to the Economy chapter, "Treated in an accompanying chapter." Section 8.5 then spends fifteen lines on "Alice license[s] a proprietary agent stack $S$... to execute over Bob's confidential data $D$" — a scenario that is definitionally cross-operator (two different principals, mutual distrust, licensing) — inside the substrate paper's obligation-and-enforcement section, introducing new machinery (a hypervisor, dynamic taint propagation, an LLM-proxy DLP scan, execution-bond slashing) that appears nowhere else in the paper's seven-organ inventory or Table `tab:appendix-map`. **Current text** (line 1401): "To allow Alice to license a proprietary agent stack $S$ (compiled Wasm or opaque container) to execute over Bob's confidential data $D$ without mutual data exfiltration:" **Proposed rewrite:** Either cut §8.5 from this chapter and move it to *The Harbor Economy* (where the abstract already says cross-operator material belongs), replacing it here with a one-paragraph forward pointer ("A companion chapter, *The Harbor Economy*, extends this organ's taint-tagging primitive to a cross-operator compute-to-data airlock — see [chapter reference]"); or, if a same-machine, same-operator version of taint tracking genuinely belongs at the substrate layer, rewrite the scenario to match: two agents under one operator's control, not "Alice licenses to Bob." **Priority:** high. ---

records.title: A10. The controllability Remark is written in the formal paper's register, with no scene and no analogy — and a ready-made one already exists in the companion paper
records.result: **Location:** Remark `rem:controllability-scope`, lines 941–943. **Issue:** *Definitions First* / missing structural analogy (harbor-exposition Move 3). This is the single densest paragraph in the whitepaper and the one furthest from "a smart-but-non-specialist reader": "partition the event alphabet into controllable events $\Sigma_c$... and uncontrollable events $\Sigma_u$... A safety policy is regimentable iff it is \emph{controllable} with respect to $\Sigma_u$ --- no uncontrollable event enabled after a legal prefix can exit the specification." It reads exactly like `docs/harbor-research/tex/paper2.tex` (its formal counterpart — see Part D), which is appropriate for paper2 and not for a whitepaper chapter. Paper2 itself opens with a bouncer/nightclub analogy that maps cleanly onto this exact content: "A door policy (`no entry after 2am') is enforceable by prevention. A thought policy (`no ill intent inside') is enforceable only by observation and ejection" (paper2.tex, lines 51–52). **Current text** (line 941, opening clause): "Theorem~\ref{thm:decidability} is the \emph{operational} form of a more general boundary. In supervisory-control terms (Ramadge--Wonham, 1987), partition the event alphabet into controllable events $\Sigma_c$..." **Proposed rewrite:** Precede the formal remark with a two-sentence scene, reusing the companion paper's analogy so the two chapters reinforce rather than duplicate each other: "Think of the daemon as a bouncer at one door of a club. Turning someone away at the door is prevention --- \emph{regimentable}; noticing bad behavior once someone is already inside and walking them out is detection --- \emph{enforced}. Theorem~\ref{thm:decidability} is the special case where the only door the bouncer stands at is the database commit; a companion formal chapter generalizes the same boundary to every controllable event a runtime can gate, not only writes." Keep the existing formal sentences as the box that follows. **Priority:** medium. ---

records.title: A11. Algorithms are captioned as `Figure`, referenced as `Algorithm`
records.result: **Location:** Algorithm `alg:acquire` (lines 651–674) and `alg:close` (lines 983–1004) — both `\begin{figure}[H]` wrapping an `lstlisting` whose `caption=`/`label=` keys register against the active float, i.e., the `figure` counter, not a dedicated `algorithm` counter. **Issue:** The linter flagged both as "no `\caption`"/"no `\label`" (false positive — see Tooling notes), but its false alarm points at something real: prose calls these "Algorithm~\ref{alg:acquire}" and "Algorithm \ref{alg:close}" (lines 648, 977), but the counter that actually numbers them is `figure`. **[needs render]** to confirm the printed text, but as authored this will very likely print as "Figure 3: Claim acquisition..." with the caption-hyperref target correctly resolving, while the prose sentence around it says "Algorithm 3" — a numbering label mismatch a careful reader (the paper's own target audience, per §"a systems engineer" in the Reader's Map) would notice. **Proposed rewrite:** Either load `algorithm`/`algorithmic` (or the simpler `algorithm2e`) and give these their own float type and counter, or stop calling them "Algorithm" in prose and call them what the counter will print ("Figure~\ref{alg:acquire}"). The former is more in keeping with the paper's rigor elsewhere (Theorem, Lemma, Property, and Definition all have dedicated counters; Algorithm should too). **Priority:** medium — cosmetic today, but a real inconsistency **[needs render to confirm]**. ---

records.title: A12. Alice and Bob are reused across three unrelated scenarios without a beat marking the shift
records.result: **Location:** §5 "Worked dramatization: Alice and Bob race for one port" (lines 684–697); §8.2 "Worked dramatization: Bob attempts a forbidden action" (lines 903–918); §8.5's IFC scenario, "Alice license a proprietary agent stack... to execute over Bob's confidential data" (line 1401). **Issue:** In the first two dramatizations, Alice and Bob are cooperating (or one misbehaving) agents on the *same* machine under the *same* operator — exactly the substrate paper's threat model. By §8.5 they have become two different *operators* who do not trust each other and are licensing proprietary stacks across a trust boundary — a completely different relationship. Reusing the same two names for structurally incompatible roles risks a reader importing the earlier "same-machine, cooperating" mental model into a scenario that is its opposite. (This compounds A9 — if §8.5 moves to the Economy chapter per that recommendation, this issue moves with it and can be fixed by introducing new names appropriate to a cross-operator scenario, e.g. "Acme Corp" and "Bexley Labs.") **Proposed rewrite:** If §8.5 stays, rename its principals (e.g., "a license-holder" and "a data-holder," or new proper names) so "Alice" and "Bob" remain reliably bound to "the two agents on my machine" throughout the chapter. **Priority:** low. ---

records.title: A13. The abstract crams three separable claims into one dense paragraph
records.result: **Location:** Abstract, lines 197–229. **Issue:** The abstract's opening (lines 198–205) is a genuinely good Move-1 scene ("A swarm of autonomous coding agents sharing one machine collides over the same scarce things..."). But from "This paper presents that kernel" onward it runs, unbroken, through the reference-monitor framing, the invariants-as-theorems claim, the durability split, *and* the enforcement correction — five distinct ideas in one 30-line paragraph, harder to skim than the rest of the paper, which is organized with real discipline elsewhere (the Reader's Map exists precisely to help a busy reader avoid reading exactly this kind of block linearly). **Proposed rewrite:** Split after "...realized locally rather than as an abstract security kernel." into two paragraphs: one stating what the kernel *is and proves* (definitions, invariants-as-theorems), a second stating *where the promises stop* (the durability split, the detector/regimenter correction). This mirrors the paper's own two-halves thesis in §1.1 ("Durability... Mediation...") and would let the abstract itself demonstrate the structure it argues for. **Priority:** low. ---

records.title: Part B — Existing figures/tables: clarity audit
records.result: **Cross-cutting finding before the per-figure audit:** the accent pair cobalt/teal is reused across at least five figures with inconsistent, sometimes inverted, meaning. In `fig-swk-reference-monitor.tex` and `fig-swk-deontic-split.tex`, cobalt marks the *stronger* guarantee (regimented, pre-commit) and teal the *weaker* one (enforced/monitor, post-commit). In `fig-swk-durability-faultclass.tex`, the mapping flips: teal marks the guarantee that *holds* (I1a survives) and cobalt the one that *fails* (I1b not guaranteed) — the opposite valence from the first two figures. In `fig-swk-commitment-oracle.tex`, teal is success and cobalt is refusal (matching durability-faultclass's valence, not reference-monitor/deontic-split's). In `fig-swk-dual-runtime.tex`, the same pair means "test" vs. "production," a third, unrelated dimension. A reader who builds a mental color-legend from the first figure they see will misread the others. This is a house-style violation (`high-quality-latex-whitepaper/SKILL.md`, cheap tell #3 and #6) even though each individual figure, read in isolation, is well-crafted. ### B1. `fig-swk-stack-map.tex` — the four-layer stack **What it shows:** Five stacked rungs (economy, legibility, coordination, substrate, machine) with "this paper" flags on the two lowest, and assumes/provides arrows crossing the machine/substrate boundary. **What the reader should take away:** This chapter owns exactly the bottom two layers; everything above is a different chapter's job. **Will they get it?** Yes. Position-on-a-common-scale (Cleveland–McGill's strongest channel) does the work; the cobalt "this paper" flags are a single, correctly-restrained accent use pointing at the one thing that matters on this page. Caption states the finding, not just the parts. **Verdict:** Good, keep. ### B2. `fig-swk-reference-monitor.tex` — the kernel as reference monitor **What it shows:** A request-flow diagram: agent → uniqueness/boot gate → WAL (committed) → operation log, with an explicit "commit line" and a policy-monitor subscriber positioned *downstream* of it, connected by a dashed "compensate" edge back to the WAL. **What the reader should take away:** The policy monitor

records.title: B12. `fig-swk-continuity-organs.tex` — the three continuity organs
records.result: **What it shows:** Three boxes (Memory / Checkpoint / Witnessed-outcome ledger) in a row, each with a status label in a *different* color (teal for "implemented," cobalt for "partial" on Checkpoint, amber for "partial" on Ledger), and a star annotation over Checkpoint calling it "the weakest continuity link." **What the reader should take away:** The whole cross-machine economy rests on these three organs, and the middle one is the weak link. **Will they get it?** The finding lands (the star + caption are effective), but the color choices actively work against the house style: this is the paper's clearest instance of cheap tell #3 ("multi-colored / multi-weight bold... status labels: muted ink/gray, differentiated by weight or small-caps, not by hue") — three different hues for what is really a two-value status set, with the *same* word "partial" rendered in two *different* colors (cobalt for Checkpoint, amber for Ledger) in the same figure. That specifically contradicts the main file's own documented rule (preamble comment, `single-writer-kernel.tex` lines 48–49: "the four grades differ by WEIGHT and SMALL-CAPS / italic, never by hue"). It also, per A3, currently disagrees with the master Open Problems list about whether OP-4/Checkpoint is solved. **Verdict:** Needs fix, on both craft and consistency grounds. **Concrete fix:** replace the three `\color{hhteal}`/`\color{hhcobalt}`/`\color{hhamber}` status labels with the document's own `\Built`/`\BuiltWeak` macros (which the main file already defines as ink/gray, small-caps/weight-differentiated, no hue) — the same technique B8 already uses correctly via border style. Then reconcile the Checkpoint status with A3's resolution. ---

records.title: Part D — Cross-reference notes
records.result: **Chapter-to-paper mapping** (established by grepping, not fully reading, both `paper3.tex` and `paper5.tex`): - **§4 Continuity is a personal-identity problem** (Locke/Parfit, the no-mint theorem status note at lines 695–710) → **paper5**, §"Forks and distillation: reputation you cannot photocopy" (`sec:nomint`). Tight, verified match: the whitepaper's numbers (4,000 fork DAGs, 0 violations, the refuted budget-only chain $0.9+0.81+0.729=2.44>1$, the 2-op mint crime, the 8.2× multiplier from an 8-way copy-fork) are identical to paper5's Theorem 1 and its "wrong turn, reported" box, down to the seed and script name (`a6_no_mint.py`). No drift. - **§5 The three organs of continuity** → **paper5**, §"Resurrection with teeth" (`sec:resurrection`), *for the reputation-correctness half only*. Paper5's Theorem 3 (resurrection soundness) is genuinely about whether sanctions/scores survive provider migration — a ledger-correctness property — and its own Honest Boundary explicitly refuses the claim that a checkpoint "restored the agent's experience." records.title: Thm 1.8.3 (regimentation is controllability) assumes full observability and omits the Lin–Wonham observability condition from its statement; §1.8.4 discusses it
records.result: Thm 1.8.3 (regimentation is controllability) assumes full observability and omits the Lin–Wonham observability condition from its statement; §1.8.4 discusses it only informally. | The statement is under full observation without saying so. The subsubsection *Partial observation: the second boundary* (`whitepaper/single-writer-kernel.tex:1393–1410`, §1.8.3, lb p. 47) states the Lin–Wonham condition in prose ("controllability *plus* observability: the supervisor's decisions must be constant on observation-equivalence classes"), and boundary (iv) after the theorem names it ("Full observation is the assumption this classification rests on", lb p. 48). `b3_controllability.py` checks controllability only. | **ACCEPT-IN-PART** | *Statement*: add the hypothesis $\Sigma_o=\Sigma$ to Thm 1.8.3 and state the refinement as a numbered Proposition: with projection $P:\Sigma^*\to\Sigma_o^*$, a regimentation mechanism exists iff $K$ is controllable and observable, where observable means for all $s,s'\in\overline K$ with $P(s)=P(s')$ and $\sigma\in\Sigma_c$: $s\sigma\in\overline K \wedge s'\sigma\in\overline L \Rightarrow s'\sigma\in\overline K$ (Lin–Wonham 1988, already `\cite{lw88}`). *Left*: the charge that the assumption is omitted; it is stated twice, one paragraph and one page after the box. records.title: Thm 1.11.2 (linearizability) needs `fsync` and monotonic host-clock synchronization as hypotheses, because event loops reorder requests and `synchronous=NORMAL`
records.result: Thm 1.11.2 (linearizability) needs `fsync` and monotonic host-clock synchronization as hypotheses, because event loops reorder requests and `synchronous=NORMAL` lets committed transactions roll back on power loss. | The statement's hypotheses are the single-writer discipline, no `read_uncommitted`, response only after commit, no out-of-band writer (§1.11, lb p. 60). Durability is typed by fault class in §1.5 (`single-writer-kernel.tex:522, 648, 680`; `synchronous=NORMAL`; `POWER_LOSS` writes routed to `synchronous=FULL`, OP-10), and I1b "power-loss durability on any write path" is listed as *not provided* (`:2249`). The theorem is silent about histories that span a crash. | **ACCEPT-IN-PART** | *Statement*: add "in crash-free executions, or for operations routed at `synchronous=FULL`"; name the crash-spanning property as *durable linearizability* (Izraelevitz, Mendes, Scott, DISC 2016) and say it holds only on the FULL path — under NORMAL a history across a power loss can carry a response whose effect is gone, which is a durability failure, not a reordering. *Refuted within the row*: (a) no clock appears in the proof; Herlihy–Wing real time is the one daemon's own invocation/response order; (b) a request the event loop reorders before it reaches the daemon has no response yet, so it overlaps, and overlapping operations may be ordered either way — the proof already says so. *Verify*: the consistency-model figure (`figures/fig-swk-consistency-model.tex`) gains the fifth assumption; OP-10's row cross-references it.
assumptions: Adjudication is dated 2026-09-08; its receipt is not current proof.

records.title: Thm 4.4.1 ($M/M/c$ specialization boundary) assumes stationary Poisson arrivals and exponential service; agent workloads are heavy-tailed and bursty; qualify wi
records.result: Thm 4.4.1 ($M/M/c$ specialization boundary) assumes stationary Poisson arrivals and exponential service; agent workloads are heavy-tailed and bursty; qualify with an $M/G/1$ Pollaczek–Khinchine expansion. | The setup names Poisson arrivals, exponential service, FCFS, mean cost (`whitepaper/legible-swarm.tex`, the "queueing-specialization setup" paragraph before Thm 4.4.1, §4.4). Nothing in ch. 4 discusses service-time variance (no hit for heavy-tail, Pareto, Kingman, $M/G$). | **ACCEPT-IN-PART** | *Boundary*, not statement: the theorem is exact inside its named model. Add a boundary paragraph: under the Allen–Cunneen heuristic $W_q^{M/G/c}\approx W_q^{M/M/c}\,(c_a^2+c_s^2)/2$ and Pollaczek–Khinchine for the specialist, service-time variance scales both *waiting* components by about the same factor $\kappa=(1+c_s^2)/2$, so to first order the boundary $g$ moves little while the accountability term enters as $A/\kappa$: variance makes single-writer attribution weigh *less* against queueing, not more. *Left*: a $M/G/1$ expansion for the $c$-server pool — $M/G/c$ has no closed form and the review's tool is the single-server one. *New*: the robustness statement is an Empirical hypothesis; extend `b8_specialization.py` with lognormal and Pareto service and report where the crossing moves (falsifier: further than the heuristic predicts); Trial Basin scenario when 3.1 exists.

records.title: Thm 5.6.3 (probation cliff) ignores capital constraints: a front-loaded penalty is a liquidity barrier that excludes honest but capital-poor entrants while well
records.result: Thm 5.6.3 (probation cliff) ignores capital constraints: a front-loaded penalty is a liquidity barrier that excludes honest but capital-poor entrants while well-capitalized attackers absorb it. | $g_t$ is a holdback on the newcomer's *earning ceiling*, not a posted bond ("the amount by which a newcomer's economic ceiling is reduced", statement, lb p. 244); nothing is posted. The statement carries the cap $0\le g_t\le L$ and the infeasibility $G_{\max}>L/(1-\delta_f)$ "as part of the statement, not footnotes to it" — which is the well-capitalized attacker: deterrence is bounded by what a ceiling can withhold. | **ACCEPT-IN-PART** | *Refuted*: the liquidity reading of the instrument. *Taken*: an honest entrant with an outside option $u$ per period participates only if $\sum_t\delta_h^t(\pi_t-g_t)\ge\sum_t\delta_h^t u$; the cliff maximises period-0 friction, so an income floor binds first at $t=0$ and the optimum becomes fill-from-zero up to $\min(L,\pi_0-u)$ — a one-line corollary under the theorem, with adverse selection of the entrant mix as the named falsifier. *Verify*: `b6_probation.py` sweep with a floor; Trial Basin newcomer-mix scenario.

records.title: Thm 5.11.1 (tower contraction) assumes independent auditor failures; model monocultures correlate errors; add a diversity index to the contraction factor.
records.result: Thm 5.11.1 (tower contraction) assumes independent auditor failures; model monocultures correlate errors; add a diversity index to the contraction factor. | The clique count $C$ *is* the diversity parameter (statement, lb p. 266: "a pool spanning $C$ disjoint cliques"; the worked numbers contrast $C=8$ with a monoculture $C=1$), and boundary (iii) says cross-clique correlation is "a measurement obligation on deployed judge telemetry … not an assumption" (`spawn-to-person.tex:2158–2161`). | **ACCEPT-IN-PART** | The parameter exists; what is missing is one symbol shared with ch. 6's Purchased Assurance Bound (CA-041). Give correlation a model in both places: with a per-panel detection rate $D$ drawn from a mixing distribution of mean $d$, $\Pr(\text{all }k\text{ miss})=\mathbb E[(1-D)^k]\ge(1-d)^k$ by Jensen; under $D\sim\mathrm{Beta}(a,b)$ with $\rho=1/(a+b+1)$ the closed form is $B(a,b+k)/B(a,b)$. *Left*: the review's $k_{\text{eff}}=k/(1+(k-1)\rho)$ — it is the design effect for the variance of a mean, exact for this quantity only at $\rho\in\{0,1\}$, and derived from no model in between.

records.result: Thm 6.7.1 asserts functorial conservation $\Delta(g\circ f)=\Delta(g)+\Delta(f)$ across heterogeneous currencies; this breaks under floating rates; restrict to a fixed numéraire or add priced slippage. | The theorem is titled *Single-unit conservation composes* and its first hypothesis is "all harbors use one unit of account" (`harbor-economy.tex:1087`, lb p. 301). A scalar portfolio total additionally requires a valuation map $v_t$ at a named instant $t$, plus explicit fee and slippage accounts. records.result: Maturity grades mean different things per chapter ("Built" is TypeScript in ch. 1, Kani-verified Rust in ch. 2, Python scripts in ch. 6, TLA⁺ in ch. 7); adopt a five-tier Artifact Assurance Register: mechanized proof, conformance-tested implementation, bounded verification, paper proof, conjecture. | The maturity macros are one vocabulary already (`\Built`=implemented, `\BuiltWeak`=partial, `\Designed`=specified, `\Vision`=proposed; `coordination-papers-mega-volume-preamble.tex:218–221`), and ch. 6's `\Built` grades the bond-ledger *module*, shipped code (`harbor-economy.tex:676`), not a script. records.title: OP-12 (new)
records.result: OP-12 (new) | Sheaf-Laplacian diffusion versus epidemic gossip is unresolved in §8.5.4 and admitted in §8.12; formalise as OP-12. | The Book states it plainly, and states why the two are different objects: "The Hansen–Ghrist rate governs continuous-time linear diffusion … anti-entropy gossip over signed append-only logs with a Byzantine equivocator is discrete, asynchronous, adversarial, and monotone-join … The two convergence stories … are not reconciled, and neither is a second proof of the other" (`federated-harbor-whitepaper.tex`, *Sheaf Laplacian dynamics — and what is not claimed here*, lb p. 424). | **ACCEPT-IN-PART** | Not as ch. 1's OP-12: that numbering is the kernel's namespace and other chapters deliberately do not extend it (`spawn-to-person.tex:2960`). As a ch. 8 §8.12 open question with a falsifier, and sharper than the review's: Thm 8.5.2 detects only when the lie's endpoints' reports have been *relayed*, and relay is the gossip of §8.5.1, so time-to-detection is a function of rounds — after $t$ rounds, which visible cycles are closed, hence $\Pr(\text{detect}\mid e)$ against $t$; the relation to $\lambda_2$ is a conjecture to be swept, not a bound. Beside plan §7 (origination of unowned work) it sits only in method — both are time-to-$X$ measurements in the Trial Basin — not in substance; do not merge them.

records.result:
Current reconciliation: the seven named mathematical/scope conflicts have source patches and bounded checks. Chapters 5, 6 and 8 now develop safe continuation, finite reachable-family admission and least-cost categorical certificates. The rebuilt 592-page Book has been inspected at the changed claims; the source/PDF hashes and exact text searches are recorded in PROGRAM-RECONCILIATION. Hosted checks remain pending. Remaining research imports retain their open status. The assessment below is the hash-bound audit snapshot; its findings are superseded only by explicit resolutions.

The research already supplies much of the Book's formal backbone. The largest remaining value is to make evidence conditions operational, repair inconsistent statements, and carry source claims into the actual publication artifact.

#### Scope and defensible coverage

The authoritative corpus is the eight chapters selected by `whitepaper/textbook.json`. The Swiss, maritime and technical roots use the same generated chapter body, so they are three presentations of one argument. This assessment covers those sources and the checked-in 589-page public Book PDF; it does not certify an external worktree or a deployed website.

All 17 R1–R17 index entries name a chapter. Of 34 total indexed entries, 20 have chapter locators and 14 Paper 8 entries have none. These are structural counts, not percentages of scientific correctness or pedagogical adoption. In particular, R17 and CR are marked `standalone-only` while also having chapter locations; the inspected chapter text takes precedence over that status field. The core is frequently developed through statements, proofs, examples and exercises, rather than merely cited. Paper 8's typed two-complex, relative extension and report-error distance remain substantial opportunities.

#### Chapter-by-chapter assessment

| Chapter | What is actually incorporated | What importing more research would let the reader do |
|---|---|---|
| 1. The Single-Writer Kernel | Strong: controllability, partial observation, work-unit invariants and mutation witnesses (R5, R8). | Turn incomplete observations into an adapter-specific safe-action rule; connect the unknown-effect warning to a worked retry/refusal case. |
| 2. The Anchor Protocol | Applies the control boundary to capability admission; its own attenuation proof estate also lies outside R1–R17. | Bind admission to the exact evidence snapshot and current authority epoch; show why an authentic claim can still be stale or insufficient. |
| 3. The Sealed Harbor | Strong: finite noninterference, atomic privacy-budget accounting, canary power and sequential detection (R9–R11). | Import the explicit payload-release factorization test; a small output alphabet alone does not establish release of the permitted information. |
| 4. The Legible Swarm | Extensive: digest floors, split preferences, decision loss, zoom, escalation, specialization and paging (R1–R4, R14–R16); several statements need correction. | Correct formula/hypothesis mismatches first; then teach witness-preserving summaries and complementary evidence acquisition under a human inspection budget. |
| 5. From Spawn to Person | Strong: no-mint transfer, engine substitution, migration, probation and inspection incentives (R7, R12, R13, B6). | Separate liability continuity from safe execution continuity; give an adapter table for atomic dedup/result, fenced readback, and unresolved remote effects. |
| 6. The Harbor Economy | Strong: specialization/succession and a tractable deontic fragment (R15, R17). | Add future-fact admission conditions and distinguish deciding existence of conflict from enumerating every witness; the latter must pay for output size. |
| 7. The Bonded Commons | Substantial institutional and settlement proof content; inspection-game calibration and evidence selection are only partially connected. | Derive an audit rate from the stated gain, detection and penalty model; choose cheap checkable dispute certificates without calling known-answer selection an optimal query policy. |
| 8. The Federated Harbor | Current source substantially incorporates Paper 7: visibility, sender blind spots, residual scope, robustness and marginal receipt value. Typed Paper 8 constructions and exact categorical certificates are not developed. | Add a typed worked example, exact categorical contradictions, partial-section extension and edge-group error distance; use them to design observations for a declared fault model. |

#### Corrections before expansion

1. **Decision odds, Chapter 4 / Paper 1.** The displayed expected-cost rule is `Cmiss*a >= catt + Cfa*(1-a)`. When `Cmiss > catt`, its odds denominator is `Cmiss-catt`, not `Cmiss`. At `Cmiss=10, catt=1, Cfa=1, a=0.17`, passing costs 1.70 and inspecting costs 1.83, but the printed odds rule orders inspection. Handle equality and degenerate costs explicitly rather than dividing through a nonpositive denominator. Source: `legible-swarm.tex` lines 2205–2226; `paper1.tex` lines 125–136.
2. **Strict zoom savings, Chapter 4 / Paper 1.** The displayed guaranteed-advantage expression equals one at density `d=1/12`. Strict improvement requires `d<1/12`, hence `f>12(p-delta)` for the stated composition; equality is break-even for that bound. Sources: Chapter 4 lines 1800–1888 and Paper 1 lines 214–228.
3. **Split-floor reasoning, Chapter 4 / Paper 1.** The shared-budget inequality survives, but the numerator-only binomial-growth explanation is false. Use the increasing summands of `F(t)=sum(i=0..t-1) log2((N-i)/(m-i))` for `2k<=m<N`. Do not infer that separate model processes or separate stored representations are necessary from a result about incompatible scalar orderings. Source: Chapter 4 lines 2447–2459; ledger `P1-SPLIT-CORRECTION`.
4. **Escalation hypotheses, Chapter 4.** Nondecreasing benefit and monotone validation do not imply a strictly increasing payoff or a unique exact root. For example, constant `b=V=1/2` and `delta*w=1` give zero payoff everywhere. Continuity, strictness, endpoint conditions and tie policy must match the claimed threshold theorem. Source: lines 1192–1211.
5. **Paging contract, Chapter 4.** The theorem uses `h` as pinned-set size while the detailed research bound uses `h` for offline comparator capacity and `p` for pins. A guarantee for the specified Landlord algorithm does not certify arbitrary recency-plus-pin policies. Align algorithm, comparator, pins and repair-on-touch assumptions before presenting the bound as one theorem. Source: lines 2514–2552 and `b9_context_paging.py` lines 17–32.
6. **Conflict enumeration, Chapter 6.** The every-witness interval bound omits emitted output. One scope with `n` obligations and `n` prohibitions yields `n^2` distinct clashes. Separate a yes/no or first-witness interface from full enumeration and include output cost. Source: `harbor-economy.tex` lines 786–800; ledger `P6-OUTPUT`.
7. **Continuity claim, Chapter 5.** Behavioral-equivalence language for replay outruns the nearby unmeasured-fidelity qualification. Score/obligation preservation does not establish correct state restoration or absence of duplicate external effects. Source: `spawn-to-person.tex` lines 844–905 and 1575–1638.

#### Publication artifact gap

The checked-in Book PDF, physical pages 459–461 (printed pages 441–443), asserts a `313/1101` pairwise-blind advantage and describes minimum adversary perturbation achievability too broadly. The current Chapter 8 source, lines 512–539 and 590–614, instead states zero residual-only and 209 direct-only cases under the equal-information synthetic comparison, and limits achievability to unrestricted edge-data correction. Those are different mathematical claims. Source incorporation therefore cannot be reported as PDF incorporation. Rebuild and inspect the Book after the scientific edits, then verify the same statements in each intended publication edition. No PDF was regenerated as part of this assessment.

#### Highest-value imports and their boundaries

- **Safe continuation (Chapters 1 and 5; `UNKNOWN-EFFECT`).** Give a decision table for retry, readback and refusal. A negative read does not justify retry while an earlier remote operation can still arrive. The finite one-operation/two-epoch model supports a bounded worked example; concurrent operations, retention windows and a real adapter require more work.
- **Future-safe commitment admission (Chapters 1 and 6; `FUTURE-HORN`).** Show a conflict that is dormant at admission and activated by a permitted fact. A greatest-future-fact closure is exact under fixed positive rules and a jointly reachable maximum. Mutually exclusive futures require reachable-state reasoning; their union can conservatively reject a policy that is safe in every reachable state.
- **Payload-aware release (Chapter 3; `RELEASE-FACTORIZATION`).** Teach the deterministic condition that the composed release must factor through the declared permitted observation. Then extend the model to submitted values, refusals, timing and adaptive traces before claiming a complete secrecy theorem.
- **Exact evidence certificates (Chapters 4, 7 and 8; `CLAIM-EXACT`, `CLAIM-COST`).** For registered categorical facts, test feasibility before a real-valued residual. A contradictory path can have zero linear residual. Two incompatible pins plus a zero-equality path give a checkable certificate; optimize its cost among known observations. Authentication, fixed fact/schema/snapshot and missingness are admission requirements.
- **Topology as an observation-design rule (Chapter 8; `P8-T3`, `P8-T4`, `P8-T6`).** Work through heterogeneous stalks and restriction maps, then show what declared redundancy buys: group distance greater than `k` detects every nonzero `k`-group error, and distance greater than `2k` identifies every such error modulo compatible data. In the graph model the latter is `lambda(G)>2k`. This concerns edge-report errors, not the identity or intention of an agent. Relative obstruction addresses extension of a visible compatible section; zero obstruction gives possible extension, not truth of unseen data. Adding a face without an independent observation does not add detection information.
- **Evidence acquisition (Chapters 4, 7 and 8; `P7-BUNDLES`, `NEXT-P7`).** Use two individually uninformative receipts whose combination resolves a question. This refutes zero-one-step-gain stopping. An optimal adaptive policy still needs answer distributions or an adversarial objective, prices, privacy constraints and stopping loss; the known-answer certificate optimizer does not supply it.
- **Calibrated institutional audit (Chapters 5 and 7; `R7`, `REVIEW-PILOT`).** Tie a rate and bond to an explicit gain, detection and slash convention. The chapter's 10% human-audit example is not itself a deterrence calculation. Correlated reviewers and wrongful penalties need measured, equal-budget cases; the prepared review protocol is not a completed experiment.

The main text should teach these as a small set of worked decisions, with exact hypotheses and witnesses beside each claim. Full algebra and exhaustive fixtures can sit in the research papers or appendices. Mathematical examples can be incorporated once their statements and independent checks agree; deployment and comparative-utility claims additionally require authenticated traces, adapter conformance and matched-information baselines.

deepDives.oneLine: Kofman and Lawarrée leave the unbounded-collateral regress as an open question in their conclusion, almost word for word the question the tower theorem answers, which makes them a supporting citation rather than a competitor. The same pass caught an arithmetic slip in the paper's own C=1 counter-case and fixed it.

The rumoured same-year preprint turned out to be real but orthogonal; the prior work that actually mattered was Basin et al. (TISSEC 2013), which nobody had flagged. Two correctness bugs against Schneider's theorem were found and fixed along the way, and the Ramadge–Wonham identification (the paper's real contribution) survived.

The tractable-then-NP-complete shape was already mapped by the compliance-checking literature, so the framing had to narrow; the specific fragment, and conflict-freedom rather than compliance as the decision problem, survive as novel. An iff with the wrong strictness had been stated three different ways across four sites, and was unified.

The citation the sweep had flagged as fabricated is real (just irrelevant), so it was excluded on relevance rather than fraud. The genuine omission was the combinatorial-topology canon: Herlihy–Shavit and three foundational citations were added to close it.

Each of the four pillars narrows to a known result (delimited release, a privacy filter) that the paper mostly concedes up front; one corollary had leaned on a composition bound that doesn't hold in its setting and was rewritten to the model where it does.

No prior work proves the theorems, but Theorem 2a is Akerlof's lemons result wearing the wrong name (it had been called the unraveling theorem) and was renamed, and a crossing value that the paper's own figure contradicted was corrected.

The typed cellular-sheaf theorems and exact fixture are sound within the declared model; mathematical foundations are established, and field utility depends on authenticated evidence and an equal-information direct-check comparison.

wrongTurns.lesson: The meter was charging bits for tie-breaking as well as identification, which manufactured 8 spurious floor violations out of 14 and briefly looked like a refutation of the theorem. The corrected experiment is the one the paper cites.

Zoom was tested in the dense-flag regime, which is exactly where it can't help, and duly showed a 0.5× "advantage" that meant nothing. The frontier only exists where flags are sparse, and the experiment now says so.

Computed the dimension of the abstract sheaf's first cohomology, a number that doesn't depend on the data at all, when the quantity that detects a lie is the obstruction of the particular observed assignment.

A vector-stalk wrapper whose random restriction maps were surjective (so the cokernel was always zero), on top of inconsistent masking and the wrong partition detector. Thrown out and rebuilt from a minimal proof of the mechanism.

studies.title: Is the single-writer rail the right collaboration model, and is the enforcement point below the agent the right substrate?
studies.question: The kernel chapter argues that confinement needs an enforcement point below the agent, and that much is a theorem. What it doesn't know is whether the single-writer rail is also the right way for several agents to share one repository, compared with a worktree per agent and a merge queue, which is what most of the industry does. Until this study reports, the rail is a design invariant and nothing stronger.
studies.design: Real commit histories from three public repositories, replayed through six coordination substrates (an uncoordinated shared tree; advisory claims with a bypass rate; the enforced rail; a worktree per agent with a merge queue; and the rail with region-level claims) at 2, 4, 8, and 16 agents, with cooperative and impatient temperaments and twenty seeds per cell. The five metrics were fixed before the first run, so none could be added after the data came in.

hypotheses.title: Confinement
hypotheses.statement: Torn-tree incidents under advisory claims grow with the bypass rate, the agent count, and file overlap, and are zero under every enforced substrate. This one is the self-check: if it fails for the rail, the harness is broken, and we fix the harness before believing anything else it says.

hypotheses.title: The real question
hypotheses.statement: At low overlap the merge queue matches or beats the rail on throughput and time to land. At high overlap the rail beats the merge queue on wasted work by at least a factor of two and matches it on throughput within 20%. If the merge queue matches or beats the rail on every metric in every high-overlap cell, the book demotes the rail to a confinement mechanism.

hypotheses.title: Enforcement, or only confinement
hypotheses.statement: The shim used exactly as designed and the enforced rail are indistinguishable on every coordination metric. If that holds, the case for the enforcement point rests on confinement alone, and the book has to say so plainly.

hypotheses.title: Granularity
hypotheses.statement: Region claims recover at least half of the rail's throughput deficit against the merge queue at high overlap, where a deficit exists.

studies.notRunnableHere: S1, the substrate cost and controllability table (bare process, seccomp and Landlock, gVisor, Firecracker), needs KVM or unprivileged user namespaces, which the build container doesn't have, so it runs on the author's machine.
studies.reportRule: One report, whatever the outcome. If H2's kill condition holds, the report says so in its first sentence, and the kernel chapter and the front matter are amended in the same pull request rather than in some later one. Numbers reach the book with the verified tag only once the pinned corpora and seeds regenerate them.

plannedLifts.title: Lift the work-unit machine to TLA+ and Apalache
plannedLifts.statement: The 536-state work-unit machine is checked exhaustively today by a Python model each of whose guards is proven necessary by mutation, which is real evidence but not the same kind as the rest of the estate. The lift restates it in TLA+ and checks it with Apalache, so the kernel's invariants sit in the same checker as the relay's and the ledger's.

plannedLifts.title: Lift sealed-room noninterference to Isabelle
plannedLifts.statement: Noninterference holds under every interleaving to depth seven in the finite model, and depth seven is where the model checker stops, not where the property does. The unbounded statement is an unwinding argument, and the lift is to state it in Isabelle against the Archive of Formal Proofs' noninterference library.

plannedLifts.title: Discharge the three admitted steps in the Merkle binding proof
plannedLifts.statement: The bond ledger's Merkle binding is sketched in EasyCrypt with three admitted tactics, and EasyCrypt doesn't run in CI, so right now this is a proof outline that a person reviewed rather than a proof a machine checked. The manifest grades it partial until the admits are discharged and the tool is pinned.

plannedLifts.title: The minimum viable take-rate
plannedLifts.statement: The economy chapter prices the three-sided market on one conserving ledger, but it doesn't yet derive the smallest platform take that keeps that market open, and that number is the one a pricing page would eventually have to cite.

openProblems.title: Authority transfer between harbors
openProblems.statement: Writer epochs appear in the book only as a revocation mechanism. There is no written procedure for freezing a harbor's authority, exporting it, importing it under verification, activating the new epoch, and rolling back by epoch, and the Chartroom cutover decision can't be graded until there is. Of the silences, this is the one we'd fix first.

openProblems.title: The release ledger in the other direction
openProblems.statement: The release ledger meters the customer's data leaving the sealed room. A provider's implementation leaking out through the customer's queries is the same ledger with the roles swapped, and nobody has written it down yet, so no claim about protecting provider IP can be graded until someone does.

openProblems.title: Dispute windows, partial work, and refunds
openProblems.statement: The Bonded Commons gives you conservation and two-of-three settlement, and the economy chapter gives you prices, but neither says anything about the time and arithmetic of a dispute: how long the window stays open, what a half-delivered work order is worth, and how a refund conserves.

openProblems.title: A constitution for the registry
openProblems.statement: Who may suspend a publisher, under what review, and with what appeal. The book has the bond and the audit worked out; the emergency path, the one you need on the bad day, isn't written.

openProblems.title: One label scheme for product, roadmap, and book
openProblems.statement: The product's five evidence labels, the book's five assurance modes, and its four statement kinds ought to be one table, so that a product badge, a roadmap item, and a chapter claim all speak the same words and nobody has to translate between them.

openProblems.title: Equivocation by a coalition on a cycle
openProblems.statement: The consistency radius certifies a lower bound on any single equivocator's lie, but two liars placed on the same cycle can cancel each other to a residual of zero (measured at 6×10⁻¹⁵, which is to say exactly zero up to floating point). Catching coordinated equivocation needs a different invariant, and we don't have it.

openProblems.title: Context paging against an adaptive pin adversary
openProblems.statement: The paging bound holds against a pin oracle corrupted at a fixed rate, with repair on touch. An adversary that adapts its corruptions to the operator's access pattern is strictly stronger than the greedy one the proof assumes, and nobody has tested against it.

openProblems.title: An incremental conflict checker for the tractable fragment
openProblems.statement: Conflict-freedom inside the tractable fragment is decided in polynomial time, with a witness, from scratch every time. An amortized checker that updates the witness as a single policy changes is stated in the paper and hasn't been built.

openProblems.title: Origination of unowned work
openProblems.statement: Every mechanism the book has -- receipts, bonds, escrow, reputation as a ledger position, the deterrence and discount thresholds -- binds an agent to something it agreed to do. A dead daemon or a red test has no counterparty and no price, and nothing in the institution assigns a defect nobody chartered; Ostrom's monitoring and graduated sanctions presuppose a promise to monitor against. Four parts: what mechanism makes an unowned defect somebody's and prices it (a bounty on the commons' own invariants, a rotation, an obligation attached to proximity, a market in noticing); how variable agent lifetimes change the answer, since a worker alive only for one pull request values nothing after it and the reviewers who check it face the same question one level up; who remembers old plans and old ideas, and whether memory induction into standing orders is measurable; and whether this is solved by a market in which agents that do the thing better win the work, or requires evaluators who give feedback immediately and in aggregate, or both, with the boundary between them unwritten.

openProblems.title: Policy control when gate triggers are only partly observed
openProblems.statement: Paper 2 proves a fully observed controllability boundary but leaves the real observation-tier map open. For a finite policy and event model, enumerate which histories each assurance tier can distinguish; test whether indistinguishable histories demand the same gate decision. Compare the resulting implementable policies with the fully observed checker before making any runtime guarantee.

openProblems.title: Inspection towers with partial sampler leakage and dependent cliques
openProblems.statement: Paper 3 gives sealed and fully revealed draw endpoints, while its clique multiplier assumes independent pools. Derive the bribery threshold when a draw leaks with probability q or clique outcomes are correlated, and compare a finite exact game with the sealed and revealed formulas. Treat leakage and correlation rates as model parameters until measured from a real audit system.

openProblems.title: Canary detection under correlated misses and adaptive discovery
openProblems.statement: Paper 4 quotes detection power 1-beta^k under independent canary misses and names secrecy as critical. Hold each canary's marginal miss rate fixed while varying shared failure and adaptive canary discovery; compare exact or simulated power with the independent curve and state when a target power fails. Field power still needs measured suppressor behavior.

openProblems.title: Typed sheaf evidence auditing against equal-information baselines
openProblems.statement: Test provenance-bound typed vertex, edge, and face receipts from real workflows at a fixed schema and watermark. Predeclare face violations, closed handoff obstructions, relative extension failures, sparse packet faults, and coherent false reports with independent ledger truth. Compare full sheaf certificates with the strongest exact direct-contract solver given the same receipts, reporting detection, ambiguity, false alarms, explanation quality, acquisition cost, and privacy cost. When raw endpoint claims are visible, direct duplicate checks already dominate graph-cycle detection. Reassess Paper 7's beyond-pairwise claim under the same-information baseline. Prefer direct checks if cohomological certificates bring no measured benefit.

critique_rows.Section / page: Correctness audit #1: Chapter I -- Signal Detection Theory points the wrong way (p.10)
critique_rows.Item: The diagram defines danger as increasing rightward yet 'zoom if evidence exceeds beta,' so moving the criterion left is more stringent, not laxer as the prose claims; the objective may also double-count attention if C_fa already includes wasted inspection.

critique_rows.Section / page: Correctness audit #2: Chapter I -- roadmap-as-truth repeats the Scott failure (p.10)
critique_rows.Item: A roadmap is an authoritative statement of intent/priority/dependency, not truth about the world; calling it truth turns learning into drift. Make it a versioned, amendable projection reconciled and compiled by an owner, not editable-as-reality.
critique_rows.Notes: sec:roadmap (l.929-937) is still titled 'Roadmap-as-truth' and frames legitimacy as 'whether the roadmap stays true'; not reframed as an amendable intent-projection per the critique.; sec:roadmap is retitled and reframed: a versioned, amendable statement of intent whose legitimacy is honesty, not truth about the world; the status-table row follows

critique_rows.Section / page: Correctness audit #3: Chapter II -- exact-key uniqueness is not mutual exclusion (p.10)
critique_rows.Item: The mutual-exclusion theorem proves at most one live row per exact normalized key; it says nothing about overlapping ranges or hierarchical resources, and needs canonical conflict classes or a transactional overlap predicate plus a fencing epoch.
critique_rows.Prior adjudication: RT Change 2 states the same correction and adds the fencing-epoch requirement.
critique_rows.Notes: Fencing epoch and the canonical conflict-domain predicate are in `whitepaper/single-writer-kernel.tex` (the mutual-exclusion theorem and its proof, checked inside one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`).

critique_rows.Section / page: Correctness audit #4: Chapter II -- WAL auto-checkpoint does not bound elapsed loss time (p.10-11)
critique_rows.Item: SQLite's WAL auto-checkpoint is a page threshold, not a timer, so it cannot bound the elapsed vulnerability window; durability must be typed by fault class and given synchronous=FULL for money/authority writes.
critique_rows.Prior adjudication: RT Change 7(b) is the identical correction.
critique_rows.Notes: Durability is typed by fault class in `whitepaper/single-writer-kernel.tex` (Selective Checkpointing, OP-10: NORMAL for ephemeral claims, `synchronous=FULL` before returning on money/authority writes).

critique_rows.Notes: The five assurance modes (Observed/Coordinated/Brokered/Confined/Attested) are defined in `whitepaper/figures/pd-pedagogy.tex` and used throughout `whitepaper/single-writer-kernel.tex` in place of 'reference monitor'.

critique_rows.Section / page: Correctness audit #6: Chapter III -- the nonforgeable-identity theorem is false as stated (p.11)

critique_rows.Section / page: Correctness audit #8: Chapter V -- attenuation must compare every edge, not every node to the root (p.12)
critique_rows.Item: The main Anchor algorithm compares each capability to the root, admitting write->read->write escalation; each hop must be checked against its immediate parent, and the Kani harnesses need a relational proof over symbolic parent/child capabilities, not two concrete vectors.

critique_rows.Section / page: Correctness audit #9: Chapter VI -- the game matrix and repeated-game bound are wrong (p.12)
critique_rows.Item: For the displayed payoffs A prefers T against F (1>0), so F is not dominant and (F,F) is not Nash; the repeated-game deviation is profitable whenever delta<1/3, not the printed threshold; recommends modeling this as a hidden-type reporting game, not an observed Prisoner's Dilemma.
critique_rows.Prior adjudication: RT Change 1 states the identical matrix correction and threshold re-derivation.
critique_rows.Notes: `website-v2/public/whitepaper/agent-transactions-whitepaper.tex` §sec:economic already prints a genuine Prisoner's Dilemma (F strictly dominates T, 4>3 and 1>0) with the corrected threshold delta>=1/3 (grim) / delta*~=0.342 (graduated), mechanized in `proofs/economics/claim_signaling.tla` and `proofs/economics/delta-threshold.z3`.

critique_rows.Section / page: Correctness audit #10: Chapter VII -- cross-harbor resource substitution is a new grant (p.12)

critique_rows.Item: The stage-game table is not a Prisoner's Dilemma: A prefers F against T (4>3) but T against F (1>0); (F,F) is not Nash; the delta~=0.253 claim-signaling proposition does not establish the stated equilibrium for this game.

critique_rows.Section / page: Exercise key VI.C E1 -- Advisory claims (p.31)
critique_rows.Item: An advisory claim is strictly more permissive than an enforced lock (admits intentional-conflict/override traces on top of every enforced-lock trace); Sen's cost-of-decisive-rights analogy is not a theorem that locks are impossible or permissiveness always desirable.
critique_rows.Notes: ex:bonded-advisory-claims solution (703): advisory strictly more permissive than a lock, "feature" framing tied to Theorem prop:sen.

critique_rows.Section / page: Exercise key VI.C E2 -- Reputation instead of bonds (p.31)
critique_rows.Item: Reputation compensates nobody for a first/final harm and can be whitewashed via cheap identities; a pre-funded performance bond creates recoverable value before authority is granted and keys exposure to the durable principal.
critique_rows.Notes: ex:bonded-reputation-vs-bonds solution (772): compensates nobody, whitewash via fresh IDs, bond keys to durable principal.

critique_rows.Section / page: Exercise key VI.C E3 -- Magic-link ProVerif model (p.31)
critique_rows.Item: Specifies the ProVerif model needed (fresh token, issuance event, atomic consume, recovery-key rotation) and the properties to prove (token secrecy, injective authentication, at-most-once consumption), noting ProVerif has no built-in wall-clock semantics.
critique_rows.Notes: ex:bonded-magic-link-proverif (1621-1627): fresh token/injective auth/atomic consume; "ProVerif has no wall-clock semantics".

critique_rows.Section / page: Exercise key VI.C E4 -- Coverage-bound A5 (p.31-32)
critique_rows.Item: An attacker can underwrite several liabilities from one reused deposit if concurrent aggregate exposure is not reserved; full reimbursement of a single loss does not by itself prove attacker profitability without the premium/loss distribution.
critique_rows.Notes: ex:bonded-a5-coverage-bound solution (1217): reused-deposit/aggregate-exposure attack; premium/loss distribution needed for profitability.

critique_rows.Section / page: Exercise key VI.C E5 -- Cartel detection (p.31-32)
critique_rows.Item: Derives p_d* at the chapter's own parameters (~5.4% per round in the negligible-undercut limit) and notes the prompt's missing epsilon/x term leaves no unique decimal as literally posed; a reusable or under-sized bond merely prices re-entry, it may not deter it.
critique_rows.Notes: ex:bonded-cartel-detection solution (1230): p_d*=97/1797 approx 5.4%; "prices always, deters conditionally, prevents never".

critique_rows.Section / page: Exercise key VI.C E6 -- Capability attenuation (p.32)
critique_rows.Item: A 20-minute child TTL violates temporal attenuation against a shorter parent expiry; gives an acceptable narrower card example under a stated capability lattice.
critique_rows.Notes: No treatment of TTL/temporal attenuation across delegation hops or a capability-lattice example anywhere in the chapter; only capability-set subset attenuation (not TTL) is modeled and proved.; ch.2 states temporal attenuation: a child's expiry is the earlier of the parent's expiry and the requested lifetime; the twenty-minute child under a ten-minute parent is refused, the ten-minute card is the acceptable one

critique_rows.Section / page: Exercise key VI.C E7 -- Cuckoo-filter pollution (p.32)
critique_rows.Item: Many authenticated-looking random revocation IDs can push a cuckoo filter outside its bound-holding load regime, creating a denial-of-revocation-service; the 0.95 load ceiling does not defeat a pollution DoS and needs quotas, exact overflow logging, and fail-closed handling.
critique_rows.Notes: Revocation section (L279) only says a loaded filter "rejects or rebuilds"; no quotas, no overflow logging, no fail-closed language for an adversarial-flooding pollution DoS as the item describes.; sec:revocation names pollution as denial of revocation and the three design requirements: per-issuer insertion quota, overflow record, lookups against the event log while the filter rebuilds

critique_rows.Section / page: Exercise key VI.C E8 -- Alternative insurance pricing (p.32)

critique_rows.Notes: ex:bonded-insurance-alt-pricing solution (1239-1241): posted-price catalog vs idle-capital cost; CC/NC/RP/NS needed before a Pareto claim.

critique_rows.Section / page: Exercise key VI.C E9 -- Gossip proof (p.32)

critique_rows.Notes: ex:bonded-gossip-proof solution (1633-1636): no numbered Demers theorem yields Theta(log m); general graphs need conductance/mixing time.

critique_rows.Section / page: Exercise key VII.4 -- Cross-harbor attenuation correction (p.32-33)
critique_rows.Item: att_B(att_A(C_A)) is a subset only when both harbors share one capability universe; translating test-database authority into staging authority is a new local authorization requiring B's own minted grant, not attenuation; a failed test does not itself establish A caused it.

critique_rows.Section / page: Exercise key VII.12.1 -- Multi-principal correlation (p.33)
critique_rows.Item: A witness log is a correlation device only with a modeled signal/incentive structure; during partitions there is no single public signal, so the clean model is a stochastic/Bayesian game with local correlation devices plus a delayed public signal and a separate degraded-safe policy.
critique_rows.Notes: ex:fh-correlated-equilibrium (line 1144-1148) models a Bayesian game with a common-view/freshness event as the correlation trigger and a degraded local-plus-Nash fallback policy.

critique_rows.Section / page: Exercise key VII.12.2 -- Non-fungible trustless settlement (p.33)
critique_rows.Item: HTLCs settle conditional asset exchange, not a subjective off-chain delivery predicate; two identical-on-ledger worlds with different true quality force a deterministic trustless contract into one wrong answer, so progress requires an oracle/TEE/dispute game -- each is a trust assumption.
critique_rows.Notes: ex:fh-trustless-settlement (line 1151-1156): HTLC's objective bit vs. the subjective causation predicate; sketches the impossibility shape; names oracle/TEE/dispute-window/arbiter as the needed trust addition.

critique_rows.Section / page: Exercise key VII.12.3 -- Cross-federation cartels (p.33)
critique_rows.Item: A witness log cannot distinguish unanimous honesty from unanimous collusion; deterrence needs p*d*L > G for one-shot collusive gain G; no structural mechanism eliminates a cartel controlling every oracle and witness in scope.
critique_rows.Notes: ex:fh-cartel-formation (line 1158-1165) states p*d*L>G needs an outside witness/audit source and that no structural mechanism closes the all-witnesses-controlled case.

critique_rows.Section / page: Exercise key VII.12.4 -- Cold-start admission (p.33-34)
critique_rows.Item: Proposes multiple independent sponsors, small auto-expanding probation scopes, sponsorship auctions, and concentration caps; notes these reduce but do not prove openness -- an incumbent-sponsorship monopoly can still form an invitation cartel.
critique_rows.Notes: ex:fh-cold-start-admission (line 1167-1172) proposes acceptance-rate/sponsor-concentration/time-to-entry/false-rejection metrics and states none proves openness against an invitation cartel.

critique_rows.Section / page: Exercise key VII.12.5 -- Equivocation propagation (p.34)
critique_rows.Item: Separates constant local verification from network dissemination time; a general graph needs a conductance/mixing-based bound, and any unbounded partition makes worst-case detection time and stale-authority window infinite, requiring TTL and fail-closed freshness.

critique_rows.Section / page: Sec.2 Tier A -- A1 Split-Digest Theorem (p.1)
critique_rows.Item: A single scoring head serves two readers iff their induced preference orders are comonotone; the successor and operator readers are provably non-comonotone, and a joint zero-miss digest pays the sum of the two floors when the two critical sets are disjoint. Converts the SLM-sidecar architecture from opinion to necessity.

critique_rows.Section / page: Sec.2.1 Solution 1 (6.1) -- why read-poverty binds (p.4)
critique_rows.Item: The write side already has mature primitives (claims, uniqueness, locks, merge queues); the read side (find the right agent/work/collaborator) has no primitive, so legible state accumulates faster than it can be consulted.

critique_rows.Section / page: Sec.2.1 Solution 2 (6.2) -- write-time cost vs. read-time speed (p.4)
critique_rows.Item: Every registration/claim/note/episode update must also maintain the directory index (write-time O(log n) or O(1) cost); queries then answer 'who/what matches q' in O(query) instead of scanning O(n) participants.
critique_rows.Notes: ex:ls-directory-database-analogy (l.1834-1835): write-time O(log n)/O(1) index maintenance buys O(log n+k) selective reads instead of O(n) scanning.

critique_rows.Section / page: Sec.2.1 Solution 3 (6.3) -- discovery is vacuous at n=1 (p.4)
critique_rows.Item: At n=1 the session briefing, honest-attestation/completion gate, and footgun guard already reduce uncertainty; none is discovery-ranking because with a single agent there is no candidate set to rank.
critique_rows.Notes: ex:ls-value-curve-n1 (l.1841-1842): at n=1 briefing/attestation/footgun-gating/completion/resurrection already pay off and none of them is discovery ranking.

critique_rows.Section / page: Sec.2.1 Solution 4 (6.4) -- the digest floor at the extremes (p.4)
critique_rows.Item: As k->0 the floor vanishes (a mostly-safe swarm is cheap to digest); as k->N/2 the floor grows to Theta(N) bits for any fixed review budget m<<N, so past a critical density 'summarize' degenerates to 'list' -- the formal justification for keeping the dangerous set small by construction.
critique_rows.Notes: ex:ls-floor-limits (l.1849-1850) gives both endpoints: floor to 0 as k to 0, floor to ~N bits at k=N/2 for fixed m<<N -- the formal case for keeping the dangerous set small.

critique_rows.Section / page: Sec.2.1 Solution 5 (6.5, starred) -- adversarial critical-set estimation (p.4)
critique_rows.Item: Against an adaptive adversary the bound becomes log2 C(N,k') with k' the indistinguishability-class size; the adversary attacks by inflation (drive the floor toward Theta(N), a legibility denial-of-service) or mimicry (make critical artifacts appear inert); the defense is building the digest only from signals the agent cannot forge, with the residue an inspection game sharing Conjecture III.11.1's Becker condition.
critique_rows.Notes: ex:ls-adversarial-critical-set (l.1858-1859) covers the general adversarial argument but omits the log2 C(N,k') refinement, the named inflation/mimicry attacks, and the Becker-condition link.; ex:ls-adversarial-critical-set gives the log2 C(N,k') refinement, names inflation and mimicry, and links to the Becker condition

critique_rows.Section / page: Sec.2.2 Solution 6 (7.1) -- no monotone transform unifies discovery and attention (p.4-5)
critique_rows.Item: Discovery maximizes capability fit (Eq I.2); the attention queue maximizes regret-if-ignored=stakes*irreversibility*anomaly (Eq I.3); high-fit/low-risk and low-fit/high-risk items order oppositely under the two, so no strictly monotone scalar transform can identify them.

critique_rows.Section / page: Sec.2.4 Solution 16 (III.6 ex.1) -- one cause, two attacks, one cure (p.6)
critique_rows.Item: Whitewashing mints a fresh identity at zero cost to route around a sanction; Sybil mints n identities to outweigh honest signal and forge a quorum; both share one cure -- strictly positive abandonment cost.
