critique_rows.Section / page: Sec.2.4 Solution 17 (III.6 ex.2) -- reduced ceiling taxes fraud, reduced work ability taxes honesty (p.6)
critique_rows.Item: Full work ability with a reduced economic ceiling charges the whitewasher the cumulative surplus gap every reset while the honest newcomer pays only one maturation; 'distrust newcomers' (reduced work ability) instead imposes deadweight loss on the honest party while barely touching the fraudster.
critique_rows.Notes: ex:stp-newcomer-shape solution (L1648-1655): reduced ceiling taxes the whitewasher's reset while "reduced work" taxes all honest entrants for no targeted gain -- matches closely.

critique_rows.Section / page: Sec.2.4 Solution 18 (III.6 ex.3, starred) -- bond-farming and counterparty-diversity weighting (p.6-7)
critique_rows.Item: Principal binding is necessary but not sufficient against a principal inflating its own record; the sufficient defense is counterparty-diversity weighting (discount reputation earned against a same-principal or high-correlation counterparty) plus sampled adversarial re-audit of high-velocity, low-diversity pairs at the Becker rate.
critique_rows.Notes: ex:stp-bond-farming (L1664-1673) has diminishing per-principal-pair credit plus adversarial re-audit, but never names "counterparty-diversity weighting" or ties its rate to sec:oracle's rho*=G/(dB).; ex:stp-bond-farming names counterparty-diversity weighting and ties the re-audit rate to rho* = G/(dB) of sec:oracle

critique_rows.Section / page: Sec.2.4 Solution 19 (III.11 ex.1) -- 'the daemon derives the grade' relocates trust without discharging it (p.7)
critique_rows.Item: The grade's producer must itself be incentive-compatible; if a judge gains from a dishonest input, mechanical daemon derivation faithfully launders the dishonesty into an authoritative-looking grade.
critique_rows.Notes: ex:stp-grading-oracle-hole solution (L2478-2483): "the daemon derives the grade" only identifies the messenger; a strategic judge's chosen input still launders dishonesty into the grade.

critique_rows.Section / page: Sec.2.4 Solution 20 (III.11 ex.2) -- the overturn/slash/tombstone trace (p.7)
critique_rows.Item: Traces a dishonest judge grade through re-audit detection, tombstone retraction, bond slashing to the harmed party or commons, judge-reputation debit, and downstream reputation recomputation net of the tombstoned entry.
critique_rows.Notes: ex:stp-bond-flow-reaudit (L2488-2494) + S4 (L2612-2629) walk detection, tombstone append, bond slash to harmed/commons, judge-reputation debit, and recomputation net of the tombstone.

critique_rows.Item: The five assurance modes (Observed/Coordinated/Brokered/Confined/Attested) are the Book's one taxonomy of its own and had never been placed against Sheridan's levels of automation, Parasuraman-Sheridan-Wickens, or the Common Criteria's EALs. critique_rows.Notes: Not a restatement; the three axes are independent and the placement now says why. Sheridan & Verplank (1978) grade the allocation of the decide-and-act loop (who does it) and Parasuraman-Sheridan-Wickens split that across four processing stages; Common Criteria EAL1-EAL7 grade how much independent evaluation effort a claim received before deployment, once, for a whole product; the ladder grades what an adversary would have to defeat for one runtime claim about one mechanism to be false. Stated at the kernel chapter's 'What it buys', with the independence written as a pdclaim{Design invariant} exhibiting the corners (a Sheridan-level-10 component whose actions are merely logged is Observed; a level-3 component routing its one effect through an attested broker is Attested; EAL7 products can contain Observed mechanisms), and the boundary in the same breath (a design vocabulary, not a measured scale; the rungs are not evenly spaced or totally ordered). sheridanverplank1978 added as a bibitem to the kernel chapter and the sealed room -- it was uncited, only parasuraman2000 was present; cciso15408 sharpened from 'current edition' to ISO/IEC 15408-1:2022. critique_rows.Section / page: README.md 'Contested or open' -- the deontic frontier against the compliance-checking dichotomy
critique_rows.Item: The tractable-then-NP-complete frontier of ch.6 stands against Colombo Tosatto, Governatori and van Beest's compliance-checking dichotomy. Determine whether L_c is inside their tractable side, outside it, or orthogonal, and make the chapter say so.
critique_rows.Prior adjudication: Supersedes LR-408 (0ac32d8b2), which added the citations and a hedge ('one does not subsume the other') but did not answer inside/outside/orthogonal.
critique_rows.Notes: ORTHOGONAL, and now demonstrated rather than asserted. Both papers read in full (arXiv:2001.10148, arXiv:2105.05431). Their axis across all eight variants is literals vs formulae in the obligation's elements: for full compliance, literals give P in all four variants and formulae coNP-complete in all four; the 1/n and G/L coordinates do not move the class. L_c fires on Horn bodies -- conjunctions, derived through a program that may chain -- so it is on the HARD side of their only decisive coordinate and is polynomial anyway, which is the tell that the problems differ. Their hardness comes from the process model, not the obligations: the coNP-completeness reduction builds an interpretation WF-net with one XOR bond per propositional variable so the 2^n executions enumerate every interpretation, and quantifies over them universally. L_c has no process model to branch and conflict-freedom is existential over schedules, which is exactly why one step out is NP rather than coNP. Honest residue recorded in the chapter: the nearest variant in their lattice is PARTIAL compliance (NP-complete in six of eight, P in one, and still open for 1L-, a single conditional obligation over literals); our theorems neither close that hole nor can, and a reduction in either direction between L_c-conflict-freedom and 1L- partial compliance would settle the relation. Nobody has written one. Also fixed: both ctgvb bibitems gave van Beest the initial P; he is Nick.

critique_rows.Section / page: Rigorous mathematical and formal analysis -- Thm 4.4.1
critique_rows.Item: Theorem 4.4.1's Erlang-C specialization boundary assumes stationary Poisson arrivals and strictly exponential service; agent execution durations are heavy-tailed and submissions arrive in correlated bursts, so the specialist queue is exposed to Kingman-type delay explosions. critique_rows.Prior adjudication: ADJUDICATION-2026-09-08.md CA-004 ACCEPT-IN-PART: a boundary paragraph, not a change of statement, plus an Allen-Cunneen heuristic and a Pareto/lognormal sweep of `skills/harbor-results/scripts/b8_specialization.py`.
critique_rows.Notes: New $\S4.4.3.1$ *What heavy tails do to the boundary*: Kingman for the general cost, Allen--Cunneen and Pollaczek--Khinchine worked through both sides, and the un-obvious conclusion the adjudication predicted -- variance scales both waiting terms by about the same $\kappa=(1+c_s^2)/2$, so the boundary barely moves and accountability enters as $A/\kappa$, weighing *less* against queueing rather than more. Stated as an Empirical hypothesis with its falsifier and the `b8_specialization.py` sweep that would settle it; no number is quoted because no sweep has run, and infinite-variance Pareto is named as where the heuristic stops rather than degrades. Boundary, not statement -- the theorem is exact inside its named model.

critique_rows.Prior adjudication: ADJUDICATION-2026-09-08.md CA-035 ACCEPT and called apt: `slash(id,p)` routes p to the commons pool and never back to the counterparty, which is exactly the budget breaker.
critique_rows.Notes: The adjudication called this the most valuable of the literature set and it reads that way. Holmström (1982) now explains a design decision the conservation worked example walked past: the slashed bond routes to the commons pool and never back to the counterparty, which is a budget breaker, and budget balance has to break for his reason -- a penalty that is another participant's windfall costs the pair nothing. Scoped: the mechanism is not claiming first-best effort, only borrowing the structural reason, which is why Conservation holds over $W+E+C$ and not over wallets alone.

Beta mixture with intra-panel correlation $\theta$ telescopes into a product of $k$ fractions. Worked example uses only numbers the chapter had already fixed ($d=0.8$, $k=3$) and lands on the pitfall's own sentence as arithmetic: at $\theta\to1$ three reviewers deliver the assurance of one, 25x worse than the line item. Checked against a Monte Carlo run and the Gamma-function form before printing. $\theta$ is unmeasured and the text says what would measure it.

critique_rows.Section / page: Chapter-by-chapter -- ch. 5 Sybil resistance
critique_rows.Item: Theorem 5.6.1 proves non-forgeable identity is necessary for any sanction-respecting reputation; explicitly contrast the centralized daemon-attested identity chosen for Port Daddy with alternative Sybil-resistance mechanisms from permissionless systems such as proof-of-stake or deposit bonding, to justify the architectural trade-off.
critique_rows.Prior adjudication: ADJUDICATION-2026-09-08.md CA-055 ACCEPT-IN-PART: one paragraph in §5.7 -- stake binds capital, not a principal; the Book's answer is the no-mint result plus per-principal exposure pooling, and ch. 7's bonds are where capital enters.
critique_rows.Notes: $\S$*Why not stake?* after the no-mint result. The contrast is made on the axis that matters: stake bounds how many identities an adversary mints and says nothing about whose they are, which is the wrong axis when the conduct being sanctioned is a party's; the no-mint result conserves creditable reputation across a derivation graph whether identities are cheap or dear, and per-principal exposure pooling does the rest. The trade is named rather than won by definition -- daemon attestation costs a trusted local authority, which is what a permissionless system refuses to assume -- and capital is placed where it does enter, as ch. 7's bonds priced against a breach rather than a toll at the door.

critique_rows.Prior adjudication: ADJUDICATION-2026-09-08.md CA-061 ACCEPT-IN-PART: the taxonomy yes (with CA-070); for the succession result, name the exercise by label, because the exercise number is edition-specific and the formula the review quotes does not occur in the source.
critique_rows.Notes: The accepted half (naming `ex:ls-succession-corner` by label rather than by edition-specific number) predates this pass. The remaining half turned out to be smaller than the row reads, and the reason is worth recording. The result was ALREADY in the Book's narrative -- ch. 6 carries it as `thm:succession-price` with the full closed form, the $\eta K<1$ proviso, the $\eta K\ge1$ case, a `pdboundary` that declares the death-at-all-times breakdown model as decisive, and verification against a matrix-geometric solution (1.95e-13), a truncated CTMC (1.38e-14) and a Gillespie DES [verified, `b8_specialization.py`]. It belongs there: it is a condition on what a succession plan costs, which is an economic statement. What ch. 4 needed was a pointer, not a second copy -- a copy would have been the CA-014 defect (one result defined twice in two chapters) in a new place. `sec:succession-corner` in $\S4.4$ is now that pointer plus the two consequences that change what a sole-responsibility role MEANS rather than what it costs: skill has a ceiling ($W_\infty$ is never attained, so past a point the fix is a better handoff and not a better owner), and the ceiling binds absolutely only while $\eta K<1$. Two LOCAL corrections land in the ch. 4 exercise solution, which is where the genuine defects were: it gave $D^\star$ unconditionally, dropping the $\eta K<1$ proviso (and $\eta K\ge1$ is the commoner case in a well-run fleet, so this was not a corner), and it called the breakdown-corrected wait 'exact' without naming the model that makes it exact. PROCESS NOTE, since the skill forbids silent rewrites: this pass first drafted a full duplicate theorem in ch. 4 together with a claim that ch. 6's closed form was not exact, on the strength of a 7-46% disagreement with a Pollaczek-Khinchine computation. Running `b8_specialization.py` refuted that: the disagreement was against a DIFFERENT model (active-only breakdowns), not a defect in the formula, and ch. 6's boundary already declares which model it means. The draft was retracted before commit. The surviving observation is the one the chapters now state: under active-only breakdowns the floor is 0 and $D^\star$ does not exist, so the model choice is the whole result.

critique_rows.Section / page: Chapter/module table -- ch. 5
critique_rows.Item: Unify Parfitian psychological continuity with cryptographic key-lineage transfer protocols.
critique_rows.Prior adjudication: New row: not separately adjudicated.
critique_rows.Notes: Done as $\S$`sec:parfit-lineage-map` in ch. 5, and done at the epistemic kind the claim actually earns -- `pdclaim{Design invariant}`, not Theorem, because it states what the system is built to do and takes no position on whether it tracks personal identity. The correspondence that holds is exact and narrow: both Relation R and credential lineage are the ANCESTRAL of a direct relation that is not itself transitive ($\mathsf{conn}^*$ and $\mathsf{succ}^*$), so the engineering is not Parfit-inspired but the same construction on a witnessed base. The previous pass was right that the honest version has to say where the analogy fails, and the `pdboundary` names three places. (i) Connectedness admits degree and signature verification does not, so the ledger criterion cannot express partial survival at all -- the case Parfit finds most interesting is the one it is structurally unable to represent. (ii) Fission gets a determinate answer from the no-mint rule (debit the source, discount each child) that Parfit deliberately refuses to give; that is a decision imposed because an economy needs conservation, not a discovery about identity. (iii) Lineage is constitutively third-personal, which immunises it against the Williams framing warning the chapter already cites -- its one clear advantage over its source -- but means possession of a predecessor's key proves CUSTODY TRANSFER, not continuity of anything psychological. (iii) carries a stated obligation rather than an answer, per the skill's open-problem rule: a continuity witness attesting WHAT THE SUCCESSOR ACTUALLY LOADED (which notes, which checkpoint, which ledger positions), which is a schema and attestation-coverage question and which no design in the chapter specifies.

critique_rows.Section / page: Literature grounding -- Hodge decomposition
critique_rows.Item: Cite Jiang et al. (Statistical Ranking on Graphs via Hodge Decomposition, 2011), who resolved inconsistent pairwise comparisons into gradient and curl components; the equivocator's split-view lie is the curl component over the visible witness graph, and connecting the detection residual to it gives students visual and algebraic intuition.
critique_rows.Prior adjudication: ADJUDICATION-2026-09-08.md CA-039 ACCEPT (Jiang), split from the Hansen-Ghrist half here because the review makes two distinct asks in the same paragraph and the verdicts differ.
critique_rows.Notes: Jiang, Lim, Yao and Ye cited and, more to the point, *used*: their gradient/curl decomposition of inconsistent pairwise comparisons is the same object as the completion residual, the gradient part being the history one global score explains and the curl what refuses to have one, so the equivocator's split-view lie is curl over the visible witness graph. Two of the chapter's own results fall out of the analogy and are flagged as separately proved: no cycles means no curl to measure (severed edges, trees), and a global clock relabelling is pure gradient, so the detector is blind to it and should be.

Worth recording from this pass: the floor checks only that a kind TAG EXISTS, never that the chosen kind is CORRECT, and the one claim added on this branch (`inv:parfit-lineage`, tagged Design invariant rather than Theorem because it states what the system is built to do) was kind-checked by hand, not by the linter.
